# Cheatsheet - Kafka Security & Governance dalam Java/Jersey Microservice

## 1. Core Mental Model

Kafka security di aplikasi Java/Jersey bukan hanya menambahkan `security.protocol=SASL_SSL`. Security harus dilihat sebagai kombinasi beberapa layer:

```text id="0lemg2"
Kafka Security & Governance
│
├── Transport security
│   ├── TLS encryption
│   ├── hostname verification
│   └── truststore / keystore
│
├── Authentication
│   ├── mTLS certificate identity
│   ├── SASL/SCRAM
│   ├── SASL/PLAIN over TLS
│   ├── SASL/OAUTHBEARER
│   └── Kerberos/GSSAPI
│
├── Authorization
│   ├── ACL
│   ├── topic permissions
│   ├── consumer group permissions
│   ├── transactional id permissions
│   └── admin operation permissions
│
├── Data governance
│   ├── topic ownership
│   ├── event contract
│   ├── schema compatibility
│   ├── data classification
│   ├── retention
│   └── auditability
│
├── Runtime hardening
│   ├── secret management
│   ├── least privilege
│   ├── environment isolation
│   ├── network policy
│   └── config validation
│
└── Operational governance
    ├── onboarding/offboarding service identity
    ├── ACL review
    ├── certificate/secret rotation
    ├── schema review
    ├── DLQ review
    └── incident/runbook
```

Kafka menyediakan authorization framework yang pluggable; pada Kafka KRaft modern, default ACL implementation menyimpan ACL di cluster metadata / KRaft metadata log. Ini penting karena ACL bukan sekadar file lokal broker, melainkan bagian dari metadata cluster yang perlu dikelola secara konsisten. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/security/authorization-and-acls/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 2. Security Layer Table

| Layer | Pertanyaan utama | Contoh kontrol |
|---|---|---|
| Network | Siapa boleh reach broker? | VPC/VNet, firewall, Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, private endpoint |
| Transport | Apakah traffic terenkripsi? | TLS / `SSL` / `SASL_SSL` |
| Authentication | Client ini siapa? | mTLS cert, SCRAM user, OAuth client/principal |
| Authorization | Principal boleh melakukan apa? | ACL topic/group/cluster/transactional ID |
| Data contract | Data apa yang boleh dipublish? | Schema Registry, event review |
| Data classification | Apakah ada PII/secret/restricted data? | Topic classification, redaction, ACL |
| Runtime config | Secret disimpan di mana? | Kubernetes Secret, Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault |
| Observability | Bisa diaudit? | Structured log, audit event, ACL change log |
| Operations | Bagaimana rotasi/revokasi? | Credential rotation, cert expiry alerts, offboarding |

---

## 3. `security.protocol`

Kafka client menggunakan `security.protocol` untuk menentukan protokol koneksi ke broker. Nilai umum yang didukung adalah `PLAINTEXT`, `SSL`, `SASL_PLAINTEXT`, dan `SASL_SSL`; untuk production, kombinasi tanpa enkripsi seperti `PLAINTEXT` dan `SASL_PLAINTEXT` biasanya tidak layak kecuali benar-benar dibatasi di network yang aman dan disetujui security. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/configuration/producer-configs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

| Protocol | Authentication | Encryption | Production stance |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `PLAINTEXT` | Tidak | Tidak | Hindari |
| `SSL` | Bisa mTLS certificate | Ya | Cocok jika cert-based auth |
| `SASL_PLAINTEXT` | SASL | Tidak | Hindari untuk production |
| `SASL_SSL` | SASL | Ya | Umum untuk production |

Baseline untuk service Java:

```properties id="17yry3"
security.protocol=SASL_SSL
sasl.mechanism=SCRAM-SHA-512
sasl.jaas.config=org.apache.kafka.common.security.scram.ScramLoginModule required \
  username="${KAFKA_USERNAME}" \
  password="${KAFKA_PASSWORD}";
ssl.endpoint.identification.algorithm=https
```

---

## 4. TLS / SSL

TLS memberi encryption in transit dan, jika menggunakan client certificate, bisa juga menjadi mekanisme authentication melalui mTLS. Kafka producer config mendokumentasikan setting SSL seperti cipher suite dan `ssl.endpoint.identification.algorithm`, yang dipakai untuk validasi hostname server berdasarkan certificate broker. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/42/configuration/producer-configs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```text id="w0zsv8"
Client
  ↓ TLS handshake
Broker certificate validation
  ↓
Optional client certificate validation
  ↓
Encrypted Kafka protocol traffic
```

### Client config example - TLS truststore

```properties id="w72bcx"
security.protocol=SSL

ssl.truststore.location=/etc/kafka/secrets/client.truststore.jks
ssl.truststore.password=${KAFKA_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD}

ssl.endpoint.identification.algorithm=https
```

### Client config example - mTLS

```properties id="2pxq0t"
security.protocol=SSL

ssl.truststore.location=/etc/kafka/secrets/client.truststore.jks
ssl.truststore.password=${KAFKA_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD}

ssl.keystore.location=/etc/kafka/secrets/client.keystore.jks
ssl.keystore.password=${KAFKA_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD}
ssl.key.password=${KAFKA_KEY_PASSWORD}

ssl.endpoint.identification.algorithm=https
```

| TLS item | Praktik |
|---|---|
| Truststore | Berisi CA yang dipercaya untuk broker certificate |
| Keystore | Berisi client certificate/private key jika mTLS |
| Hostname verification | Jangan disable di production |
| Cert rotation | Harus ada alert sebelum expiry |
| Private key | Jangan masuk image/container layer |
| Password | Ambil dari secret manager |
| Protocol/cipher | Ikuti platform security baseline |

---

## 5. SASL Mechanisms

Kafka mendukung beberapa SASL mechanism. Dokumentasi Kafka 4.3 menjelaskan konfigurasi SASL client, termasuk JAAS configuration, dan menyebut bahwa untuk beberapa listener SASL, section JAAS dapat diprefix dengan listener name. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/security/authentication-using-sasl/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

| Mechanism | Kapan dipakai | Catatan |
|---|---|---|
| `SCRAM-SHA-256` / `SCRAM-SHA-512` | Username/password dengan challenge-response | Umum untuk self-managed / managed Kafka |
| `PLAIN` | Username/password sederhana | Harus over TLS; jangan plain network |
| `OAUTHBEARER` | Integrasi OAuth2/OIDC identity provider | Cocok untuk enterprise identity |
| `GSSAPI` | Kerberos | Banyak di enterprise legacy/Hadoop |
| mTLS via `SSL` | Certificate identity | Bagus jika PKI matang |

Kafka mendukung SCRAM-SHA-256 dan SCRAM-SHA-512, dan Confluent juga mendokumentasikan keduanya sebagai mekanisme yang dapat digunakan dengan TLS untuk authentication. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/40/security/authentication-using-sasl/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 6. SASL/SCRAM Java Client Config

```properties id="gz6p94"
bootstrap.servers=kafka-1:9093,kafka-2:9093,kafka-3:9093

security.protocol=SASL_SSL
sasl.mechanism=SCRAM-SHA-512
sasl.jaas.config=org.apache.kafka.common.security.scram.ScramLoginModule required \
  username="${KAFKA_USERNAME}" \
  password="${KAFKA_PASSWORD}";

ssl.truststore.location=/etc/kafka/secrets/truststore.jks
ssl.truststore.password=${KAFKA_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD}
ssl.endpoint.identification.algorithm=https
```

### Java `Properties`

```java id="b6zm7q"
Properties props = new Properties();

props.put(CommonClientConfigs.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG,
        System.getenv("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS"));

props.put(CommonClientConfigs.SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG, "SASL_SSL");
props.put(SaslConfigs.SASL_MECHANISM, "SCRAM-SHA-512");

props.put(SaslConfigs.SASL_JAAS_CONFIG,
        "org.apache.kafka.common.security.scram.ScramLoginModule required "
                + "username=\"" + System.getenv("KAFKA_USERNAME") + "\" "
                + "password=\"" + System.getenv("KAFKA_PASSWORD") + "\";");

props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_TRUSTSTORE_LOCATION_CONFIG,
        "/etc/kafka/secrets/truststore.jks");

props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD_CONFIG,
        System.getenv("KAFKA_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD"));

props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_ENDPOINT_IDENTIFICATION_ALGORITHM_CONFIG, "https");
```

### Pitfall

| Pitfall | Dampak |
|---|---|
| Password ditulis di repo | Credential leak |
| `SASL_PLAINTEXT` di production | Credential bisa disadap |
| Hostname verification disabled | Rentan MITM |
| Satu SCRAM user untuk semua service | Audit dan revocation buruk |
| Tidak ada rotation plan | Secret menjadi long-lived risk |
| Log full JAAS config | Password masuk log |

---

## 7. SASL/OAUTHBEARER

OAuth/OIDC cocok jika perusahaan ingin Kafka client identity mengikuti identity provider enterprise. Kafka memiliki implementasi OAUTHBEARER; dokumentasi Kafka mencatat bahwa default OAUTHBEARER lama yang membuat/validasi unsecured JWT hanya cocok untuk non-production, sementara versi baru mendukung integrasi dengan identity provider OAuth2-compliant untuk production. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/41/security/authentication-using-sasl/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```properties id="jwt4om"
security.protocol=SASL_SSL
sasl.mechanism=OAUTHBEARER
sasl.jaas.config=org.apache.kafka.common.security.oauthbearer.OAuthBearerLoginModule required;
```

Kafka producer configs juga mencantumkan berbagai config terkait OAuth bearer assertion, termasuk algoritma JWT assertion yang dipakai client saat berinteraksi dengan identity provider. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/configuration/producer-configs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

| OAuth concern | Praktik |
|---|---|
| Token source | Gunakan approved identity provider |
| Token lifetime | Pendek, refresh otomatis |
| Client credential | Secret manager |
| Audience/scope | Batasi untuk Kafka |
| Principal mapping | Jelas: service identity → Kafka principal |
| Rotation | Client secret/cert rotation |
| Non-prod unsecured token | Jangan dibawa ke production |

---

## 8. ACL / Authorization

ACL menjawab: **principal ini boleh melakukan operasi apa pada resource apa?** Kafka memiliki pluggable authorizer; default implementation pada Kafka KRaft menyimpan ACL di metadata cluster. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/security/authorization-and-acls/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) Confluent juga menekankan ACL sebagai kontrol authorization penting untuk data Kafka cluster. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/security/authorization/acls/overview.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```text id="o2ulfd"
Principal:
  User:order-service

Resources:
  Topic: order.order.events.v1
  Group: order-projection-service
  TransactionalId: order-service-tx-*
  Cluster: kafka-cluster

Operations:
  READ
  WRITE
  CREATE
  DELETE
  ALTER
  DESCRIBE
  DESCRIBE_CONFIGS
  ALTER_CONFIGS
  IDEMPOTENT_WRITE
```

### Common ACL model

| Service role | Needed ACL |
|---|---|
| Producer | `WRITE` + `DESCRIBE` on output topic |
| Consumer | `READ` + `DESCRIBE` on input topic, `READ` on group |
| Retry/DLQ publisher | `WRITE` + `DESCRIBE` on retry/DLQ topic |
| Admin diagnostics | `DESCRIBE` topic/group/cluster as needed |
| Transactional producer | Transactional ID ACL as platform requires |
| Topic bootstrapper | `CREATE`/`ALTER_CONFIGS`, usually not in app service |

---

## 9. Least Privilege Examples

### Producer-only service

```text id="l06unj"
Principal: User:order-service

Allow:
  WRITE on Topic:order.order.events.v1
  DESCRIBE on Topic:order.order.events.v1

Deny/avoid:
  READ on unrelated topics
  WRITE on billing/payment topics
  DELETE topic
  ALTER configs
```

### Consumer-only projection service

```text id="ssnrr8"
Principal: User:order-projection-service

Allow:
  READ on Topic:order.order.events.v1
  DESCRIBE on Topic:order.order.events.v1
  READ on Group:order-projection-service
  WRITE on Topic:order.projection.dlq.v1
  DESCRIBE on Topic:order.projection.dlq.v1
```

### Outbox relay

```text id="5rgppg"
Principal: User:order-outbox-relay

Allow:
  WRITE on Topic:order.order.events.v1
  DESCRIBE on Topic:order.order.events.v1

If producer idempotence/transactions require:
  IDEMPOTENT_WRITE / TransactionalId permissions according to platform policy
```

### Admin diagnostics service

```text id="i84cd4"
Principal: User:order-admin-diagnostics

Allow:
  DESCRIBE on selected topics
  DESCRIBE on selected groups
  DESCRIBE_CONFIGS on selected topics if needed

Avoid:
  CREATE
  DELETE
  ALTER
  ALTER_CONFIGS
```

---

## 10. ACL Design by Resource

| Resource | Governance question | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Topic | Who can read/write? | Only producer writes; approved consumers read |
| Group | Who can commit/read as this consumer group? | Projection service owns its group |
| Transactional ID | Who can use transactional producer identity? | Only specific service instance pattern |
| Cluster | Who can describe/create/admin? | Platform/admin only |
| Delegation token | Who can create/use tokens? | Platform/security only |
| Schema subject | Who can register/update schema? | Producer owner via CI/CD |
| Connect connector | Who can deploy connector? | Platform/data infra team |

## 12. Secret Management

Kafka credential tidak boleh masuk:

```text id="34qv1v"
Do not put secrets in:
  - Git repository
  - Docker image layer
  - Maven resources committed to repo
  - application logs
  - exception message
  - actuator/config endpoint
  - command-line args visible through ps
```

### Kubernetes pattern

```text id="5adgxq"
Kubernetes Secret / External Secret
  ↓
Mounted file or env var
  ↓
Application config loader
  ↓
Kafka client Properties
```

| Secret type | Better storage |
|---|---|
| SCRAM username/password | Secret manager / Kubernetes Secret |
| JAAS config | Generated at runtime from secret values |
| Truststore | Mounted secret volume |
| Keystore/private key | Mounted secret volume with restricted permissions |
| OAuth client secret | Secret manager |
| Schema Registry credential | Secret manager |
| Connect/Debezium DB password | Secret manager |

### Avoid logging config

```java id="4xnibt"
private static Map<String, Object> sanitizeKafkaConfig(Map<String, Object> config) {
    Set<String> sensitiveKeys = Set.of(
            "sasl.jaas.config",
            "ssl.truststore.password",
            "ssl.keystore.password",
            "ssl.key.password",
            "schema.registry.basic.auth.user.info"
    );

    return config.entrySet().stream()
            .collect(Collectors.toMap(
                    Map.Entry::getKey,
                    e -> sensitiveKeys.contains(e.getKey()) ? "***" : e.getValue()
            ));
}
```

## 13. Topic Governance

Topic adalah public contract surface. Jangan anggap topic hanya “queue teknis”.

```text id="bz2b1j"
Topic governance record:
  name
  owner
  purpose
  data classification
  producer service
  allowed consumers
  key semantics
  schema subject
  retention
  cleanup policy
  partition count
  replication/min ISR
  SLA/SLO
  deprecation policy
```

### Topic naming

```text id="38zk3s"
<domain>.<entity-or-capability>.<stream-type>.v<major>
```

Contoh:

```text id="vylahp"
order.order.events.v1
billing.payment.events.v1
case.enforcement.events.v1
customer.profile.changelog.v1
risk.payment-alerts.v1
```

| Naming smell | Problem |
|---|---|
| `events` | Tidak ada ownership |
| `test-topic` | Tidak production-safe |
| `service-a-output` | Terlalu teknis |
| `new-topic-final-v2` | Tidak governance-driven |
| `orders2` | Tidak jelas semantic versioning |

---

## 14. Data Classification

Kafka topic bisa menyimpan data lama sesuai retention, bisa direplay, dan bisa dikonsumsi banyak service. Jadi classification wajib.

| Classification | Contoh data | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Public/internal-low | Non-sensitive system signal | Basic ACL |
| Internal | Business event non-PII | Topic ACL + retention |
| Confidential | Customer/account/business-sensitive | Strict ACL, audit, encryption |
| Restricted/PII | Personal identifier, address, identity data | Minimization, masking, retention review |
| Secret | Password/token/API key/private key | Jangan publish ke Kafka |

Rule:

```text id="k5t1dy"
Never publish:
  password
  access token
  refresh token
  private key
  full credential
  unnecessary PII
```

---

## 15. Event Contract Governance

Schema Registry membantu menjaga schema evolution. Confluent Schema Registry default compatibility mode adalah `BACKWARD`; compatibility types menentukan perubahan schema yang diizinkan, dan transitive mode mengecek terhadap semua versi sebelumnya, bukan hanya versi terakhir. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/schema-registry/fundamentals/schema-evolution.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

| Contract item | Governance |
|---|---|
| Event envelope | `eventId`, `eventType`, `eventVersion`, `occurredAt`, `producer`, `correlationId` |
| Schema format | JSON Schema / Avro / Protobuf / JSON |
| Subject strategy | TopicName / RecordName / TopicRecordName |
| Compatibility | BACKWARD, FULL, TRANSITIVE sesuai kebutuhan |
| Versioning | Minor schema evolution vs major topic/event v2 |
| Golden event | Sample event valid untuk test |
| Consumer tolerance | Unknown fields, optional fields, enum fallback |
| Semantic review | Field meaning tidak berubah diam-diam |

### Compatibility policy guide

| Topic type | Compatibility recommendation |
|---|---|
| Internal low-risk | `BACKWARD` |
| Public integration event | `BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE` atau `FULL_TRANSITIVE` |
| Long-retention/replay-heavy | Transitive compatibility |
| Disposable dev/test | Bisa longgar, tapi jangan tiru di prod |
| Kafka Streams state/input | Hati-hati; Kafka Streams memiliki constraint tersendiri pada compatibility/order upgrade menurut Confluent docs. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/schema-registry/fundamentals/schema-evolution.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)) |

---

## 16. Producer Governance

Producer adalah owner event. Producer wajib menjamin:

```text id="hldbug"
Producer responsibilities:
  - publish only valid contract
  - choose correct key
  - set headers/tracing
  - avoid sensitive fields
  - obey schema compatibility
  - use outbox for business-critical events
  - emit metrics for publish success/failure
```

### Producer checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| ACL | Hanya `WRITE` ke topic yang dimiliki |
| Key | Stable aggregate/business key |
| Contract | Schema valid sebelum publish |
| Privacy | Payload reviewed |
| Headers | correlation/causation/trace |
| Reliability | `acks=all`, idempotence, outbox if needed |
| Error handling | Callback/relay failure monitored |
| Audit | eventId and producer version logged |

---

## 17. Consumer Governance

Consumer bertanggung jawab atas side effect-nya sendiri.

```text id="wse45q"
Consumer responsibilities:
  - validate contract
  - handle unknown version/type
  - deduplicate eventId
  - commit offset only after safe processing
  - use retry/DLQ
  - protect downstream resources
  - monitor lag/failure
```

### Consumer checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| ACL | `READ` only on needed topics |
| Group | Own group id; no accidental sharing |
| Idempotency | `processed_event` or business key |
| Offset | Manual commit for business processing |
| Error | Retry/DLQ classification |
| Privacy | Do not log full sensitive payload |
| Replay | Handler replay-safe |
| Observability | Lag, failure, DLQ, duplicate metrics |

---

## 18. Multi-Tenant Isolation

Untuk multi-tenant system, Kafka governance harus menjawab apakah isolation dilakukan di topic, key, payload, ACL, atau cluster.

| Isolation model | Bentuk | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|---|
| Topic per tenant | `tenant-a.order.events.v1` | ACL kuat per tenant | Banyak topic |
| Shared topic + tenant key | `tenantId` in key/header/payload | Efisien | ACL tidak granular per tenant |
| Shared topic + tenant field | payload/header only | Simpler | Risiko consumer lupa filter |
| Cluster per tenant | Dedicated cluster | Isolasi kuat | Mahal/operasional berat |
| Namespace per environment/domain | Prefix/topic governance | Balance | Butuh convention kuat |

### Multi-tenant invariant

```text id="xvq79w"
Every event in multi-tenant Kafka must carry:
  - tenantId
  - producer identity
  - data classification
  - authorization context if needed
```

### Consumer guard

```java id="6yzoar"
public void handle(EventEnvelope event) {
    if (!tenantAccessPolicy.canProcess(event.tenantId(), serviceIdentity)) {
        throw new UnauthorizedTenantEventException(event.tenantId());
    }

    process(event);
}
```

---

## 19. Environment Isolation

Jangan campur dev/staging/prod di topic yang sama.

```text id="6478ku"
Bad:
  same topic name, same cluster, unclear env

Better:
  separate clusters per env
  or clear env namespace/prefix
  separate credentials
  separate ACLs
```

| Environment concern | Guardrail |
|---|---|
| Dev producer writes prod topic | Separate credentials and network |
| Staging reads prod PII | Separate ACL/data masking |
| CI creates topic in shared cluster | Prefix / ephemeral namespace |
| Prod config accidentally used local | Environment validation |
| Shared schema registry subject | Env-specific context/subject naming |

---

## 20. Network Hardening

Security tidak cukup di Kafka ACL saja.

```text id="c2kay7"
Application pod
  ↓
Kubernetes NetworkPolicy / VPC SG / firewall
  ↓
Private Kafka endpoint
  ↓
Broker listener
  ↓
TLS/SASL authentication
  ↓
ACL authorization
```

| Layer | Control |
|---|---|
| Kubernetes | NetworkPolicy egress to broker only |
| Cloud | Security Group / NSG / private endpoint |
| On-prem | Firewall, VLAN, broker listener separation |
| DNS | Internal broker DNS only |
| Broker listener | Internal/external listener separation |
| Client | TLS hostname verification |
| Observability | Connection/auth failure metrics |

---

## 21. Internal vs External Listener

Kafka broker sering punya multiple listener: internal, external, replication, controller, etc. Apache Kafka docs note that different SSL/SASL settings can be configured per listener using listener-specific config prefixes. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/31/configuration/broker-configs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

| Listener | Use |
|---|---|
| Internal application listener | Microservices inside network |
| External client listener | Controlled external access |
| Inter-broker listener | Broker-to-broker communication |
| Controller listener | KRaft controller communication |
| Replication/cluster link listener | Multi-cluster replication |

Application team biasanya tidak mengelola listener, tetapi harus tahu endpoint mana yang dipakai dan auth mechanism mana yang berlaku.

---

## 22. Schema Registry Security

Schema Registry adalah bagian governance penting jika memakai Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema.

| Concern | Guardrail |
|---|---|
| Who can register schema | Producer owner / CI/CD only |
| Who can read schema | Approved consumers |
| Compatibility | Subject-level policy |
| Schema deletion | Restricted |
| Subject naming | Standardized |
| Credentials | Secret manager |
| Audit | Schema change history |
| CI/CD | Compatibility check before deploy |

Schema Registry compatibility checks membandingkan schema baru terhadap versi sebelumnya sesuai compatibility type yang dikonfigurasi; setiap schema version mendapatkan ID unik dan version number meningkat. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/schema-registry/fundamentals/schema-evolution.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 23. DLQ Governance

DLQ sering mengandung payload gagal, error message, dan metadata original record. Ini menjadikannya sensitive operational store.

| DLQ concern | Guardrail |
|---|---|
| Contains PII | Redaction/masking |
| Contains raw invalid payload | Restricted ACL |
| Long retention | Retention review |
| Replay risk | Approval and audit |
| No owner | Assign owning team |
| No monitoring | Alert on DLQ count |
| Error details | Avoid secrets in error message |
| Cross-tenant payload | Tenant validation |

### DLQ minimal metadata

```json id="h3k3ho"
{
  "failureId": "01JZDLQ123",
  "failedAt": "2026-07-13T10:15:30Z",
  "consumerGroup": "order-projection-service",
  "originalTopic": "order.order.events.v1",
  "originalPartition": 2,
  "originalOffset": 88123,
  "eventId": "evt-001",
  "eventType": "OrderCreated",
  "tenantId": "tenant-a",
  "errorClass": "SchemaValidationException",
  "errorMessage": "Missing required field customerId"
}
```

## 24. Audit Model

Security governance harus bisa menjawab:

```text id="q5uhav"
Who produced this event?
Who was allowed to read it?
Who actually consumed it?
Which schema version was used?
Which credential/principal was used?
Which service version emitted it?
Was it replayed?
Was it sent to DLQ?
Was it manually corrected?
```

### Audit fields in event/log

| Field | Function |
|---|---|
| `eventId` | Event identity |
| `eventType` | Semantic |
| `eventVersion` | Contract version |
| `producer` | Owning service |
| `producerVersion` | Deployment version |
| `principal` | Kafka authenticated identity |
| `tenantId` | Tenant boundary |
| `correlationId` | Trace |
| `causationId` | Cause chain |
| Topic/partition/offset | Kafka evidence |
| Schema subject/id | Contract evidence |
| Consumer group | Processing ownership |

## 25. Java/Jersey Config Loading Pattern

```text id="i7i7jl"
Environment / mounted secrets
  ↓
Config loader
  ↓
Validate required config
  ↓
Build Kafka Properties
  ↓
Create Producer / Consumer / Admin
  ↓
Expose sanitized diagnostics
```

### Config validator

```java id="3t514v"
public final class KafkaSecurityConfigValidator {
    public static void validate(Properties props) {
        require(props, CommonClientConfigs.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG);
        require(props, CommonClientConfigs.SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG);

        String protocol = props.getProperty(CommonClientConfigs.SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG);

        if ("PLAINTEXT".equals(protocol) || "SASL_PLAINTEXT".equals(protocol)) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Insecure Kafka security.protocol is not allowed in this environment: " + protocol
            );
        }

        if (protocol.startsWith("SASL")) {
            require(props, SaslConfigs.SASL_MECHANISM);
            require(props, SaslConfigs.SASL_JAAS_CONFIG);
        }

        if ("SSL".equals(protocol) || "SASL_SSL".equals(protocol)) {
            require(props, SslConfigs.SSL_ENDPOINT_IDENTIFICATION_ALGORITHM_CONFIG);
        }
    }

    private static void require(Properties props, String key) {
        if (!props.containsKey(key) || props.getProperty(key).isBlank()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Missing required Kafka config: " + key);
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 26. Startup Security Validation

At startup, service bisa fail-fast jika config jelas salah.

```text id="lmed2y"
Startup validation:
  - security.protocol allowed?
  - SASL mechanism present?
  - truststore path exists?
  - secrets not blank?
  - bootstrap server environment matches app env?
  - required topics accessible?
  - required group id configured?
  - schema registry reachable if required?
```

### Safe validation using Admin

```java id="te4q8n"
public void validateKafkaAccess(Admin admin, Set<String> requiredTopics) {
    try {
        admin.describeTopics(requiredTopics)
                .allTopicNames()
                .get(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS);
    } catch (ExecutionException e) {
        Throwable cause = e.getCause();

        if (cause instanceof TopicAuthorizationException) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Kafka topic authorization failed", cause);
        }

        if (cause instanceof UnknownTopicOrPartitionException) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Required Kafka topic missing", cause);
        }

        throw new IllegalStateException("Kafka validation failed", cause);
    } catch (InterruptedException e) {
        Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        throw new IllegalStateException("Kafka validation interrupted", e);
    } catch (TimeoutException e) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("Kafka validation timed out", e);
    }
}
```

---

## 27. Authorization Failure Handling

| Failure | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `TopicAuthorizationException` | Principal tidak punya ACL topic | Fail startup or stop affected flow |
| `GroupAuthorizationException` | Principal tidak boleh memakai group | Fail consumer startup |
| `ClusterAuthorizationException` | Principal tidak punya cluster-level permission | Remove operation or request ACL |
| `AuthorizationException` on producer send | Write not allowed | Alert, do not swallow callback |
| Schema Registry 403 | Schema subject access denied | Fail contract validation/deploy |
| Admin describe denied | Diagnostics principal too weak | Either grant describe or disable diagnostics |

Rule:

```text id="sb8vt4"
Authorization failure is usually non-retriable until ACL/config changes.
Do not retry forever like transient network failure.
```

---

## 28. Secure Logging

### Do log

```json id="xw6som"
{
  "message": "Kafka authorization failed",
  "service": "order-service",
  "principal": "User:order-service",
  "operation": "WRITE",
  "topic": "billing.payment.events.v1",
  "correlationId": "corr-123"
}
```

### Do not log

```text id="xbrp5a"
sasl.jaas.config=... password="secret"
ssl.key.password=secret
full payload containing PII
OAuth access token
private key
```

| Log field | Safe? |
|---|---:|
| Topic | Usually yes |
| Consumer group | Usually yes |
| Principal | Usually yes |
| Event ID | Yes |
| Correlation ID | Yes |
| Tenant ID | Depends on policy |
| Full event payload | Often no |
| JAAS config | No |
| Token/password | No |

---

## 29. Rotation Strategy

| Secret/cert | Rotation concern |
|---|---|
| SCRAM password | Need dual credential or rolling restart |
| OAuth client secret | Token refresh and secret rollover |
| TLS cert | Cert expiry, truststore update |
| Truststore CA | Broker/client coordination |
| Schema Registry credential | CI/CD + runtime update |
| Debezium DB password | Connector restart/reload |
| Kubernetes Secret | Pod restart or dynamic reload |

### Rotation runbook

```text id="4cl9i8"
Prepare new credential
  ↓
Grant ACL/access to new principal if needed
  ↓
Deploy app with new credential
  ↓
Verify traffic
  ↓
Revoke old credential
  ↓
Remove old secret
  ↓
Audit completion
```

---

## 30. Governance Workflow

```text id="s0t08h"
New event/topic request
  ↓
Define owner and purpose
  ↓
Define event contract/schema
  ↓
Classify data
  ↓
Choose topic name/key/retention
  ↓
Review consumers and ACL
  ↓
Register schema / compatibility
  ↓
Provision topic and ACL via IaC/platform
  ↓
Deploy producer
  ↓
Monitor publish/consume/DLQ
```

### Topic request template

```yaml id="7mk2h8"
topic: order.order.events.v1
owner: order-platform
producer: order-service
dataClassification: confidential
containsPii: false
key: orderId
partitions: 12
retention: 7d
cleanupPolicy: delete
schema:
  format: avro
  subject: order.order.events.v1-value
  compatibility: BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE
allowedConsumers:
  - billing-service
  - search-indexer
  - order-projection-service
dlq:
  topic: order.order-events.dlq.v1
audit:
  required: true
```

---

## 31. CI/CD Governance Checks

| Check | Fail build if |
|---|---|
| Schema compatibility | New schema breaks configured policy |
| Golden event validation | Sample event invalid |
| Topic naming lint | Name violates convention |
| Data classification | Missing classification |
| PII review | Restricted data without approval |
| ACL manifest | Producer/consumer ACL not declared |
| Config scan | `PLAINTEXT` or `SASL_PLAINTEXT` in prod profile |
| Secret scan | Password/token committed |
| Dependency scan | Kafka client/security lib vulnerable |
| Contract docs | Event owner/schema/version missing |

### Example policy-as-code idea

```text id="8wmi56"
Reject deployment if:
  environment = prod
  AND kafka.security.protocol IN ["PLAINTEXT", "SASL_PLAINTEXT"]

Reject schema if:
  compatibility check fails

Reject topic if:
  owner missing
  data classification missing
  retention missing
```

---

## 32. Cloud / On-Prem Notes

| Platform | Security difference |
|---|---|
| On-prem Kafka | You may own broker config, certificates, ACL store, listener setup |
| AWS MSK | IAM/SCRAM/TLS options depend on cluster config; integrate with AWS networking/secrets |
| Azure Event Hubs Kafka endpoint | Kafka protocol surface, but auth/semantics differ from self-managed Kafka |
| Confluent Cloud | API key/secret, RBAC/ACL, managed networking options |
| Confluent Platform | Full control but more ops responsibility |
| Kubernetes Kafka | Secret mounting, NetworkPolicy, operator-managed certs |

Do not assume the same auth configs work across all providers. Treat provider-specific security as part of environment contract.

---

## 33. Threat Model

| Threat | Example | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Credential theft | JAAS password leaked in log | Secret redaction, short rotation |
| Unauthorized read | Service reads PII topic | ACL least privilege |
| Unauthorized write | Rogue producer writes fake events | ACL + schema + producer identity |
| MITM | Client connects to fake broker | TLS + hostname verification |
| Cross-tenant leak | Consumer processes wrong tenant | Tenant validation + ACL model |
| Poison event injection | Malformed event causes failure | Schema validation + DLQ |
| Replay abuse | Old events replayed maliciously | Replay authorization/audit |
| Topic deletion/config change | Data loss | Restrict admin ACL |
| Schema breaking change | Consumers fail | Compatibility check |
| DLQ exposure | Raw PII visible | DLQ ACL/redaction |

---

## 34. Operational Runbooks

### Authorization failure

```text id="px81yd"
Authorization error
  ↓
Identify principal from logs/platform
  ↓
Identify operation/resource
  ↓
Check expected ACL manifest
  ↓
If missing but valid:
      request/grant ACL via platform process
  ↓
If unexpected:
      investigate misconfiguration or attempted misuse
```

### Secret leak

```text id="483erx"
Secret leak suspected
  ↓
Revoke/rotate credential
  ↓
Deploy new secret
  ↓
Audit access during exposure window
  ↓
Search logs/repos/artifacts
  ↓
Create prevention item
```

### Certificate expiry

```text id="of3b7k"
Certificate near expiry
  ↓
Generate/issue new cert
  ↓
Update secret/truststore/keystore
  ↓
Rolling deploy
  ↓
Verify connections
  ↓
Remove old cert if safe
```

### DLQ with sensitive payload

```text id="eqlbea"
Sensitive data found in DLQ
  ↓
Restrict topic access immediately
  ↓
Identify producer and event type
  ↓
Patch producer redaction/contract
  ↓
Decide retention/delete policy with compliance
  ↓
Replay only sanitized/corrected events
```

---

## 35. Production Readiness Checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| Transport | TLS enabled, hostname verification on |
| AuthN | SASL/mTLS/OAuth configured per platform |
| AuthZ | Least privilege ACL per service |
| Secrets | No secrets in repo/image/logs |
| Rotation | Credential/cert rotation plan |
| Topic ownership | Owner, purpose, classification documented |
| Schema governance | Compatibility mode and CI check |
| Producer | Valid contract, safe key, no sensitive leakage |
| Consumer | Idempotent, replay-safe, DLQ guarded |
| DLQ | Restricted ACL, redaction, monitoring |
| Multi-tenant | tenantId and isolation model clear |
| Admin API | Read-only by default, mutating ops audited |
| Observability | Auth failures, ACL failures, publish/consume logs |
| Environment | Dev/staging/prod isolated |
| Network | Private endpoint / NetworkPolicy / firewall |
| Runbook | Auth failure, secret leak, cert expiry, DLQ leak |

---

## 36. Common Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Dampak |
|---|---|
| `PLAINTEXT` di production | Traffic dan data tidak terenkripsi |
| Satu Kafka user untuk semua service | Audit dan revocation buruk |
| ACL wildcard luas | Lateral movement risk |
| Admin ACL diberikan ke business service | Risiko topic/config destruction |
| JAAS config di repo | Credential leak |
| Log full Kafka config | Password/token leak |
| Disable hostname verification | MITM risk |
| Topic tanpa owner | Governance hilang |
| Event tanpa data classification | PII risk |
| Schema compatibility `NONE` di prod | Consumer mudah rusak |
| DLQ terbuka luas | Sensitive payload leak |
| Consumer group dipakai bersama tanpa sadar | Offset konflik |
| Direct manual ACL changes tanpa IaC | Drift dan audit buruk |
| Replay tanpa approval | Side effect/data corruption |
| Truststore/keystore baked into Docker image | Secret rotation sulit |

---

## 37. Ringkasan Praktis

Kafka security yang sehat untuk Java/Jersey microservice:

```text id="3ck6g1"
Use:
  SASL_SSL or SSL/mTLS
  least privilege ACL
  per-service identity
  secret manager
  schema compatibility
  topic ownership
  data classification
  DLQ governance
  audit logs
  CI/CD policy checks

Avoid:
  PLAINTEXT
  shared credentials
  wildcard ACL
  schema compatibility NONE
  logging secrets
  ungoverned topic creation
  unmonitored DLQ
```

Invariant utama:

```text id="5atzxb"
Every Kafka-producing or consuming service must define:
  - who it is
  - what topics it can read/write
  - what consumer group it owns
  - what schemas it can publish/read
  - what data classification it handles
  - how secrets are rotated
  - how failures are audited
  - how access is revoked
```

Untuk onboarding senior engineer, cara paling cepat membaca security posture service adalah:

```text id="faimhc"
Check:
  1. Kafka client config
  2. Service principal/credential
  3. Topic ACL
  4. Consumer group ACL
  5. Schema subject permissions
  6. Event payload classification
  7. DLQ access
  8. Secret source
  9. Rotation process
  10. Audit/observability
```

# Cheatsheet - Kafka Observability & Operations dalam Java/Jersey Microservice

## 1. Core Mental Model

Kafka observability bukan hanya “lihat consumer lag”. Untuk aplikasi Java/Jersey, observability harus menjawab:

```text
Apakah service masih hidup?
Apakah Kafka reachable?
Apakah producer berhasil publish?
Apakah consumer tertinggal?
Apakah processing lambat?
Apakah retry/DLQ naik?
Apakah ada rebalance loop?
Apakah event diproses duplicate?
Apakah schema/contract error?
Apakah Kafka Streams/ksqlDB state sehat?
Apakah incident bisa didiagnosis dari log + metric + trace?
```

Kafka server dan Java client mengekspos metrics lewat JMX; Java clients memakai Kafka Metrics registry dan metrics dapat dihubungkan ke monitoring system melalui reporter. Kafka juga menekankan bahwa remote JMX disabled by default dan harus diamankan jika dipakai di production. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/42/operations/monitoring/))

```text
Kafka Observability
│
├── Application-level
│   ├── publish success/failure
│   ├── processing success/failure
│   ├── retry/DLQ
│   ├── idempotency/duplicate
│   ├── business event latency
│   └── structured logs/traces
│
├── Kafka client-level
│   ├── producer metrics
│   ├── consumer metrics
│   ├── admin client metrics
│   ├── Kafka Streams metrics
│   └── ksqlDB/client metrics
│
├── Kafka platform-level
│   ├── broker health
│   ├── topic/partition health
│   ├── ISR/replication
│   ├── controller/group coordinator
│   └── storage/network
│
└── Operational-level
    ├── alerting
    ├── dashboards
    ├── runbooks
    ├── SLO/SLA
    ├── incident triage
    └── postmortem evidence
```

---

## 2. Observability Layers

| Layer | Yang dipantau | Contoh signal |
|---|---|---|
| **Business flow** | Apakah proses bisnis berjalan? | `OrderCreated`, `PaymentAuthorized`, saga completed |
| **Application handler** | Apakah event diproses sukses? | processing latency, failure count, duplicate count |
| **Producer** | Apakah publish sehat? | send rate, error rate, request latency |
| **Consumer** | Apakah consume sehat? | lag, poll rate, commit latency, rebalance |
| **Retry/DLQ** | Apakah failure terkendali? | retry backlog, DLQ count, oldest DLQ age |
| **Kafka Streams** | Apakah topology/state sehat? | restore time, task state, state store size |
| **ksqlDB** | Apakah query jalan? | persistent query status, lag, materialized view latency |
| **Broker/platform** | Apakah cluster sehat? | under-replicated partitions, request latency, disk |
| **Security** | Apakah ada auth failure? | authorization error, TLS/SASL failures |
| **Ops** | Apakah on-call bisa bertindak? | dashboard, alert, runbook, audit trail |

---

## 3. Golden Signals untuk Kafka Microservice

| Golden signal | Kafka/Jersey interpretation |
|---|---|
| **Traffic** | Records produced/consumed per second, request rate |
| **Errors** | Publish failure, processing failure, DLQ, authorization error |
| **Latency** | Publish latency, processing latency, end-to-end event latency |
| **Saturation** | Consumer lag, queue backlog, retry backlog, DB pool pressure |

Untuk Kafka, “latency” harus dilihat minimal dalam tiga bentuk:

```text
1. Producer latency:
   app → broker ack

2. Consumer processing latency:
   poll → business handler selesai → offset commit

3. End-to-end event latency:
   event occurredAt / outbox created_at → downstream processed_at
```

---

## 4. Producer Observability

Producer sehat jika mampu publish event dengan latency wajar, error rendah, dan tidak membuat buffer/backpressure berlebihan.

```text
Application Service
  ↓
Outbox / Producer
  ↓
Kafka broker ack
  ↓
Callback success/failure
  ↓
metric + structured log
```

### Producer Metrics

| Metric | Arti | Kenapa penting |
|---|---|---|
| `records_sent_total` | Jumlah record berhasil dikirim | Throughput producer |
| `records_send_failed_total` | Jumlah send gagal | Kafka/security/network/schema issue |
| `record_send_latency_ms` | Latency publish sampai ack | Broker/network pressure |
| `record_error_rate` | Rate error producer | Incident signal |
| `record_retry_rate` | Retry producer | Broker/network instability |
| `request_latency_ms` | Latency request ke broker | Broker/client/network |
| `buffer_available_bytes` | Sisa buffer producer | Backpressure |
| `buffer_exhausted_total` | Buffer penuh | Producer overload |
| `batch_size_avg` | Ukuran batch rata-rata | Tuning batching |
| `compression_rate` | Efektivitas compression | Throughput/storage |
| `outbox_oldest_pending_age` | Umur event belum publish | Reliability SLA |
| `outbox_pending_count` | Jumlah event menunggu publish | Relay health |

Kafka dan Confluent menyediakan JMX metrics untuk producer, consumer, broker, group coordinator, security, dan Kafka Streams; Confluent docs juga menyebut Control Center sebagai alternatif monitoring out-of-the-box. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/kafka/monitoring.html))

### Structured log saat publish sukses

```json
{
  "message": "Kafka event published",
  "service": "order-service",
  "topic": "order.order.events.v1",
  "partition": 3,
  "offset": 98123,
  "key": "order-123",
  "eventId": "evt-001",
  "eventType": "OrderCreated",
  "eventVersion": 1,
  "correlationId": "corr-123",
  "durationMs": 18
}
```

### Structured log saat publish gagal

```json
{
  "message": "Kafka event publish failed",
  "service": "order-service",
  "topic": "order.order.events.v1",
  "key": "order-123",
  "eventId": "evt-001",
  "eventType": "OrderCreated",
  "correlationId": "corr-123",
  "errorClass": "TimeoutException",
  "errorMessage": "Expiring 1 record(s) for topic...",
  "retryable": true
}
```

---

## 5. Producer Alert Rules

| Alert | Severity | Kenapa |
|---|---|---|
| Publish failure rate > baseline | Critical | Event bisnis tidak keluar |
| Outbox oldest pending age > SLA | Critical | Publication pipeline tertunda |
| Outbox pending count terus naik | Warning/Critical | Relay/CDC tertinggal |
| Producer request latency tinggi | Warning | Broker/network degradation |
| Authorization failure | Critical | ACL/credential salah, biasanya non-retryable |
| Buffer exhaustion | Warning/Critical | Producer overload/backpressure |
| Serialization error > 0 | Critical | Contract/schema bug |
| Topic not found | Critical | Provisioning/governance issue |

---

## 6. Consumer Observability

Consumer sehat jika:

```text
poll berjalan rutin
  ↓
records diproses
  ↓
offset commit setelah processing aman
  ↓
lag tidak tumbuh terus
  ↓
failure masuk retry/DLQ secara terkendali
```

### Consumer Metrics

| Metric | Arti | Kenapa penting |
|---|---|---|
| `records_consumed_total` | Record dibaca dari Kafka | Input traffic |
| `records_processed_total` | Record sukses diproses | Business throughput |
| `records_failed_total` | Processing gagal | Reliability issue |
| `processing_latency_ms` | Waktu handler | Bottleneck app/DB/downstream |
| `commit_latency_ms` | Offset commit latency | Broker/group coordinator issue |
| `poll_latency_ms` | Waktu poll | Consumer health |
| `last_successful_poll_age` | Umur poll sukses terakhir | Consumer stuck detection |
| `consumer_lag` | End offset - committed offset | Backlog |
| `consumer_lag_by_partition` | Lag per partition | Hot partition/skew |
| `rebalance_total` | Jumlah rebalance | Group instability |
| `assigned_partitions` | Partition yang dipegang | Scaling/assignment |
| `duplicate_event_total` | Event duplicate | Outbox/replay/retry signal |
| `dlq_published_total` | Event masuk DLQ | Poison/contract issue |
| `retry_published_total` | Event masuk retry topic | Transient failure |

Confluent menjelaskan penyebab consumer lag dapat berasal dari konfigurasi seperti consumer group/topic/consumer properties, dan juga performance issues seperti network latency, message size besar, slow consumer, atau throughput tinggi. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/monitor/monitor-consumer-lag.html))

---

## 7. Consumer Lag

### Formula dasar

```text
consumer_lag = log_end_offset - committed_offset
```

Tapi secara operasional, lag harus dibaca bersama rate dan latency.

```text
Lag tinggi + turun
  → consumer sedang catch up

Lag tinggi + naik terus
  → consumer tidak mampu mengejar producer

Lag tinggi di satu partition
  → hot key / partition skew

Lag tinggi semua partition
  → consumer lambat, downstream lambat, atau producer surge
```

Confluent menekankan bahwa monitoring consumer lag penting untuk kesehatan Kafka cluster, dan consumer lag dapat dipantau melalui Control Center serta JMX metrics pada platform yang mendukungnya. Confluent juga mencatat consumer lag monitoring tidak berlaku untuk consumer yang menggunakan `assign()` karena assignment tidak dikelola group coordinator. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/monitor/monitor-consumer-lag.html))

### Lag interpretation table

| Kondisi | Interpretasi | Aksi |
|---|---|---|
| Lag = 0 | Consumer catch up | Normal |
| Lag naik saat traffic naik, lalu turun | Burst normal | Monitor |
| Lag naik terus | Consumer bottleneck | Scale/tune/investigate |
| Satu partition lag dominan | Hot key | Cek key distribution |
| Lag tinggi + error tinggi | Handler failure | Cek retry/DLQ/error |
| Lag tinggi + DB latency tinggi | Downstream bottleneck | Pause/reduce concurrency |
| Lag tinggi + rebalance tinggi | Group unstable | Fix lifecycle/config/deploy |
| Lag tinggi + no records processed | Consumer stuck | Thread dump/restart/runbook |
| Group empty + lag tinggi | Consumer mati | Restart/deploy |

---

## 8. Consumer Lag Dashboard

Minimal dashboard:

```text
Consumer Group: order-projection-service
Topic: order.order.events.v1

Panels:
  - total lag
  - lag by topic-partition
  - records consumed/sec
  - records processed/sec
  - processing latency p50/p95/p99
  - commit latency
  - rebalance count
  - DLQ count
  - retry count
  - duplicate count
  - last successful poll age
```

### Partition skew view

```text
Partition | End Offset | Committed | Lag
0         | 100000     | 99990     | 10
1         | 100500     | 100490    | 10
2         | 500000     | 450000    | 50000  ← hot partition
3         | 100300     | 100295    | 5
```

Kalau satu partition jauh lebih tinggi, jangan langsung scale consumer. Consumer parallelism bounded by partition assignment; hot partition sering butuh perbaikan keying atau workload handler.

---

## 9. Rebalance Observability

Rebalance normal terjadi saat consumer join/leave group, deployment, crash, topic partition berubah, atau coordinator memutus member yang dianggap tidak sehat.

### Rebalance signals

| Signal | Arti |
|---|---|
| `rebalance_total` naik saat deploy | Normal jika rolling deployment |
| `rebalance_total` naik terus tanpa deploy | Group instability |
| `last_poll_age` tinggi | Poll loop tertahan |
| `max.poll.interval.ms` exceeded | Processing batch terlalu lama |
| Assignment berubah sering | Consumer churn |
| Lag spike setelah rebalance | Partition movement/catch-up |
| Duplicate event naik setelah rebalance | Offset commit/failure window |

### Common causes

| Cause | Explanation |
|---|---|
| Processing terlalu lama | Consumer tidak poll dalam batas waktu |
| Pod restart loop | Member keluar/masuk group |
| Deployment rolling terlalu agresif | Banyak member berubah |
| Session timeout terlalu kecil | Network jitter dianggap failure |
| Consumer thread blocked | Deadlock/downstream hang |
| Cooperative assignor belum dipakai | Rebalance lebih disruptive |
| `max.poll.records` terlalu besar | Batch terlalu lama diproses |

### Runbook singkat

```text
Rebalance spike
  ↓
Cek timeline deployment
  ↓
Cek pod restart / OOMKilled
  ↓
Cek max processing latency vs max.poll.interval.ms
  ↓
Cek DB/downstream latency
  ↓
Cek consumer logs: partitions revoked/assigned
  ↓
Tune batch size, lifecycle, graceful shutdown, timeout
```

---

## 10. Retry & DLQ Observability

Retry/DLQ bukan “tempat buang error”; ia adalah safety system yang harus dimonitor.

```text
Main consumer
  ↓ failure
Error classifier
  ├── transient → retry topic
  ├── permanent → DLQ
  └── fatal → stop/incident
```

### Retry metrics

| Metric | Arti |
|---|---|
| `retry_published_total` | Record dikirim ke retry topic |
| `retry_attempt_total` | Total attempt |
| `retry_exhausted_total` | Retry habis |
| `retry_topic_lag` | Retry backlog |
| `retry_oldest_age_seconds` | Umur retry tertua |
| `retry_success_after_attempt` | Recovery quality |
| `retry_by_error_class` | Root cause grouping |

### DLQ metrics

| Metric | Arti |
|---|---|
| `dlq_published_total` | Record masuk DLQ |
| `dlq_unresolved_count` | Operational debt |
| `dlq_oldest_unresolved_age` | SLA triage |
| `dlq_by_event_type` | Impacted contract/domain |
| `dlq_by_error_class` | Root cause |
| `dlq_replayed_total` | Recovery action |
| `dlq_replay_failed_total` | Replay problem |
| `dlq_sensitive_payload_detected` | Compliance incident |

### DLQ dashboard

```text
DLQ Dashboard
├── New DLQ records per minute
├── Unresolved DLQ count
├── Oldest unresolved age
├── Top event types
├── Top error classes
├── Top producer versions
├── Top tenants
├── Replay success/failure
└── Linked runbook
```

---

## 11. End-to-End Event Latency

Untuk event-driven system, latency paling penting sering bukan producer latency atau consumer latency saja, tapi **business event end-to-end latency**.

```text
event occurredAt
  ↓
outbox created_at
  ↓
Kafka published timestamp
  ↓
consumer poll time
  ↓
processing completed_at
```

### Latency breakdown

| Latency | Formula | Makna |
|---|---|---|
| Outbox delay | `published_at - outbox.created_at` | Relay/CDC health |
| Kafka transit delay | `consumer_received_at - kafka_timestamp` | Kafka/consumer backlog |
| Processing delay | `processed_at - consumer_received_at` | Handler/downstream |
| End-to-end delay | `processed_at - event.occurredAt` | Business SLA |
| Replay delay | `reprocessed_at - original_occurredAt` | Recovery/audit |

### Example structured metric tags

```text
event_e2e_latency_ms{
  event_type="OrderCreated",
  producer="order-service",
  consumer_group="billing-order-consumer",
  tenant="tenant-a"
}
```

---

## 12. Structured Logging Standard

### Minimum fields

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `service` | Source log |
| `environment` | dev/staging/prod |
| `eventId` | Dedup/audit |
| `eventType` | Semantic grouping |
| `eventVersion` | Rollout/schema |
| `correlationId` | End-to-end trace |
| `causationId` | Event chain |
| `topic` | Kafka source/target |
| `partition` | Kafka position |
| `offset` | Kafka evidence |
| `consumerGroup` | Processing owner |
| `key` | Aggregate routing |
| `tenantId` | Multi-tenant trace |
| `durationMs` | Performance |
| `errorClass` | Failure grouping |

### Consumer success log

```json
{
  "message": "Kafka event processed",
  "service": "billing-service",
  "consumerGroup": "billing-order-consumer",
  "topic": "order.order.events.v1",
  "partition": 2,
  "offset": 88123,
  "key": "order-123",
  "eventId": "evt-001",
  "eventType": "OrderCreated",
  "eventVersion": 1,
  "correlationId": "corr-123",
  "durationMs": 42,
  "result": "SUCCESS"
}
```

### Consumer failure log

```json
{
  "message": "Kafka event processing failed",
  "service": "billing-service",
  "consumerGroup": "billing-order-consumer",
  "topic": "order.order.events.v1",
  "partition": 2,
  "offset": 88123,
  "key": "order-123",
  "eventId": "evt-001",
  "eventType": "OrderCreated",
  "correlationId": "corr-123",
  "classification": "TRANSIENT_INFRASTRUCTURE",
  "errorClass": "SQLTransientConnectionException",
  "retryAction": "SEND_TO_RETRY_TOPIC"
}
```

## 13. Distributed Tracing

Kafka tracing harus membawa context dari HTTP request ke event headers, lalu consumer membaca dan melanjutkan trace.

```text
HTTP Request
  ↓ traceparent
Jersey Resource
  ↓
Application Service
  ↓
Kafka Producer headers:
  traceparent
  correlation-id
  causation-id
  event-id
  ↓
Kafka Consumer
  ↓ extract headers
  ↓ start child span
DB/API side effect
```

### Header standard

```text
traceparent
tracestate
correlation-id
causation-id
event-id
event-type
tenant-id
producer
```

### Span model

| Span | Tag penting |
|---|---|
| HTTP inbound | route, status, correlationId |
| DB transaction | table/use case |
| Outbox insert | eventType, eventId |
| Kafka produce | topic, key, eventType |
| Kafka consume | topic, partition, offset, group |
| Event handler | eventType, eventVersion |
| Downstream DB/API | side effect |

---

## 14. Health Checks untuk Jersey Kafka App

Pisahkan liveness, readiness, dependency, dan diagnostics.

| Endpoint | Tujuan | Kafka behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `/health/live` | Apakah process hidup | Jangan fail hanya karena Kafka transient |
| `/health/ready` | Apakah siap melayani traffic | Fail jika dependency wajib tidak siap |
| `/health/dependencies` | Detail DB/Kafka/Schema Registry | Boleh degraded |
| `/internal/kafka/diagnostics` | Topic/group/lag/debug | Internal only |

### Example health response

```json
{
  "status": "DEGRADED",
  "components": {
    "db": {
      "status": "UP",
      "latencyMs": 8
    },
    "kafkaProducer": {
      "status": "UP",
      "lastSuccessAt": "2026-07-13T10:15:30Z"
    },
    "kafkaConsumer": {
      "status": "DEGRADED",
      "groupId": "order-projection-service",
      "totalLag": 1284,
      "lastPollAgeSeconds": 2
    },
    "outbox": {
      "status": "DEGRADED",
      "pendingCount": 500,
      "oldestPendingAgeSeconds": 180
    }
  }
}
```

### Liveness vs readiness rule

```text
Liveness:
  process deadlock / unrecoverable app error

Readiness:
  should this pod receive traffic now?

Dependency:
  what is degraded?

Diagnostics:
  why is it degraded?
```

---

## 15. Kafka Streams Observability

Kafka Streams perlu observability tambahan karena ada topology, task, state store, changelog, restore, rebalance, dan interactive queries.

Kafka Streams menyimpan update state store ke changelog topic; jika task pindah ke instance lain setelah failure, Kafka Streams dapat restore state store dengan replay changelog sebelum processing dilanjutkan. Standby replicas dapat mengurangi biaya restore dan mempercepat failover dengan trade-off storage tambahan. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/streams/architecture.html))

### Kafka Streams metrics

| Metric | Kenapa penting |
|---|---|
| `streams_state` | RUNNING/REBALANCING/ERROR |
| `process_rate` | Throughput topology |
| `process_latency_ms` | Bottleneck operator |
| `commit_latency_ms` | Progress commit |
| `task_count` | Assignment visibility |
| `rebalance_total` | Stability |
| `state_restore_total` | Restore activity |
| `state_restore_latency_ms` | Recovery time |
| `state_store_size_bytes` | Disk pressure |
| `changelog_lag` | Restore/standby freshness |
| `dropped_records_total` | Data loss/contract issue |
| `deserialization_error_total` | Contract issue |
| `production_error_total` | Output topic/broker issue |
| `interactive_query_latency_ms` | Query endpoint SLA |

Kafka Streams config mendokumentasikan `metric.reporters`, `metrics.recording.level`, dan `metrics.sample.window.ms`; `JmxReporter` selalu disertakan untuk mendaftarkan statistik JMX. Config `num.standby.replicas` membuat shadow copies untuk state stores, dengan rekomendasi Confluent bahwa menaikkan ke `1` dapat membantu failover tetapi membutuhkan storage client-side tambahan. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/streams/developer-guide/config-streams.html))

### Streams health states

| State | Readiness |
|---|---|
| `CREATED` | DOWN |
| `REBALANCING` | DEGRADED/DOWN untuk query endpoint |
| `RUNNING` | UP |
| `PENDING_SHUTDOWN` | DOWN |
| `ERROR` | DOWN |

### Streams dashboard

```text
Kafka Streams Dashboard
├── app state
├── input rate
├── output rate
├── process latency p95/p99
├── rebalance count
├── task assignment
├── state restore progress
├── state store size
├── changelog lag
├── dropped records
├── deserialization errors
└── interactive query latency/error
```

---

## 16. ksqlDB Observability

Untuk ksqlDB, pantau query sebagai production artifact.

| Metric/signal | Kenapa penting |
|---|---|
| Persistent query status | Query masih running atau terminated |
| Input rate | Data masuk |
| Output rate | Query menghasilkan output |
| Query lag | Query tertinggal dari input |
| Processing error | SQL/schema/runtime issue |
| Deserialization error | Contract issue |
| Materialized view size | State capacity |
| Pull query latency | API SLA |
| Push query disconnects | Streaming stability |
| ksqlDB server health | Runtime availability |
| Schema Registry errors | Format/schema issue |

### ksqlDB runbook high-level

```text
ksqlDB output stopped
  ↓
Check persistent query status
  ↓
Check input topic has data
  ↓
Check schema/deserialization errors
  ↓
Check ksqlDB server health
  ↓
Check output topic ACL/config
  ↓
Check downstream consumer lag
```

## 17. AdminClient Diagnostics

AdminClient berguna untuk diagnostics internal, bukan high-frequency monitoring loop.

### Useful diagnostics

| Diagnostic | Cara |
|---|---|
| Required topic exists | `describeTopics` |
| Partition count | `describeTopics` |
| Topic config | `describeConfigs` |
| Consumer group state | `describeConsumerGroups` |
| Group committed offsets | `listConsumerGroupOffsets` |
| Log end offsets | `listOffsets(latest)` |
| Lag snapshot | latest offset - committed offset |
| ACL diagnostics | `describeAcls` jika permitted |

### Lag snapshot endpoint

```text
GET /internal/kafka/groups/{groupId}/lag
```

Output:

```json
{
  "groupId": "order-projection-service",
  "checkedAt": "2026-07-13T10:15:30Z",
  "totalLag": 1284,
  "maxPartitionLag": 1264,
  "partitions": [
    {
      "topic": "order.order.events.v1",
      "partition": 1,
      "committedOffset": 88000,
      "endOffset": 89264,
      "lag": 1264
    }
  ]
}
```

Rule:

```text
Diagnostics endpoint:
  - internal only
  - auth protected
  - cached
  - bounded timeout
  - never public
```

## 18. Alerting Strategy

Alert harus actionable. Jangan alert hanya karena “lag > 0”.

### Good alert examples

| Alert | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Consumer stuck | `last_successful_poll_age > threshold` | Inspect worker/thread dump |
| Lag growing | `lag increasing for N minutes` | Check processing/downstream |
| Hot partition | `max_partition_lag / avg_lag > X` | Check key distribution |
| DLQ spike | `dlq rate > baseline` | Triage contract/data bug |
| Retry exhausted | `retry_exhausted_total > 0` | Incident |
| Outbox delayed | `oldest_pending_age > SLA` | Check relay/CDC/Kafka |
| Rebalance loop | `rebalance_total high without deploy` | Check lifecycle/timeouts |
| Authorization error | Any prod authz error | Check ACL/credential |
| Serialization error | Any critical producer serialization error | Block/revert deploy |
| Streams ERROR state | state = ERROR | Restart/fix topology |
| ksqlDB query terminated | persistent query not running | Restart/fix query |

### Bad alert examples

| Bad alert | Kenapa buruk |
|---|---|
| `lag > 0` | Lag kecil normal |
| `records consumed low` | Bisa karena traffic memang rendah |
| `rebalance happened once` | Normal saat deploy |
| `DLQ count total > 0` tanpa unresolved/window | Old closed DLQ bisa false positive |
| `CPU > 70%` saja | Tidak Kafka-specific/actionable |

## 20. Incident Diagnostics: Consumer Lag Spike

```text
Consumer lag spike
  ↓
Is input rate higher than normal?
  ├── yes → producer surge / expected burst?
  └── no
       ↓
Is processing latency higher?
  ├── yes → app/DB/downstream bottleneck
  └── no
       ↓
Is rebalance count high?
  ├── yes → group instability
  └── no
       ↓
Is lag concentrated in one partition?
  ├── yes → hot key/skew
  └── no
       ↓
Check Kafka broker/network issue
```

### Checklist

| Check | Signal |
|---|---|
| Deploy timeline | Was there a release? |
| Input rate | Producer surge? |
| Processing latency | Handler slow? |
| DB pool | Connection wait? |
| Downstream API | Timeout/503? |
| Retry rate | Retry storm? |
| Rebalance | Group churn? |
| Partition distribution | Hot key? |
| Message size | Larger event payload? |
| Consumer pods | OOM/restart? |

---

## 21. Incident Diagnostics: DLQ Spike

```text
DLQ spike
  ↓
Group by errorClass
  ↓
Group by eventType/eventVersion
  ↓
Group by producer version
  ↓
Check latest deploy/schema change
  ↓
Classify:
    - data contract
    - producer bug
    - consumer bug
    - business permanent rejection
    - security/privacy issue
  ↓
Stop bad producer or patch consumer
  ↓
Replay/reject DLQ records
```

### Common DLQ causes

| Cause | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Producer breaking schema | One producer version, one event type |
| Consumer deployment bug | DLQ starts after consumer deploy |
| Unknown event version | `eventVersion` newly introduced |
| Missing required field | Validation errors |
| Poison business event | Same aggregate/state rule |
| PII/security violation | Redaction/privacy checker |
| Deserializer mismatch | Format/schema subject issue |

---

## 22. Incident Diagnostics: Rebalance Loop

```text
Rebalance loop
  ↓
Check pod restarts/OOM
  ↓
Check max.poll.interval exceeded
  ↓
Check long processing batch
  ↓
Check session timeout/heartbeat
  ↓
Check rolling deploy settings
  ↓
Check thread blocking/deadlock
  ↓
Reduce batch, tune lifecycle, fix handler
```

### Evidence to collect

```text
- consumer group id
- topic partitions
- assignment changes
- consumer logs around revoke/assign
- processing p99
- max.poll.records
- max.poll.interval.ms
- pod restart reason
- DB/downstream latency
```

---

## 23. Incident Diagnostics: Producer Publish Failure

```text
Publish failure
  ↓
Classify error:
    authorization?
    timeout?
    serialization?
    topic missing?
    message too large?
    broker unavailable?
  ↓
If outbox:
    check pending age
  ↓
If direct producer:
    assess potential event loss
  ↓
Fix root cause
  ↓
Replay from outbox if available
```

### Error map

| Error | Likely cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Authorization | ACL/credential | Fix ACL/secret |
| Timeout | broker/network/down | Retry/outbox backlog |
| Serialization | schema/mapper bug | Fix deploy, mark failed |
| Topic not found | provisioning | Create topic via governance |
| Message too large | payload too big | Redesign payload |
| Buffer full | producer overload | Backpressure/tune/scale |

---

## 24. Incident Diagnostics: Kafka Streams State Restore Slow

```text
Streams restore slow
  ↓
Check state store size
  ↓
Check changelog topic throughput
  ↓
Check standby replicas
  ↓
Check disk/network
  ↓
Check rebalance frequency
  ↓
Check pod scheduling/state dir
```

### Causes

| Cause | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| State store huge | Partition/state design, retention |
| No standby replicas | Configure standby if worth storage |
| Ephemeral disk every restart | PVC or accept restore cost |
| Rebalance loop | Fix group stability |
| Changelog broker slow | Broker/platform investigation |
| State schema migration issue | Migration plan |

## 26. Metrics Naming Convention

Gunakan naming yang konsisten.

```text
<domain>_<component>_<signal>_<unit>
```

Examples:

```text
kafka_producer_records_sent_total
kafka_producer_send_failures_total
kafka_consumer_records_processed_total
kafka_consumer_processing_latency_ms
kafka_consumer_lag
kafka_consumer_rebalances_total
kafka_dlq_published_total
kafka_retry_published_total
outbox_pending_count
outbox_oldest_pending_age_seconds
event_end_to_end_latency_ms
```

### Recommended tags

| Tag | Example |
|---|---|
| `service` | `order-service` |
| `environment` | `prod` |
| `topic` | `order.order.events.v1` |
| `consumer_group` | `billing-order-consumer` |
| `event_type` | `OrderCreated` |
| `event_version` | `1` |
| `tenant` | `tenant-a` |
| `result` | `success/failure` |
| `error_class` | `TimeoutException` |

Hati-hati cardinality tinggi: jangan jadikan `eventId`, `orderId`, atau `customerId` sebagai metric tag. Simpan di log/trace, bukan metric label.

## 27. JMX, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry

### JMX

Kafka metrics secara tradisional diekspos lewat JMX. Untuk remote JMX di production, Kafka docs menekankan perlu konfigurasi security karena authentication JMX disabled by default. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/42/operations/monitoring/))

```text
Kafka Java app
  ↓
JMX MBeans
  ↓
JMX exporter / agent
  ↓
Prometheus / monitoring system
```

### Prometheus

Common setup:

```text
JMX Exporter Java Agent
  ↓
Prometheus scrape
  ↓
Grafana dashboard
  ↓
Alertmanager
```

### OpenTelemetry

Use for:

```text
- trace propagation via Kafka headers
- spans for produce/consume/handler
- application custom metrics
- logs correlation
```

### Practical combination

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| Kafka client internals | JMX / client metrics |
| App business metrics | Micrometer/OpenTelemetry |
| Distributed tracing | OpenTelemetry |
| Logs | JSON structured logs |
| Dashboards | Grafana/Control Center/Cloud monitoring |
| Alerting | Prometheus Alertmanager/platform alerts |

## 28. Jersey/JAX-RS Instrumentation Points

```text
Resource filter
  ↓
Application service
  ↓
Outbox repository
  ↓
Kafka producer callback / relay
  ↓
Kafka consumer worker
  ↓
Event handler
  ↓
Retry/DLQ publisher
```

### Instrumentation table

| Point | Instrument |
|---|---|
| HTTP inbound | request count, latency, status |
| App command | command success/failure |
| DB transaction | latency, rollback count |
| Outbox insert | count, event type |
| Outbox relay | pending age, publish latency |
| Producer callback | success/failure, topic |
| Consumer poll | records count, poll age |
| Handler | latency, success/failure |
| Idempotency | duplicate count |
| Retry publisher | retry count by attempt |
| DLQ publisher | DLQ count by error class |
| Offset commit | commit latency/failure |
| Shutdown | graceful shutdown duration |

---

## 29. Example: Consumer Instrumentation Pseudocode

```java
public void processRecord(ConsumerRecord<String, String> record) {
    long started = System.nanoTime();

    String eventType = "UNKNOWN";
    String eventId = null;

    try {
        EventEnvelope event = deserializer.deserialize(record.value());
        eventType = event.eventType();
        eventId = event.eventId();

        handler.handle(event);

        metrics.counter("kafka_consumer_records_processed_total",
                "event_type", eventType,
                "topic", record.topic()
        ).increment();

        offsets.markProcessed(record);
    } catch (Exception e) {
        FailureClassification classification = classifier.classify(e);

        metrics.counter("kafka_consumer_records_failed_total",
                "topic", record.topic(),
                "event_type", eventType,
                "error_class", e.getClass().getSimpleName(),
                "classification", classification.name()
        ).increment();

        failureHandler.handle(record, e, classification);
    } finally {
        long durationMs = Duration.ofNanos(System.nanoTime() - started).toMillis();

        metrics.timer("kafka_consumer_processing_latency_ms",
                "topic", record.topic(),
                "event_type", eventType
        ).record(durationMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);

        log.info("Kafka record processed",
                kv("topic", record.topic()),
                kv("partition", record.partition()),
                kv("offset", record.offset()),
                kv("eventId", eventId),
                kv("eventType", eventType),
                kv("durationMs", durationMs));
    }
}
```

---

## 30. Example: Outbox Metrics Query

### Pending count

```sql
SELECT count(*) AS pending_count
FROM outbox_event
WHERE status = 'PENDING';
```

### Oldest pending age

```sql
SELECT extract(epoch FROM now() - min(created_at)) AS oldest_pending_age_seconds
FROM outbox_event
WHERE status = 'PENDING';
```

### Failed by event type

```sql
SELECT event_type, count(*) AS failed_count
FROM outbox_event
WHERE status = 'FAILED'
GROUP BY event_type
ORDER BY failed_count DESC;
```

### Publish latency

```sql
SELECT
    event_type,
    percentile_cont(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (
        ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM published_at - created_at)
    ) AS p50_seconds,
    percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (
        ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM published_at - created_at)
    ) AS p95_seconds
FROM outbox_event
WHERE status = 'PUBLISHED'
  AND published_at >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY event_type;
```

---

## 31. Operational Runbook: Event Missing Downstream

```text
Downstream says event missing
  ↓
Find business id / eventId / correlationId
  ↓
Check source DB state
  ↓
Check outbox row exists
  ↓
Check outbox status:
    PENDING / PUBLISHED / FAILED
  ↓
If PUBLISHED:
    check Kafka topic by key/time
  ↓
Check downstream consumer lag
  ↓
Check downstream processed_event table
  ↓
Check DLQ/retry topic
  ↓
Decide:
    wait, replay, fix consumer, or recover outbox
```

Evidence to collect:

```text
- eventId
- aggregateId
- eventType
- outbox created_at/published_at
- Kafka topic/partition/offset
- consumer group
- processed_event status
- retry/DLQ records
- correlationId
```

---

## 32. Operational Runbook: Duplicate Side Effect

```text
Duplicate side effect detected
  ↓
Find eventId/commandId/business id
  ↓
Check if duplicate event publish occurred
  ↓
Check consumer idempotency ledger
  ↓
Check if side effect has idempotency key
  ↓
Check replay/retry activity
  ↓
Patch consumer guard
  ↓
Compensate business effect if needed
```

Common causes:

| Cause | Signal |
|---|---|
| Outbox relay duplicate | Same eventId appears twice in Kafka |
| Consumer crash after DB commit before offset commit | Same event processed twice |
| Replay without guard | Old event reprocessed |
| Side effect lacks idempotency key | Payment/email/API duplicate |
| Dedup table missing projection name | Cross-consumer conflict |

---

## 33. Operational Runbook: Consumer Stuck

```text
Consumer stuck
  ↓
Check last successful poll age
  ↓
Check thread dump
  ↓
Check DB/downstream call hanging
  ↓
Check max.poll.interval.ms
  ↓
Check worker queue saturation
  ↓
Pause/restart if needed
  ↓
Fix root cause
```

Signals:

```text
records_consumed_total flat
last_successful_poll_age high
lag increasing
no DLQ/retry increase
CPU maybe low
thread blocked in DB/API
```

---

## 34. Operational Runbook: Retry Storm

```text
Retry storm
  ↓
Check top error class
  ↓
Check downstream health
  ↓
Check retry attempt distribution
  ↓
Pause retry consumers if needed
  ↓
Increase backoff/jitter
  ↓
Enable circuit breaker
  ↓
Move exhausted to DLQ
```

Symptoms:

| Symptom | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Retry topic lag rising | Retry workload not draining |
| DB/API latency worsening | Retry amplifying outage |
| Same error class dominates | One dependency failing |
| Main + retry consumers both failing | Storm |
| DLQ exhausted increasing | Transient did not recover |

---

## 35. Production Readiness Checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| Metrics | Producer, consumer, outbox, retry, DLQ, lag |
| Logs | Structured JSON with eventId/correlationId/topic/offset |
| Tracing | Kafka headers propagate `traceparent` |
| Dashboards | Producer, consumer, DLQ, outbox, Streams/ksqlDB |
| Alerts | Actionable, threshold + duration, linked runbook |
| Lag | Total and by-partition |
| Rebalance | Count and logs for assignment changes |
| DLQ | Owner, triage workflow, replay tooling |
| Outbox | Pending count, oldest age, failed count |
| Security | Auth/ACL failures monitored |
| Health | Liveness/readiness/dependency separated |
| Runbooks | Lag, DLQ, stuck, duplicate, publish failure |
| SLO | Event publication and processing SLOs defined |
| Cardinality | Metrics tags controlled |
| JMX | Secured if remote enabled |
| Incident evidence | Can trace event from source DB to downstream |

---

## 36. Common Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Dampak |
|---|---|
| Hanya monitor broker, bukan aplikasi | Business failure tidak terlihat |
| Alert `lag > 0` | Noise |
| Tidak monitor DLQ | Poison message tersembunyi |
| DLQ tanpa owner | Operational debt |
| Tidak punya `eventId` di log | Sulit dedup/debug |
| Tidak log topic/partition/offset | Sulit audit Kafka |
| Metric label pakai `eventId` | Cardinality explosion |
| Liveness check memanggil Kafka Admin | Pod restart karena transient issue |
| Readiness selalu UP saat consumer stuck | Traffic masuk ke instance rusak |
| Tidak punya outbox pending age | Event publication delay tidak terlihat |
| Retry storm tidak terdeteksi | Downstream makin jatuh |
| Tidak instrument processing latency | Lag root cause kabur |
| Tidak monitor rebalance | Consumer instability tidak terlihat |
| Tidak punya replay audit | Recovery tidak defensible |
| Remote JMX tanpa security | Monitoring endpoint jadi security risk |

---

## 37. Ringkasan Praktis

Observability Kafka yang baik harus bisa mengikuti satu event dari awal sampai akhir:

```text
REST command
  ↓
DB transaction
  ↓
outbox_event
  ↓
Kafka publish
  ↓
Kafka topic/partition/offset
  ↓
consumer poll
  ↓
handler processing
  ↓
DB/projection/side effect
  ↓
offset commit
  ↓
success / retry / DLQ
```

Invariant utama:

```text
Every Kafka flow must expose:
  - event ID
  - correlation ID
  - producer identity
  - topic/partition/offset
  - publish status
  - processing status
  - lag
  - retry/DLQ status
  - duplicate handling
  - end-to-end latency
```

Minimal production dashboard untuk satu consumer service:

```text
1. Total lag + lag by partition
2. Records consumed vs processed
3. Processing latency p95/p99
4. Failure rate by error class
5. Retry topic count/age
6. DLQ count/age
7. Rebalance count
8. Last successful poll age
9. Duplicate event count
10. Recent deploy markers
```
