# Cheatsheet - Kafka Performance & Capacity Tuning dalam Java/Jersey Microservice

## 1. Core Mental Model

Kafka performance tuning bukan sekadar menaikkan `batch.size` atau menambah consumer pod. Tuning harus dimulai dari **target workload**:

```text
Performance question
│
├── Throughput target
│   ├── records/sec
│   ├── MB/sec
│   └── peak burst
│
├── Latency target
│   ├── producer ack latency
│   ├── consumer processing latency
│   └── end-to-end latency
│
├── Durability target
│   ├── acks
│   ├── replication
│   ├── min.insync.replicas
│   └── idempotence
│
├── Ordering target
│   ├── per aggregate
│   ├── per tenant
│   └── no strict ordering
│
├── Processing model
│   ├── plain consumer
│   ├── Kafka Streams
│   ├── ksqlDB
│   └── outbox relay
│
└── Infrastructure constraint
    ├── broker capacity
    ├── network
    ├── disk
    ├── CPU
    ├── JVM memory
    └── Kubernetes scaling
```

Kafka performance testing sebaiknya mengukur **throughput, latency, dan resource utilization**, lalu meniru workload production seperti ukuran message, rate, burst, dan failure mode. Confluent juga menekankan bahwa performance testing harus dilakukan secara iteratif: define objective, create test scenario, execute, analyze, lalu tune ulang. ([Confluent](https://www.confluent.io/learn/kafka-performance-testing/))

---

## 2. Performance Tuning Axes

| Axis | Tujuan | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| Producer batching | Naikkan throughput | Latency bisa naik |
| Compression | Turunkan network/storage | CPU naik |
| Partition count | Naikkan parallelism | Operasional/rebalance/metadata overhead |
| Consumer concurrency | Naikkan processing rate | DB/downstream pressure |
| Fetch batching | Kurangi request overhead | Latency bisa naik |
| Message size | Efisiensi payload | Serialization/network/memory impact |
| Backpressure | Cegah overload downstream | Lag bisa naik |
| Kubernetes scaling | Elastisitas consumer/processor | Rebalance dan cold start |
| Outbox relay batch | Naikkan publish throughput | Ordering/duplicate handling makin penting |
| Broker capacity | Stabilitas cluster | Butuh platform-level planning |

---

## 3. Throughput vs Latency

```text
Throughput-oriented:
  bigger batch
  higher linger
  compression on
  larger fetch
  more partitions
  more consumers
  tolerate higher latency

Latency-oriented:
  smaller linger
  smaller batch
  lower fetch wait
  fewer buffering layers
  faster processing
  lower queueing delay
```

| Requirement | Tuning bias |
|---|---|
| Real-time notification | Low latency |
| Audit/event log high volume | Throughput |
| Payment/transaction flow | Reliability + bounded latency |
| Analytics/event tracking | Throughput + compression |
| Read model projection | Balanced |
| Retry/DLQ replay | Throughput but rate-limited |
| Kafka Streams aggregation | Throughput + state capacity |

Rule praktis:

```text
Jangan optimize throughput sampai business latency SLA rusak.
Jangan optimize latency sampai broker/client CPU boros tanpa alasan.
```

---

## 4. Producer Performance Mental Model

Producer Java bekerja seperti ini:

```text
producer.send(record)
  ↓
serialize key/value
  ↓
choose partition
  ↓
append to per-partition batch buffer
  ↓
linger until:
  - batch.size reached, or
  - linger.ms elapsed
  ↓
send request to broker
  ↓
wait for ack
  ↓
callback success/failure
```

Producer throughput terutama dipengaruhi oleh:

| Area | Config / factor |
|---|---|
| Batch size | `batch.size` |
| Wait for batching | `linger.ms` |
| Compression | `compression.type` |
| Buffer capacity | `buffer.memory` |
| Acknowledgement | `acks` |
| Retry/delivery deadline | `delivery.timeout.ms`, `request.timeout.ms` |
| Partition spread | key distribution / partition count |
| Message size | payload size, serializer |
| Network | bandwidth, RTT |
| Broker | CPU, disk, replication |

---

## 5. Producer Batching

Kafka producer mencoba menggabungkan records ke batch lebih sedikit ketika beberapa record dikirim ke partition yang sama. `batch.size` mengontrol ukuran batch default dalam bytes; batch kecil membuat batching lebih jarang dan bisa menurunkan throughput. Jika batch belum penuh, producer akan menunggu sampai `linger.ms`; sejak Apache Kafka 4.0, default `linger.ms` berubah dari `0` ke `5ms` karena batch yang lebih efisien sering memberi latency yang sama atau lebih rendah meskipun ada small linger. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/producer-configs.html))

### Config baseline

```properties
batch.size=16384
linger.ms=5
```

### Throughput-oriented example

```properties
batch.size=65536
linger.ms=20
compression.type=lz4
```

### Low-latency example

```properties
batch.size=16384
linger.ms=0
compression.type=lz4
```

| Setting | Naikkan jika | Turunkan jika |
|---|---|---|
| `batch.size` | Request terlalu banyak, throughput kurang | Memory boros, batch jarang penuh |
| `linger.ms` | Ingin batch lebih penuh | Latency SLA ketat |
| `compression.type` | Network/storage bottleneck | CPU bottleneck berat |

Confluent menyebut tuning producer batching sebagai langkah penting untuk throughput: batch yang lebih besar mengurangi jumlah request dan mengurangi CPU overhead di producer/broker, sementara `linger.ms` memberi waktu agar batch terisi; trade-off-nya adalah latency tambahan. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/optimizing/throughput.html))

---

## 6. Compression

`compression.type` default-nya `none`; valid value mencakup `none`, `gzip`, `snappy`, `lz4`, dan `zstd`. Compression bekerja pada full batch, sehingga efektivitas compression juga dipengaruhi oleh batching: batch lebih besar biasanya memberi compression ratio lebih baik. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/producer-configs.html))

| Compression | Karakter umum | Cocok untuk |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | CPU rendah, network/storage tinggi | Local/dev, payload kecil, latency sangat ketat |
| `lz4` | Cepat, rasio baik | Default praktis untuk throughput |
| `snappy` | Cepat, rasio sedang | Ekosistem lama/kompatibilitas |
| `zstd` | Rasio bagus, CPU lebih tinggi | Payload besar, storage/network mahal |
| `gzip` | Rasio bagus, CPU tinggi | Batch besar, latency kurang sensitif |

Confluent Cloud throughput guide juga merekomendasikan compression untuk throughput dan menyebut `lz4` sebagai codec yang direkomendasikan untuk performance. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/optimizing/throughput.html))

---

## 7. Producer Buffer & Backpressure

`buffer.memory` adalah total memory producer untuk buffering records yang menunggu dikirim. Jika record dikirim lebih cepat daripada bisa dikirim ke broker, producer akan block sampai `max.block.ms`, lalu gagal dengan exception. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/producer-configs.html))

```text
Application produce rate > Kafka send/ack rate
  ↓
producer buffer fills
  ↓
send() blocks
  ↓
max.block.ms exceeded
  ↓
application sees exception
```

### Config

```properties
buffer.memory=33554432
max.block.ms=5000
delivery.timeout.ms=120000
request.timeout.ms=30000
```

`delivery.timeout.ms` adalah upper bound waktu untuk melaporkan success/failure setelah `send()` return; default-nya 120 detik, dan nilainya harus lebih besar atau sama dengan `request.timeout.ms + linger.ms`. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/producer-configs.html))

| Symptom | Kemungkinan |
|---|---|
| `TimeoutException` saat send | Broker slow/down, network, delivery timeout |
| `BufferExhaustedException` / send block | Producer lebih cepat dari broker |
| Latency producer naik | Broker/network/backpressure |
| Outbox pending naik | Relay lebih lambat dari event creation |
| CPU producer tinggi | Compression/serialization terlalu berat |
| Payload too large | `max.request.size` / broker/topic cap |

---

## 8. Producer Tuning Profiles

### Profile A - Reliable business event

Untuk event penting seperti `OrderCreated`, `PaymentAuthorized`, `CaseEscalated`.

```properties
acks=all
enable.idempotence=true
compression.type=lz4
linger.ms=5
batch.size=32768
delivery.timeout.ms=120000
request.timeout.ms=30000
max.block.ms=5000
```

Gunakan dengan **transactional outbox** jika event berasal dari perubahan PostgreSQL.

---

### Profile B - High-throughput telemetry

Untuk event non-critical, analytics, clickstream, activity tracking.

```properties
acks=1
enable.idempotence=true
compression.type=zstd
linger.ms=20
batch.size=65536
buffer.memory=67108864
```

Catatan: `acks=1` mengurangi durability dibanding `acks=all`. Jangan pakai untuk event bisnis yang harus reliable.

---

### Profile C - Low-latency notification

Untuk event kecil yang perlu cepat sampai.

```properties
acks=all
enable.idempotence=true
compression.type=lz4
linger.ms=0
batch.size=16384
delivery.timeout.ms=30000
```

---

## 9. Producer Tuning Decision Table

| Goal | Tune |
|---|---|
| Throughput kurang | Naikkan `batch.size`, naikkan `linger.ms`, aktifkan compression |
| Latency terlalu tinggi | Turunkan `linger.ms`, cek broker/network latency, cek buffer pressure |
| Network bottleneck | Aktifkan `lz4`/`zstd`, kurangi payload |
| CPU producer tinggi | Pakai `lz4`/`snappy`, kurangi serialization cost |
| Buffer penuh | Naikkan `buffer.memory`, kurangi produce rate, cek broker |
| Duplicate dari retry | Pastikan idempotence on, downstream idempotent |
| Event loss risk | Pakai outbox, `acks=all`, callback monitored |
| Hot partition | Cek key distribution |
| Message too large | Kurangi payload, gunakan object reference |

---

## 10. Partitioning & Keying

Partition adalah unit parallelism Kafka.

```text
Topic order.events.v1
├── partition 0
├── partition 1
├── partition 2
└── partition 3
```

Producer memilih partition berdasarkan:

```text
if explicit partition:
  use it
else if key exists:
  hash(key) → partition
else:
  sticky partitioning / default partitioning
```

Dokumentasi producer config menjelaskan default partitioning: jika partition tidak ditentukan dan key ada, Kafka memilih partition berdasarkan hash key; jika tidak ada partition dan key, producer menggunakan sticky partition yang berubah saat batch cukup besar. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/producer-configs.html))

### Keying strategy

| Key | Cocok untuk | Risiko |
|---|---|---|
| `aggregateId` | Ordering per entity | Hot aggregate |
| `customerId` | Ordering per customer | High-volume customer hot partition |
| `tenantId` | Tenant ordering | Hot tenant sangat mungkin |
| random UUID | Distribusi merata | Ordering hilang |
| composite key | Kontrol distribusi | Consumer harus paham semantics |
| null key | Load spread | Tidak ada ordering per business key |

Rule praktis:

```text
Butuh ordering per order?
  key = orderId

Butuh throughput dan ordering tidak penting?
  key random/null

Butuh ordering per tenant?
  hati-hati: tenant besar bisa hot partition
```

---

## 11. Partition Count Capacity

Partition count menentukan maximum parallelism untuk satu consumer group.

```text
max active consumers in one group <= number of partitions
```

Jika topic punya 12 partition, maka consumer group dengan 20 pod tetap hanya 12 pod yang aktif membaca partition; sisanya idle untuk topic itu.

Confluent menekankan bahwa jumlah partition harus dipilih berdasarkan producer throughput, consumer throughput, benchmarking di environment sendiri, serta pola key agar message tersebar merata dan tidak overload pada partition tertentu. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/optimizing/throughput.html))

### Rough capacity formula

```text
required_partitions_by_producer =
  ceil(required_topic_MBps / sustainable_MBps_per_partition_produce)

required_partitions_by_consumer =
  ceil(required_topic_records_per_sec / sustainable_records_per_sec_per_partition_consume)

recommended_partitions =
  max(required_partitions_by_producer, required_partitions_by_consumer, ordering_requirement_minimum)
```

Contoh:

```text
Target:
  30,000 records/sec
  consumer handler per partition sustainable = 2,500 records/sec

required partitions:
  ceil(30,000 / 2,500) = 12 partitions
```

### Caveat

Partition terlalu sedikit membatasi parallelism. Partition terlalu banyak menambah overhead metadata, file handles, leader election/recovery, rebalance, dan operational complexity. Jadi partition count harus diuji, bukan ditebak.

---

## 12. Hot Partition

Hot partition terjadi saat sebagian besar traffic masuk ke satu partition karena key distribution tidak merata.

```text
partition 0 lag = 10
partition 1 lag = 20
partition 2 lag = 500000  ← hot
partition 3 lag = 5
```

| Penyebab | Contoh |
|---|---|
| Key tenant besar | `tenantId=big-telco` |
| Key status | `status=CREATED` semua record sama |
| Key constant | Semua event key `order` |
| Aggregate sangat aktif | Satu order/case punya ribuan event |
| Custom partitioner salah | Tidak spread merata |

### Mitigasi

| Strategy | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| Ganti key lebih granular | Ordering berubah |
| Composite key | Lebih merata, lebih kompleks |
| Split tenant besar ke topic khusus | Operasional lebih banyak |
| Increase partition count | Tidak menyelesaikan key tunggal hot |
| Shard key | Ordering per original aggregate bisa pecah |
| Handle hot aggregate khusus | Complexity naik |

---

## 13. Consumer Performance Mental Model

Consumer performance tergantung dua pipeline:

```text
Kafka fetch pipeline:
  broker → consumer fetch buffer → poll()

Application processing pipeline:
  poll() → deserialize → validate → handler → DB/API → commit offset
```

Consumer lag bisa disebabkan oleh fetch lambat atau processing lambat. Jangan tuning `fetch.min.bytes` kalau bottleneck sebenarnya ada di DB handler.

---

## 14. Consumer Fetch Tuning

`fetch.min.bytes` adalah minimum data yang broker kembalikan untuk fetch request; default `1` berarti broker menjawab segera ketika ada data atau fetch timeout. Nilai lebih besar bisa meningkatkan throughput server karena broker menunggu data lebih banyak, tetapi menambah latency. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html))

`fetch.max.wait.ms` adalah waktu maksimum broker menunggu jika data belum cukup untuk memenuhi `fetch.min.bytes`; default-nya 500ms. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html))

```properties
fetch.min.bytes=1
fetch.max.wait.ms=500
```

### Throughput-oriented consumer

```properties
fetch.min.bytes=65536
fetch.max.wait.ms=1000
max.poll.records=1000
```

### Latency-oriented consumer

```properties
fetch.min.bytes=1
fetch.max.wait.ms=100
max.poll.records=100
```

| Config | Naikkan jika | Turunkan jika |
|---|---|---|
| `fetch.min.bytes` | Banyak request kecil, throughput kurang | Latency terlalu tinggi |
| `fetch.max.wait.ms` | Ingin fetch lebih besar | Consumer butuh cepat |
| `max.poll.records` | Handler cepat dan batch overhead tinggi | Processing batch terlalu lama |
| `max.partition.fetch.bytes` | Message/batch per partition besar | Memory pressure |

`max.partition.fetch.bytes` membatasi jumlah data per-partition yang dikembalikan server. Jika batch pertama di partition non-empty lebih besar dari limit ini, batch tetap dikembalikan agar consumer bisa maju; broker/topic juga punya cap message batch size sendiri. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html))

---

## 15. `max.poll.records` dan Processing Time

`max.poll.records` membatasi jumlah record yang dikembalikan dalam satu `poll()`, default-nya 500. Config ini tidak mengubah fetching behavior bawahnya; consumer bisa cache records dari fetch request lalu mengembalikannya bertahap dari `poll()`. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html))

`max.poll.interval.ms` default-nya 300000ms atau 5 menit. Jika aplikasi tidak memanggil `poll()` sebelum timeout ini saat memakai consumer group management, consumer dianggap gagal dan group akan rebalance. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html))

### Safe batch sizing formula

```text
max_poll_records * p99_processing_time_per_record
  < max.poll.interval.ms * safety_factor
```

Contoh:

```text
p99 handler = 200ms/record
max.poll.records = 500

worst batch = 100,000ms = 100s

max.poll.interval.ms = 300,000ms

safe enough? yes, but watch DB/downstream spikes
```

Jika handler p99 = 2 detik:

```text
500 * 2s = 1000s > 300s
→ consumer risk max.poll.interval exceeded
→ reduce max.poll.records or parallelize safely
```

---

## 16. Consumer Concurrency Models

| Model | Cara kerja | Cocok untuk | Risiko |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single-thread consumer | Poll dan process di thread yang sama | Simpel, ordering kuat | Throughput terbatas |
| More consumer instances | Scale pod/instance dalam group | Workload partitioned | Bounded by partition count |
| Consumer thread + worker pool | Poll thread dispatch ke workers | Handler lambat tapi parallelizable | Offset tracking kompleks |
| One worker lane per partition | Parallel antar partition, ordered per partition | Ordering per partition | More code |
| Kafka Streams | Library manage tasks/state | Stream processing | External side effect caveat |
| Batch processing | Process batch per poll | Throughput tinggi | Failure granularity |

### Recommendation

```text
Untuk business side effect:
  mulai dengan single-thread atau one-thread-per-partition model.

Untuk projection idempotent:
  worker pool bisa dipakai dengan offset tracker.

Untuk stream transform:
  Kafka Streams lebih natural.
```

---

## 17. Consumer Scaling in Kubernetes

```text
Topic partitions = 12
Consumer group replicas:
  1  → 1 pod handles 12 partitions
  3  → each roughly 4 partitions
  12 → each roughly 1 partition
  20 → only 12 active, 8 idle
```

### Scaling rules

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Lag naik semua partition | Tambah consumer sampai partition count |
| Lag naik satu partition | Scaling pod tidak banyak membantu |
| CPU high per consumer | Tambah replicas jika partition cukup |
| DB bottleneck | Scaling consumer bisa memperburuk |
| Rebalance sering | Jangan autoscale terlalu agresif |
| Processing latency high | Optimize handler/downstream |
| Poll interval exceeded | Kurangi batch atau parallelize |

### HPA/KEDA caution

Autoscaling berdasarkan lag berguna, tetapi:

```text
scale up
  ↓
rebalance
  ↓
temporary pause/assignment movement
  ↓
lag may spike
  ↓
autoscaler may overreact
```

Gunakan cooldown, stabilization window, dan max replicas yang masuk akal.

---

## 18. Backpressure Strategy

Backpressure mencegah consumer menghancurkan DB/downstream.

```text
Kafka has backlog
  ↓
consumer pulls records
  ↓
handler hits DB/API
  ↓
DB/API slow
  ↓
consumer must slow down intentionally
```

| Lever | Level | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `max.poll.records` | Consumer | Kurangi batch per poll |
| `pause/resume` | Consumer runtime | Stop fetch partition sementara |
| Worker queue limit | App | Cegah memory blow-up |
| DB pool limit | Infrastructure | Batasi concurrent DB ops |
| Circuit breaker | App | Fail fast saat dependency down |
| Retry topic | Reliability | Pindahkan transient failure |
| Rate limiter | App | Kontrol records/sec |
| HPA scale | Kubernetes | Tambah processing capacity |
| Outbox relay rate | Producer side | Kontrol publish rate |

### Backpressure pattern

```text
if DB pool wait high:
  pause consumer partitions
  continue poll for heartbeat
  resume when downstream healthy
```

---

## 19. Message Size Tuning

Message size memengaruhi producer memory, network, broker disk, compression, consumer fetch, GC, dan deserialization.

### Payload rule

```text
Small event:
  good for latency and memory

Huge event:
  bad for broker/network/consumer
  can hit max.request.size/max.message.bytes
```

Producer `max.request.size` default 1MB dan menjadi cap ukuran request serta maximum uncompressed record batch size; server juga memiliki cap batch size sendiri yang bisa berbeda. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/producer-configs.html))

| Message size issue | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Payload besar karena full document | Simpan object di storage, kirim reference |
| Event membawa semua field table | Design contract minimal |
| Compression CPU tinggi | Pakai `lz4` atau payload trimming |
| Consumer memory pressure | Kurangi `max.poll.records`, fetch size |
| Broker rejects large message | Check topic/broker max message config |
| Slow deserialization | Optimize format/mapper |

### Anti-pattern

```json
{
  "eventType": "DocumentUploaded",
  "payload": {
    "fileBase64": "very very large..."
  }
}
```

Better:

```json
{
  "eventType": "DocumentUploaded",
  "payload": {
    "documentId": "doc-123",
    "storageUri": "s3://bucket/key-or-internal-ref",
    "sha256": "..."
  }
}
```

---

## 20. Serialization Performance

| Format | Performance note |
|---|---|
| JSON | Easy debug, larger payload, CPU parse cost |
| Avro | Compact, schema-based, good Kafka ecosystem |
| Protobuf | Compact, strong contract, good polyglot |
| JSON Schema | Governance + readability, still verbose |
| Custom binary | Fast if well-designed, but high governance burden |

### Java tips

| Problem | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| ObjectMapper created per record | Reuse singleton `ObjectMapper` |
| Reflection-heavy mapping | Use generated serializers if needed |
| Large allocation | Avoid unnecessary string copies |
| Date parsing hot path | Use stable ISO format and efficient parser |
| Unknown fields fail | Configure compatibility intentionally |
| Payload validation too heavy | Validate required fields first |

---

## 21. Outbox Relay Performance

Outbox relay has two bottlenecks:

```text
PostgreSQL claim/read/update
  +
Kafka publish/ack
```

### Tuning levers

| Lever | Effect |
|---|---|
| Batch claim size | More rows per DB roundtrip |
| Partial index pending | Faster pending scan |
| Lease-based claim | Avoid long DB locks |
| Producer batching | Higher Kafka throughput |
| Relay concurrency | More parallel publish |
| One in-flight per aggregate | Preserve ordering |
| Cleanup/partitioning | Avoid table bloat |
| Rate limit | Protect Kafka/downstream |

### Outbox batch examples

Low volume:

```text
batch_size=50
poll_interval=500ms
relay_threads=1
```

Medium volume:

```text
batch_size=200
poll_interval=100ms
relay_threads=2-4
compression=lz4
```

High volume:

```text
batch_size=500-1000
relay_threads=N
partitioned outbox table
careful ordering strategy
or Debezium CDC
```

---

## 22. Kafka Streams Performance

Kafka Streams tuning has additional state dimensions.

| Area | Concern |
|---|---|
| Input throughput | Source topic rate |
| Processing latency | Operator complexity |
| Repartition topics | Internal shuffle overhead |
| State store | RocksDB/disk usage |
| Changelog | Restore speed and write rate |
| Cache | Record cache can reduce downstream writes |
| Commit interval | Throughput vs duplicate/recovery window |
| Standby replicas | Faster failover but more storage |
| Interactive query | Query latency and routing |

### Key rules

```text
Avoid unnecessary re-keying.
Name state stores explicitly.
Monitor state store size.
Monitor restore time.
Do not put external side effects inside stream topology casually.
```

---

## 23. ksqlDB Performance

ksqlDB performance depends on query shape, input topic partitioning, state store size, joins, windows, and server resources.

| Query type | Performance concern |
|---|---|
| Filtering/projection | Usually cheap |
| Aggregation | State store growth |
| Windowing | Window retention/cardinality |
| Stream-table join | Table bootstrap/staleness |
| Stream-stream join | Window size and event rate |
| Pull query | Materialized state lookup latency |
| Push query | Long-lived connection/backpressure |

### ksqlDB tuning thinking

```text
Simple SQL transform:
  ksqlDB is often efficient

High-cardinality windowed aggregation:
  watch state size

Pull query serving many clients:
  capacity-plan like read API

Push query at high volume:
  prefer output topic + consumer
```

---

## 24. Broker/Platform Capacity Awareness

Application engineers may not own broker config, but must understand bottleneck signals.

| Bottleneck | App-level symptom |
|---|---|
| Broker CPU high | Producer/consumer request latency naik |
| Broker disk I/O slow | Produce latency, replication lag |
| Network saturated | Throughput flat, latency naik |
| Under-replicated partitions | Durability risk, producer latency |
| Controller instability | Metadata errors, leader changes |
| Topic partition skew | One broker/partition hot |
| Quota throttling | Producer/consumer throughput capped |
| Auth/ACL failures | Non-retryable send/consume errors |

Confluent performance testing guidance menyebut bottleneck umum seperti disk I/O, network congestion, insufficient partitioning, dan misconfigured broker settings; test harus meniru production workload agar bottleneck terlihat realistis. ([Confluent](https://www.confluent.io/learn/kafka-performance-testing/))

---

## 25. Capacity Planning Inputs

Sebelum tuning, kumpulkan angka berikut.

| Input | Example |
|---|---|
| Average message size | 2 KB |
| p95 message size | 8 KB |
| Peak records/sec | 20,000 |
| Peak MB/sec | 40 MB/sec |
| Retention | 7 days |
| Replication factor | 3 |
| Compression ratio | 3:1 |
| Consumer processing p95 | 30 ms |
| Consumer processing p99 | 200 ms |
| Required end-to-end SLA | 60 seconds |
| Number of consumer groups | 5 |
| Replay requirement | full 7-day replay |
| DLQ/retry expected | <0.1% |

### Storage estimate

```text
raw_data_per_day =
  average_message_size_bytes * records_per_sec * 86400

compressed_data_per_day =
  raw_data_per_day / compression_ratio

cluster_storage_with_replication =
  compressed_data_per_day * retention_days * replication_factor
```

Example:

```text
avg message = 2 KB
rate = 10,000/sec
retention = 7 days
compression ratio = 3:1
replication factor = 3

raw/day = 2KB * 10,000 * 86,400
        ≈ 1.728 TB/day

compressed/day = 1.728 / 3
               ≈ 576 GB/day

cluster storage = 576GB * 7 * 3
                ≈ 12.1 TB
```

---

## 26. Consumer Capacity Formula

```text
consumer_capacity_records_per_sec =
  active_consumers * records_per_sec_per_consumer

active_consumers <= partitions
```

If one record takes 20ms average processing time in a single-thread consumer:

```text
records_per_sec_per_consumer ≈ 1000ms / 20ms = 50 records/sec
```

If target is 5,000 records/sec:

```text
required active consumers = 5000 / 50 = 100
required partitions >= 100
```

But if handler writes to PostgreSQL, DB may not support that concurrency. Always capacity-plan downstream too.

---

## 27. DB/Downstream Capacity Coupling

Kafka can buffer far more than PostgreSQL or REST dependencies can process.

```text
Kafka throughput capacity high
  ↓
Consumer scales up
  ↓
DB connection pool exhausted
  ↓
Processing latency rises
  ↓
Lag rises more
  ↓
Retry storm
```

### Guardrails

| Guardrail | Purpose |
|---|---|
| DB pool max | Hard cap DB concurrency |
| Worker queue bound | Avoid memory blow-up |
| Rate limiter | Smooth load |
| Circuit breaker | Stop hammering failed dependency |
| Retry backoff+jitter | Avoid retry storm |
| Consumer pause/resume | Slow intake |
| HPA max replicas | Avoid uncontrolled DB pressure |
| Bulkhead pools | Separate main/retry workloads |

---

## 28. Kubernetes Resource Tuning

### Producer service

| Resource | Watch |
|---|---|
| CPU | Compression/serialization |
| Memory | Producer buffer, batch accumulation |
| Network | outbound throughput |
| Pod restarts | lost in-flight records if no outbox |
| Shutdown | flush/close producer |

### Consumer service

| Resource | Watch |
|---|---|
| CPU | Deserialization/business logic |
| Memory | batch size, worker queue |
| Network | inbound fetch |
| DB pool | downstream bottleneck |
| Pod restart | rebalance/duplicate window |
| Graceful shutdown | commit completed offsets only |

### Kafka Streams service

| Resource | Watch |
|---|---|
| Disk | state store/RocksDB |
| Memory | cache, RocksDB block cache |
| CPU | topology processing |
| Network | changelog/repartition topics |
| Startup time | state restore |
| PVC/ephemeral | restore cost trade-off |

---

## 29. JVM Tuning Considerations

| Concern | Practical note |
|---|---|
| Large batches | More heap pressure |
| JSON serialization | Allocations and GC |
| Worker queues | Avoid unbounded queues |
| Direct buffers | Network/client libs may use off-heap |
| Container memory | Set JVM container-aware limits |
| GC pauses | Can trigger consumer poll delay/rebalance |
| Thread count | Consumer + workers + HTTP + DB pool |
| Metrics cardinality | Too many label values can blow memory |

### Practical safeguards

```text
- Bound every queue.
- Avoid max.poll.records too high.
- Reuse serializers/deserializers.
- Do not create KafkaProducer per request.
- Do not create KafkaConsumer per request.
- Monitor heap, GC pause, thread count.
```

---

## 30. Performance Test Strategy

Confluent recommends defining objectives, creating realistic scenarios, executing tests, analyzing results, and iterating; realistic tests should include message size, rates, burst patterns, and failure modes close to production. ([Confluent](https://www.confluent.io/learn/kafka-performance-testing/))

### Test types

| Test | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Producer throughput test | Max publish rate |
| Consumer throughput test | Max consume/process rate |
| End-to-end latency test | Business SLA |
| Burst test | Spike handling |
| Soak test | Long-run stability |
| Failure test | Broker/downstream outage |
| Replay test | Backfill capacity |
| DLQ/retry test | Failure isolation |
| Kubernetes scale test | HPA/rebalance behavior |

Kafka ships CLI tools: `kafka-producer-perf-test.sh` produces large quantities of data to test producer performance, `kafka-consumer-perf-test.sh` tests consumer performance, and `kafka-e2e-latency` measures end-to-end latency from produce to consume. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/kafka/operations-tools/kafka-tools.html))

### Producer perf test example

```bash
bin/kafka-producer-perf-test.sh \
  --topic perf.order.events.v1 \
  --num-records 1000000 \
  --record-size 1000 \
  --throughput 50000 \
  --producer-props \
    bootstrap.servers=kafka-1:9092 \
    acks=all \
    compression.type=lz4 \
    linger.ms=20 \
    batch.size=65536
```

### Consumer perf test example

```bash
bin/kafka-consumer-perf-test.sh \
  --bootstrap-server kafka-1:9092 \
  --topic perf.order.events.v1 \
  --messages 1000000 \
  --group perf-test-consumer
```

---

## 31. Benchmarking Rules

```text
Benchmark with:
  same serializer format
  same message size distribution
  same key distribution
  same security protocol
  same compression
  same network path
  same broker class/quotas
  same consumer handler cost
```

| Bad benchmark | Kenapa misleading |
|---|---|
| Test 1KB random string, prod 20KB JSON | Payload mismatch |
| No TLS in test, TLS in prod | CPU/network mismatch |
| No compression in test, compression in prod | CPU/storage mismatch |
| Null key test, prod aggregate key | Partition skew hidden |
| Consumer perf without DB handler | Real bottleneck hidden |
| One-minute test only | GC/soak issue hidden |
| No failure test | Retry storm behavior unknown |

---

## 32. Tuning Workflow

```text
1. Define target:
   records/sec, MB/sec, latency, durability

2. Measure baseline:
   producer, consumer, broker, DB

3. Identify bottleneck:
   producer? broker? consumer? DB? network?

4. Tune one thing:
   batch, linger, compression, partition, concurrency

5. Re-test:
   same scenario

6. Check side effects:
   latency, CPU, memory, lag, retry, DLQ

7. Document profile:
   why config chosen
```

Rule:

```text
Do not tune blind.
Do not tune multiple knobs at once unless doing controlled experiment.
```

---

## 33. Common Bottleneck → Action Matrix

| Bottleneck | Evidence | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Producer too many requests | Low batch size, high request rate | Increase `batch.size`, `linger.ms` |
| Network saturated | High MB/sec, broker network high | Compression, payload trim |
| Producer CPU high | Serialization/compression heavy | Optimize serializer, use lz4 |
| Broker latency high | Request latency high across clients | Platform investigation |
| Consumer processing slow | Handler p95/p99 high | Optimize handler, DB, concurrency |
| DB bottleneck | DB pool wait/slow query | Rate limit, pause, optimize DB |
| Hot partition | One partition lag high | Key strategy |
| Rebalance loop | Rebalance count high | Tune lifecycle, batch, poll interval |
| DLQ spike | Contract errors | Fix producer/schema/consumer |
| Retry storm | Retry topic grows | Backoff, circuit breaker |
| Streams restore slow | Restore metrics high | Standby replicas/PVC/state size |
| ksqlDB query slow | Pull latency/query lag | Query/index/materialization review |

---

## 34. Configuration Cheat Table

### Producer

| Config | Default / note | Tuning effect |
|---|---|---|
| `batch.size` | Default 16384 bytes | Larger = better batching, more memory |
| `linger.ms` | Default 5ms in Kafka 4.x docs | Larger = throughput, possible latency |
| `compression.type` | Default `none`; valid `gzip`, `snappy`, `lz4`, `zstd` | Lower network/storage |
| `buffer.memory` | Total producer buffer | More burst tolerance |
| `acks` | Durability/ack behavior | `all` for important events |
| `enable.idempotence` | Avoid producer retry duplicates | Keep enabled unless strong reason |
| `delivery.timeout.ms` | Default 120s | Bound send lifecycle |
| `max.request.size` | Default 1MB | Large messages/request cap |

Producer config defaults and behavior above are documented in current Confluent/Kafka configuration references. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/producer-configs.html))

### Consumer

| Config | Default / note | Tuning effect |
|---|---|---|
| `max.poll.records` | Default 500 | Batch returned to app |
| `max.poll.interval.ms` | Default 5 minutes | Max processing gap between poll |
| `fetch.min.bytes` | Default 1 | Larger fetch = throughput, latency trade-off |
| `fetch.max.wait.ms` | Default 500ms | Max wait for fetch.min.bytes |
| `max.partition.fetch.bytes` | Per-partition fetch cap | Needed for larger batches/messages |
| `heartbeat.interval.ms` | Default 3s in classic protocol | Lower than session timeout |
| `partition.assignment.strategy` | Default includes Range + CooperativeSticky | Rebalance behavior |

Consumer config defaults and behavior above are documented in Confluent’s current consumer config reference. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html))

## 36. Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Dampak |
|---|---|
| Tuning tanpa baseline | Tidak tahu improvement/regression |
| Menambah consumer pod melebihi partition count | Pod idle, rebalance overhead |
| Key pakai `tenantId` untuk tenant besar | Hot partition |
| `max.poll.records` besar padahal handler lambat | Rebalance karena poll interval |
| Worker queue unbounded | Memory blow-up |
| Scaling consumer saat DB sudah bottleneck | DB makin jatuh |
| Payload besar berisi document/blob | Network/memory/broker pressure |
| Compression berat saat CPU bottleneck | Latency naik |
| `linger.ms` tinggi untuk low-latency event | SLA rusak |
| Direct producer tanpa callback monitoring | Publish failure tidak terlihat |
| Outbox relay tanpa rate limit | Kafka/downstream spike |
| Benchmark tanpa TLS/security | Hasil terlalu optimis |
| Benchmark tanpa real handler | Bottleneck aplikasi tersembunyi |
| Menganggap lag selalu buruk | Lag bisa normal saat burst/catch-up |
| Mengubah partition count tanpa key/order review | Semantics berubah |

---

## 37. Production Readiness Checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| Baseline | Ada angka records/sec, MB/sec, p95/p99 latency |
| Producer | `batch.size`, `linger.ms`, compression dipilih sadar |
| Reliability | `acks`, idempotence, outbox untuk event penting |
| Partition | Count dan keying sesuai throughput/order |
| Consumer | `max.poll.records` sesuai handler p99 |
| Concurrency | Consumer replicas tidak melebihi useful partition count |
| Backpressure | Queue bounded, pause/resume/rate limit |
| DB/downstream | Capacity tidak kalah dari consumer throughput |
| Message size | p95 payload diketahui dan aman |
| Serialization | Serializer reused dan tested |
| Kubernetes | CPU/memory requests, graceful shutdown |
| Observability | Producer latency, consumer lag, DLQ, retry, outbox |
| Testing | Perf test normal, peak, burst, failure, replay |
| Documentation | Config profile dan alasan tuning dicatat |

---

## 38. Quick Decision Guide

```text
Producer throughput kurang?
  → batch.size, linger.ms, compression, partition spread

Producer latency tinggi?
  → broker/network check, lower linger, check buffer/backpressure

Consumer lag naik semua partition?
  → handler/downstream bottleneck or not enough consumers

Consumer lag naik satu partition?
  → hot key / skew

Consumer rebalance terus?
  → max.poll.interval, processing time, pod restarts, graceful shutdown

DB lambat?
  → do not blindly scale consumers; apply backpressure

Payload besar?
  → trim event, use reference, compression

Need more parallelism?
  → partitions first, then consumers

Need strict ordering?
  → key by aggregate and avoid unsafe parallelism

Need high replay speed?
  → separate replay consumer, rate limit, idempotency
```

---

## 39. Ringkasan Praktis

Performance Kafka di Java/Jersey harus dituning sebagai pipeline end-to-end:

```text
Producer app
  → serialization
  → batching/compression
  → broker/topic/partition
  → consumer fetch
  → handler processing
  → DB/API side effect
  → offset commit
  → retry/DLQ/replay
```

Invariant utama:

```text
1. Throughput tidak boleh mengorbankan correctness.
2. Latency tidak boleh diukur hanya di producer.
3. Partition count menentukan parallelism, tapi key menentukan distribusi.
4. Consumer scaling tidak boleh melebihi downstream capacity.
5. Batch besar meningkatkan throughput tapi memperbesar failure/latency window.
6. Compression menghemat network/storage tapi memakai CPU.
7. Benchmark harus meniru production workload.
8. Semua tuning harus terlihat di metric, bukan feeling.
```

Untuk service bisnis berbasis PostgreSQL, baseline paling aman:

```text
Producer:
  outbox + acks=all + idempotence + lz4 + moderate batch

Consumer:
  manual commit + idempotency + bounded batch + backpressure

Scaling:
  partition-aware + DB-aware + lag-aware

Testing:
  normal + peak + burst + failure + replay
```

# Cheatsheet - Kafka Testing Strategy dalam Java/Jersey Microservice

## 1. Core Mental Model

Testing Kafka-based microservice harus membuktikan tiga hal:

```text id="kafka-testing-goal"
1. Contract benar
   Event yang dipublish/consume sesuai schema, version, key, header, dan semantic.

2. Behavior benar
   Producer, consumer, retry, DLQ, outbox, idempotency, dan offset handling bekerja sesuai failure model.

3. Integration benar
   Service benar-benar bisa bicara dengan Kafka, PostgreSQL, Schema Registry, dan komponen runtime lain.
```

Kafka sendiri menyediakan class testing seperti `MockProducer` dan `MockConsumer`; `MockProducer` adalah mock dari Producer interface untuk testing code yang memakai Kafka producer dan secara default menyelesaikan setiap `send()` secara sinkron dengan sukses, tetapi bisa dikonfigurasi agar completion dikontrol manual atau menghasilkan error. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/24/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/MockProducer.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```text id="testing-pyramid"
Kafka Testing Pyramid
│
├── Unit tests
│   ├── event mapper
│   ├── serializer/deserializer wrapper
│   ├── producer wrapper with MockProducer
│   ├── consumer handler pure logic
│   └── retry/DLQ classifier
│
├── Component tests
│   ├── consumer worker with MockConsumer
│   ├── outbox relay with fake producer
│   ├── offset tracker
│   ├── idempotency repository
│   └── failure classification
│
├── Contract tests
│   ├── schema compatibility
│   ├── golden event validation
│   ├── header/key contract
│   ├── consumer compatibility
│   └── version handling
│
├── Integration tests
│   ├── Testcontainers Kafka
│   ├── PostgreSQL
│   ├── Schema Registry if used
│   ├── outbox relay E2E
│   └── retry/DLQ topics
│
├── System/E2E tests
│   ├── REST command → DB → outbox → Kafka
│   ├── Kafka event → consumer → DB side effect
│   ├── saga/process orchestration
│   └── replay scenario
│
└── Operational tests
    ├── broker unavailable
    ├── duplicate publish
    ├── poison message
    ├── rebalance
    ├── shutdown
    └── recovery/replay
```

---

## 2. Apa yang Wajib Diuji?

| Area | Pertanyaan test |
|---|---|
| Producer wrapper | Apakah topic, key, value, headers benar? |
| Event mapper | Apakah domain object dimap ke integration event dengan benar? |
| Serialization | Apakah payload valid dan backward/forward-aware? |
| Outbox | Apakah business state + outbox insert satu transaction? |
| Relay | Apakah mark `PUBLISHED` hanya setelah Kafka ack? |
| Consumer handler | Apakah idempotent dan transaction-safe? |
| Offset commit | Apakah offset commit hanya setelah side effect sukses? |
| Retry | Apakah transient failure masuk retry topic? |
| DLQ | Apakah permanent/poison event masuk DLQ dengan metadata lengkap? |
| Rebalance | Apakah revoked partition commit safe offset? |
| Shutdown | Apakah worker close gracefully? |
| Replay | Apakah replay tidak menggandakan side effect? |
| Schema | Apakah schema baru compatible? |
| Security | Apakah auth/ACL failure diperlakukan non-retryable? |
| Observability | Apakah log/metric membawa eventId/correlationId/topic/offset? |

---

## 3. Testing Scope Matrix

| Test type | Kafka asli? | DB asli? | Cepat? | Tujuan |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Unit mapper | Tidak | Tidak | Sangat cepat | Business/event mapping |
| Unit producer wrapper | MockProducer | Tidak | Cepat | Topic/key/header/callback |
| Unit handler | Tidak | Fake/in-memory | Cepat | Business logic |
| Component consumer | MockConsumer | Fake/Test DB | Cepat-sedang | Poll loop, offset tracking |
| Contract test | Tidak selalu | Tidak | Cepat | Schema/golden event |
| Integration test | Testcontainers Kafka | Testcontainers PostgreSQL | Sedang | Real Kafka protocol |
| E2E local | Testcontainers stack | Ya | Lebih lambat | REST → Kafka → DB |
| Failure injection | Testcontainers/fake | Ya | Sedang-lambat | Recovery behavior |
| Performance smoke | Real-ish env | Real-ish | Lambat | Throughput/latency sanity |

Rule praktis:

```text id="test-scope-rule"
Jangan semua test pakai Kafka container.
Jangan semua test hanya mock Kafka.

Gunakan mock untuk logic cepat.
Gunakan Testcontainers untuk membuktikan integration boundary.
Gunakan contract test untuk mencegah breaking event.
```

---

## 4. Dependency Setup Maven

### Kafka clients + test utils

```xml id="maven-kafka-test-utils"
<dependency>
```

Untuk Kafka Streams, Apache Kafka menyediakan `TopologyTestDriver` di package `test-utils`, yang dapat dipakai untuk “pipe” data melalui topology yang dibuat dengan Processor API atau DSL `StreamsBuilder` dan memverifikasi hasilnya tanpa menjalankan cluster Kafka nyata. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/41/streams/developer-guide/testing/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

([Testcontainers for Java](https://java.testcontainers.org/modules/kafka/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 5. Unit Test Producer dengan MockProducer

### Producer wrapper

```java id="producer-wrapper"
public final class KafkaEventPublisher {
    private final Producer<String, String> producer;
    private final ObjectMapper objectMapper;
    private final String topic;

    public KafkaEventPublisher(
            Producer<String, String> producer,
            ObjectMapper objectMapper,
            String topic
    ) {
        this.producer = producer;
        this.objectMapper = objectMapper;
        this.topic = topic;
    }

    public void publish(OrderCreatedEvent event) {
        try {
            String payload = objectMapper.writeValueAsString(event);

            ProducerRecord<String, String> record =
                    new ProducerRecord<>(topic, event.aggregateId(), payload);

            record.headers()
                    .add("event-id", bytes(event.eventId()))
                    .add("event-type", bytes(event.eventType()))
                    .add("correlation-id", bytes(event.correlationId()));

            producer.send(record, (metadata, exception) -> {
                if (exception != null) {
                    // metric/log/failure handling
                }
            });
        } catch (JsonProcessingException e) {
            throw new SerializationFailureException(e);
        }
    }

    private byte[] bytes(String value) {
        return value.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }
}
```

### Test topic, key, header

```java id="mockproducer-test"
@Test
void publishShouldUseCorrectTopicKeyAndHeaders() {
    MockProducer<String, String> producer = new MockProducer<>(
            true,
            new StringSerializer(),
            new StringSerializer()
    );

    KafkaEventPublisher publisher =
            new KafkaEventPublisher(producer, new ObjectMapper(), "order.order.events.v1");

    OrderCreatedEvent event = Fixtures.orderCreatedEvent(
            "evt-001",
            "order-123",
            "corr-001"
    );

    publisher.publish(event);

    List<ProducerRecord<String, String>> history = producer.history();

    assertThat(history).hasSize(1);

    ProducerRecord<String, String> record = history.get(0);

    assertThat(record.topic()).isEqualTo("order.order.events.v1");
    assertThat(record.key()).isEqualTo("order-123");
    assertThat(header(record, "event-id")).isEqualTo("evt-001");
    assertThat(header(record, "event-type")).isEqualTo("OrderCreated");
    assertThat(header(record, "correlation-id")).isEqualTo("corr-001");
}
```

### Helper

```java id="header-helper"
private static String header(ProducerRecord<String, String> record, String name) {
    Header header = record.headers().lastHeader(name);

    assertThat(header).as("header " + name).isNotNull();

    return new String(header.value(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
}
```

---

## 6. Test Producer Failure Path

`MockProducer` bisa dipakai untuk mengontrol completion secara manual, bukan otomatis sukses.

```java id="mockproducer-failure"
@Test
void publishShouldRecordFailureWhenKafkaSendFails() {
    MockProducer<String, String> producer = new MockProducer<>(
            false,
            new StringSerializer(),
            new StringSerializer()
    );

    TestFailureRecorder failureRecorder = new TestFailureRecorder();

    KafkaEventPublisher publisher =
            new KafkaEventPublisher(producer, new ObjectMapper(), "order.order.events.v1");

    publisher.publish(Fixtures.orderCreatedEvent());

    assertThat(producer.history()).hasSize(1);

    producer.errorNext(new TimeoutException("broker timeout"));

    assertThat(failureRecorder.failures()).hasSize(1);
}
```

Yang perlu diuji:

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| Serialization failure | Tidak call producer; throw non-retryable |
| Kafka timeout callback | Failure metric/log tercatat |
| Authorization failure | Classified non-retryable |
| Topic missing | Classified provisioning/platform issue |
| Message too large | Classified contract/payload issue |
| Close producer | `producer.close()` dipanggil saat shutdown |

---

## 7. Unit Test Event Mapper

Event mapper harus stabil karena dia membentuk contract.

```java id="event-mapper-test"
@Test
void shouldMapOrderDomainToIntegrationEvent() {
    Order order = OrderFixtures.createdOrder("order-123", "customer-456");
    RequestContext context = new RequestContext(
            "tenant-a",
            "corr-001",
            "cmd-001"
    );

    OrderCreatedEvent event = mapper.toOrderCreated(order, context);

    assertThat(event.eventType()).isEqualTo("OrderCreated");
    assertThat(event.eventVersion()).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(event.aggregateType()).isEqualTo("Order");
    assertThat(event.aggregateId()).isEqualTo("order-123");
    assertThat(event.correlationId()).isEqualTo("corr-001");
    assertThat(event.causationId()).isEqualTo("cmd-001");
    assertThat(event.payload().orderId()).isEqualTo("order-123");
    assertThat(event.payload().customerId()).isEqualTo("customer-456");
}
```

Test tambahan:

| Test | Tujuan |
|---|---|
| Required field not null | Contract completeness |
| Tenant id propagated | Multi-tenant safety |
| Correlation id propagated | Observability |
| Aggregate id equals key | Ordering correctness |
| Payload tidak bocor internal field | Privacy |
| Monetary field pakai minor units/currency | Semantic stability |
| Event version benar | Evolution control |

## 9. Contract Test Schema Compatibility

Jika menggunakan Schema Registry, contract test minimal:

```text id="schema-contract-tests"
1. New schema is compatible with configured subject policy.
2. Producer sample event validates against schema.
3. Consumer can deserialize old event version.
4. Consumer tolerates new optional fields.
5. Unknown event version has defined behavior.
```

Schema Registry compatibility sangat penting karena event lama bisa tetap ada di Kafka sesuai retention dan bisa direplay. Untuk production, schema registration idealnya lewat CI/CD, bukan auto-register liar dari runtime producer.

### Compatibility gate pseudo-flow

```text id="schema-ci-gate"
Schema PR
  ↓
Run compatibility check against registry/test registry
  ↓
Run golden event validation
  ↓
Run consumer compatibility tests
  ↓
Allow merge/deploy
```

## 10. Unit Test Consumer Handler

Pisahkan handler domain dari Kafka API.

### Good boundary

```java id="consumer-handler-boundary"
public final class OrderCreatedHandler {
    private final TransactionManager transaction;
    private final ProcessedEventRepository processedEvents;
    private final OrderProjectionRepository projections;

    public void handle(OrderCreatedEvent event) {
        transaction.inTransaction(() -> {
            boolean firstTime = processedEvents.tryInsert(event.eventId());

            if (!firstTime) {
                return null;
            }

            projections.upsertOrderCreated(event);

            return null;
        });
    }
}
```

### Test idempotency

```java id="consumer-idempotency-test"
@Test
void duplicateEventShouldNotApplyProjectionTwice() {
    OrderCreatedEvent event = Fixtures.orderCreatedEvent("evt-001", "order-123");

    handler.handle(event);
    handler.handle(event);

    assertThat(processedEventRepository.count()).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(orderProjectionRepository.updateCount("order-123")).isEqualTo(1);
}
```

### Test failure rollback

```java id="consumer-rollback-test"
@Test
void processingFailureShouldRollbackProcessedEventInsert() {
    OrderCreatedEvent event = Fixtures.orderCreatedEvent("evt-001", "order-123");

    projectionRepository.failNextWrite();

    assertThrows(RuntimeException.class, () -> handler.handle(event));

    assertThat(processedEventRepository.exists("evt-001")).isFalse();
}
```

## 11. Component Test Consumer dengan MockConsumer

`MockConsumer` adalah mock dari Consumer interface untuk testing code yang memakai Kafka consumer. Class ini tidak thread-safe, tetapi menyediakan `schedulePollTask(Runnable)` untuk skenario test multithread ketika driver thread menunggu `poll()` dipanggil background thread. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/10/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/MockConsumer.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Consumer worker design

```java id="consumer-worker-testable"
public final class KafkaConsumerWorker implements Runnable {
    private final Consumer<String, String> consumer;
    private final EventDispatcher dispatcher;
    private final AtomicBoolean running = new AtomicBoolean(true);

    public void run() {
        consumer.subscribe(List.of("order.order.events.v1"));

        while (running.get()) {
            ConsumerRecords<String, String> records =
                    consumer.poll(Duration.ofMillis(100));

            for (ConsumerRecord<String, String> record : records) {
                dispatcher.dispatch(record);
            }

            consumer.commitSync();
        }
    }

    public void stop() {
        running.set(false);
        consumer.wakeup();
    }
}
```

### MockConsumer test sketch

```java id="mockconsumer-test"
@Test
void workerShouldProcessRecordsAndCommitOffsets() {
    MockConsumer<String, String> consumer =
            new MockConsumer<>(OffsetResetStrategy.EARLIEST);

    TopicPartition partition = new TopicPartition("order.order.events.v1", 0);

    consumer.schedulePollTask(() -> {
        consumer.rebalance(List.of(partition));
        consumer.updateBeginningOffsets(Map.of(partition, 0L));
    });

    consumer.schedulePollTask(() -> {
        consumer.addRecord(new ConsumerRecord<>(
                "order.order.events.v1",
                0,
                0L,
                "order-123",
                Fixtures.orderCreatedJson("evt-001")
        ));
    });

    consumer.schedulePollTask(() -> worker.stop());

    KafkaConsumerWorker worker = new KafkaConsumerWorker(consumer, dispatcher);

    worker.run();

    assertThat(dispatcher.processedEventIds()).containsExactly("evt-001");

    OffsetAndMetadata committed =
            consumer.committed(Set.of(partition)).get(partition);

    assertThat(committed.offset()).isEqualTo(1L);
}
```

Hal yang diuji:

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| 1 record sukses | Handler dipanggil, offset commit next offset |
| Handler throw | Offset tidak commit |
| Duplicate event | Handler dedup, offset commit |
| Poison event | DLQ publish, offset commit jika DLQ sukses |
| DLQ publish gagal | Offset tidak commit |
| Stop worker | Consumer close/wakeup graceful |
| Rebalance revoked | Safe offset committed |

## 12. Offset Commit Test

Offset commit harus commit **next offset** setelah record terakhir yang aman diproses.

```text id="offset-test-rule"
Processed record offset = 42
Committed offset should be = 43
```

### Test per partition

```java id="offset-tracker-test"
@Test
void shouldCommitNextOffsetPerPartition() {
    OffsetTracker tracker = new OffsetTracker();

    TopicPartition p0 = new TopicPartition("orders", 0);
    TopicPartition p1 = new TopicPartition("orders", 1);

    tracker.markProcessed(p0, 10L);
    tracker.markProcessed(p0, 11L);
    tracker.markProcessed(p1, 5L);

    Map<TopicPartition, OffsetAndMetadata> offsets = tracker.commitOffsets();

    assertThat(offsets.get(p0).offset()).isEqualTo(12L);
    assertThat(offsets.get(p1).offset()).isEqualTo(6L);
}
```

### Worker-pool gap test

```text id="offset-gap-test"
partition 0:
  offset 100 done
  offset 101 still processing
  offset 102 done

Safe commit = 101
Not 103
```

```java id="offset-gap-unit-test"
@Test
void shouldNotCommitPastGap() {
    OffsetTracker tracker = new OffsetTracker();

    TopicPartition p = new TopicPartition("orders", 0);

    tracker.markDispatched(p, 100);
    tracker.markDispatched(p, 101);
    tracker.markDispatched(p, 102);

    tracker.markCompleted(p, 100);
    tracker.markCompleted(p, 102);

    assertThat(tracker.safeCommitOffset(p)).isEqualTo(101L);
}
```

```java id="retry-classifier"
}
```

```java id="failure-classifier-test"
            arguments(new SchemaValidationException("missing field"), SEND_TO_DLQ),

            arguments(new SocketTimeoutException("downstream timeout"), SEND_TO_RETRY_TOPIC),
```

## 14. DLQ Publisher Test

DLQ test harus memastikan metadata original Kafka record tidak hilang.

```java id="dlq-publisher-test"
@Test
void shouldPublishDlqWithOriginalMetadata() {
    ConsumerRecord<String, String> original =
            new ConsumerRecord<>(
                    "order.order.events.v1",
                    2,
                    88123L,
                    "order-123",
                    "{bad-json"
            );

    dlqPublisher.publish(original, new SchemaValidationException("bad json"));

    ProducerRecord<String, String> dlqRecord = producer.history().get(0);

    assertThat(dlqRecord.topic()).isEqualTo("order.order-events.dlq.v1");
    assertThat(dlqRecord.key()).isEqualTo("order-123");

    JsonNode body = objectMapper.readTree(dlqRecord.value());

    assertThat(body.get("originalTopic").asText()).isEqualTo("order.order.events.v1");
    assertThat(body.get("originalPartition").asInt()).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(body.get("originalOffset").asLong()).isEqualTo(88123L);
    assertThat(body.get("errorClass").asText()).isEqualTo("SchemaValidationException");
}
```

DLQ metadata minimal:

```text id="dlq-test-fields"
- failureId
- failedAt
- consumerGroup
- originalTopic
- originalPartition
- originalOffset
- originalKey
- eventId if parseable
- eventType if parseable
- correlationId if parseable
- errorClass
- errorMessage sanitized
- payload or payload reference
```

## 16. Outbox Relay Test

### Fake producer

```java id="fake-producer"
public final class FakeKafkaPublisher implements EventPublisher {
    private final List<OutboxEvent> published = new ArrayList<>();
    private RuntimeException nextFailure;

    public void failNext(RuntimeException failure) {
        this.nextFailure = failure;
    }

    public void publish(OutboxEvent event) {
        if (nextFailure != null) {
            RuntimeException failure = nextFailure;
            nextFailure = null;
            throw failure;
        }

        published.add(event);
    }
}
```

### Mark published only after success

```java id="relay-success-test"
@Test
void relayShouldMarkPublishedOnlyAfterKafkaSuccess() {
    OutboxEvent event = outboxRepository.insertPending(Fixtures.outboxEvent());

    relay.runOnce();

    OutboxEvent reloaded = outboxRepository.find(event.id());

    assertThat(reloaded.status()).isEqualTo("PUBLISHED");
    assertThat(fakePublisher.published()).hasSize(1);
}
```

### Failure reschedules

```java id="relay-failure-test"
@Test
void relayShouldRescheduleWhenKafkaFails() {
    OutboxEvent event = outboxRepository.insertPending(Fixtures.outboxEvent());

    fakePublisher.failNext(new TimeoutException("broker unavailable"));

    relay.runOnce();

    OutboxEvent reloaded = outboxRepository.find(event.id());

    assertThat(reloaded.status()).isEqualTo("PENDING");
    assertThat(reloaded.retryCount()).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(reloaded.nextAttemptAt()).isAfter(Instant.now());
}
```

### Crash after publish simulation

```text id="relay-crash-test"
1. Relay publishes event to Kafka.
2. Relay crashes before markPublished.
3. Lease expires.
4. Relay publishes same outbox row again.
5. Consumer dedup must handle duplicate eventId.
```

Test expected: duplicate publish possible, downstream idempotency works.

## 24. Rebalance Test

Rebalance test sulit tetapi penting untuk worker yang commit offset manual.

### What to test

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Partition revoked after processing | Safe offsets committed |
| Partition revoked while record in-flight | Do not commit beyond completed |
| Worker shutdown | Wakeup and close cleanly |
| Duplicate after rebalance | Idempotency handles duplicate |
| Assignment changes | Internal state reset per partition |

### MockConsumer approach

Gunakan `schedulePollTask` untuk trigger `rebalance()` dan records.

```java id="mockconsumer-rebalance-test"
@Test
void shouldCommitSafeOffsetsOnPartitionRevoked() {
    MockConsumer<String, String> consumer =
            new MockConsumer<>(OffsetResetStrategy.EARLIEST);

    TopicPartition p0 = new TopicPartition("orders", 0);

    consumer.schedulePollTask(() -> {
        consumer.rebalance(List.of(p0));
        consumer.updateBeginningOffsets(Map.of(p0, 0L));
    });

    consumer.schedulePollTask(() -> {
        consumer.addRecord(new ConsumerRecord<>("orders", 0, 0L, "order-1", eventJson("evt-1")));
    });

    consumer.schedulePollTask(() -> {
        consumer.rebalance(List.of()); // revoke partition
        worker.stop();
    });

    worker.run();

    assertThat(offsetCommitRecorder.committedOffset(p0)).isEqualTo(1L);
}
```

## 25. Graceful Shutdown Test

```text id="shutdown-test-flow"
SIGTERM / stop called
  ↓
consumer.wakeup()
  ↓
poll loop exits
  ↓
finish completed records
  ↓
commit safe offsets
  ↓
close consumer
```

### Test expectation

| Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|
| Stop while idle | Worker exits quickly |
| Stop while processing | Completed offsets committed |
| Stop while record in-flight fails | Unsafe offset not committed |
| Producer close | Flush/close called |
| Outbox relay stop | No new claims; in-flight handled safely |

## 26. Kafka Streams TopologyTestDriver

`TopologyTestDriver` mensimulasikan Kafka Streams runtime untuk topology test. Test dapat memberikan input records ke source topic dan membaca output records dari sink topic; Apache docs juga mencatat test driver mensimulasikan single-partitioned input topics. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/24/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/streams/TopologyTestDriver.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Example

```java id="topology-test-driver"
@Test
void shouldEnrichOrderCreated() {
    StreamsBuilder builder = new StreamsBuilder();

    Topology topology = OrderTopology.build(builder);

    Properties props = new Properties();
    props.put(StreamsConfig.APPLICATION_ID_CONFIG, "order-topology-test");
    props.put(StreamsConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, "dummy:9092");

    try (TopologyTestDriver driver = new TopologyTestDriver(topology, props)) {
        TestInputTopic<String, OrderCreated> orders =
                driver.createInputTopic(
                        "order.created.v1",
                        new StringSerializer(),
                        orderCreatedSerde.serializer()
                );

        TestInputTopic<String, CustomerProfile> customers =
                driver.createInputTopic(
                        "customer.profile.v1",
                        new StringSerializer(),
                        customerSerde.serializer()
                );

        TestOutputTopic<String, EnrichedOrder> output =
                driver.createOutputTopic(
                        "order.enriched.v1",
                        new StringDeserializer(),
                        enrichedOrderSerde.deserializer()
                );

        customers.pipeInput("customer-456", Fixtures.customerProfile());
        orders.pipeInput("order-123", Fixtures.orderCreated());

        KeyValue<String, EnrichedOrder> result = output.readKeyValue();

        assertThat(result.value.customerSegment()).isEqualTo("PREMIUM");
    }
}
```

Test Kafka Streams:

| Pattern | Test |
|---|---|
| Filter/branch | Input → expected output topic |
| Enrichment | Table input + stream input → enriched output |
| Aggregation | Multiple records → state/output count |
| Windowing | Records with timestamps → windowed result |
| Dedup | Duplicate eventId → single output |
| Materialized state | Query state store |
| Unknown event | Routed to invalid/DLQ stream |

## 28. Contract Test untuk Header dan Key

Schema sering hanya mengecek value. Padahal Kafka key dan headers bagian dari contract.

```java id="key-header-contract-test"
@Test
void orderCreatedKafkaContractShouldUseAggregateIdAsKey() {
    ProducerRecord<String, String> record =
            eventPublisher.toRecord(Fixtures.orderCreatedEvent("order-123"));

    assertThat(record.key()).isEqualTo("order-123");
    assertThat(header(record, "event-id")).isNotBlank();
    assertThat(header(record, "event-type")).isEqualTo("OrderCreated");
    assertThat(header(record, "event-version")).isEqualTo("1");
    assertThat(header(record, "correlation-id")).isNotBlank();
}
```

Contract yang perlu diuji:

| Contract | Test |
|---|---|
| Topic name | Exact expected topic |
| Key | Aggregate id / expected partition key |
| Headers | Required headers exist |
| Event id | UUID/ULID/non-null unique |
| Correlation id | Propagated |
| Tenant id | Present if multi-tenant |
| Content type | Matches serializer |
| Schema subject/id | Present if used |

---

## 29. Replay Test

Replay test membuktikan handler aman saat event lama dibaca ulang.

```text id="replay-test-flow"
Produce historical events
  ↓
Consumer processes projection
  ↓
Reset/re-run same events
  ↓
Projection remains correct
  ↓
No duplicate side effect
```

### Projection replay test

```java id="replay-projection-test"
@Test
void replayShouldRebuildProjectionDeterministically() {
    List<OrderEvent> history = List.of(
            Fixtures.orderCreated("evt-1", "order-123"),
            Fixtures.orderPaid("evt-2", "order-123"),
            Fixtures.orderShipped("evt-3", "order-123")
    );

    replay(history);

    OrderProjection first = projectionRepository.find("order-123");

    projectionRepository.clear();
    processedEventRepository.clear();

    replay(history);

    OrderProjection second = projectionRepository.find("order-123");

    assertThat(second).isEqualTo(first);
}
```

### Side-effect replay guard

```java id="replay-side-effect-test"
@Test
void replayShouldNotSendEmailTwice() {
    OrderCreatedEvent event = Fixtures.orderCreatedEvent("evt-001", "order-123");

    handler.handle(event);
    handler.handle(event); // replay/duplicate

    assertThat(emailGateway.sentEmails()).hasSize(1);
}
```

---

## 30. Failure Injection Test Matrix

| Failure | Test setup | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Kafka broker down | Stop container / wrong bootstrap | Outbox pending grows, no data loss |
| Producer timeout | MockProducer error | Retry/reschedule |
| Serialization error | Bad event object | Non-retryable failure |
| Consumer handler DB timeout | Fake transient exception | Retry topic |
| Poison JSON | Invalid payload | DLQ |
| DLQ publish failure | Fake DLQ producer failure | Main offset not committed |
| Duplicate event | Same eventId twice | One side effect |
| Rebalance | MockConsumer rebalance | Safe offset |
| Shutdown | Stop worker mid-processing | No unsafe commit |
| Schema incompatible | Compatibility test fails | CI fails |
| Authorization error | Fake AuthorizationException | Stop/fail fast |
| Message too large | Large payload integration | Failure classified |

---

## 31. CI/CD Quality Gates

```text id="ci-quality-gates"
Pull request
  ↓
Unit tests
  ↓
Contract tests
  ↓
Schema compatibility
  ↓
Integration tests with Testcontainers
  ↓
Failure scenario tests
  ↓
Build image
  ↓
Deploy to staging
  ↓
Smoke E2E
```

| Gate | Fail if |
|---|---|
| Unit tests | Mapper/handler/producer logic broken |
| Golden event | Contract changed unintentionally |
| Schema compatibility | Breaking schema |
| Header/key contract | Missing required header/key |
| Integration Kafka | Cannot produce/consume real topic |
| Outbox transaction | Outbox not atomic |
| Idempotency | Duplicate creates duplicate side effect |
| Retry/DLQ | Failure not isolated |
| Replay | Projection not deterministic |
| Security config | PLAINTEXT/prod secret leak |
| Performance smoke | Latency/throughput regression beyond threshold |

---

## 32. Test Data Strategy

| Data type | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Event ID | Stable in golden tests, random in property tests |
| Timestamp | Fixed clock |
| Correlation ID | Explicit |
| Aggregate ID | Meaningful: `order-123` |
| Tenant ID | Include multi-tenant cases |
| Payload | Minimal valid + edge cases |
| Invalid payload | Missing required, wrong type, unknown enum |
| Duplicate | Same eventId |
| Out-of-order | Aggregate version gap |
| Large message | p95/p99 payload size |
| Old version | V1 event after V2 consumer |

### Fixed clock

```java id="fixed-clock-test"
Clock fixedClock = Clock.fixed(
        Instant.parse("2026-07-13T10:15:30Z"),
        ZoneOffset.UTC
);
```

---

## 33. Property-Based / Fuzz Testing Ideas

| Property | Example |
|---|---|
| Unknown optional fields ignored | Add random fields to JSON |
| Required fields enforced | Remove required field |
| Duplicate event idempotent | Same event repeated N times |
| Ordering by aggregate version | Shuffle events and detect gap |
| Retry classifier total | Every exception maps to action |
| DLQ redaction | Secret-like fields never appear raw |
| Event mapper never emits null required fields | Generate domain objects |
| Monetary values never use floating point | Validate schema/type |

---

## 34. Test Naming Convention

Use behavior-oriented names:

```text id="test-naming"
shouldPublishOrderCreatedWithAggregateIdAsKey
shouldRollbackOutboxWhenOrderCreationFails
shouldNotCommitOffsetWhenHandlerFails
shouldPublishPoisonMessageToDlq
shouldDeduplicateRepeatedEventId
shouldResumePendingOutboxAfterRelayCrash
shouldCorrelateSagaReplyOnlyOnce
shouldRejectSchemaBreakingChange
```

Avoid vague names:

```text id="bad-test-names"
testKafka
testConsumer
testPublish
testOutbox
```

---

## 35. What Not to Over-Test

| Avoid | Kenapa |
|---|---|
| Testing Kafka internals | Kafka already tested |
| Testing exact partition number with default partitioner | Hash may vary with config/key/partition count |
| Testing timing with arbitrary sleeps | Flaky |
| Full container stack for every unit test | Slow CI |
| Mocking everything in E2E | False confidence |
| Snapshotting every JSON formatting detail | Brittle, unless golden contract intentional |
| Testing one happy path only | Kafka bugs often failure-mode bugs |

Use Awaitility-style polling for async integration tests instead of `Thread.sleep`.

```java id="awaitility-example"
await()
    .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
    .pollInterval(Duration.ofMillis(100))
    .untilAsserted(() ->
            assertThat(repository.exists("order-123")).isTrue()
    );
```

---

## 36. Flaky Test Prevention

| Flake source | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Async Kafka timing | Await with timeout |
| Reusing consumer group | Unique group id per test |
| Reusing topic | Unique topic per test or cleanup |
| Container startup slow | Proper wait strategy |
| Race with consumer assignment | Wait until assigned |
| Clock/time window | Fixed clock |
| Parallel tests sharing Kafka | Isolate topics/groups |
| Sleep-based assertions | Poll/assert until |
| External network | Testcontainers/local only |
| Order assumption across partitions | Key or single partition in test |

### Unique topic helper

```java id="unique-topic-helper"
String topic(String base) {
    return base + "." + UUID.randomUUID();
}
```

### Unique group helper

```java id="unique-group-helper"
String group(String base) {
    return base + "-" + UUID.randomUUID();
}
```

## 38. Production Smoke Tests

Setelah deploy staging/prod, smoke test harus aman dan tidak merusak data.

| Smoke | Cara |
|---|---|
| Producer connectivity | Publish synthetic low-risk event ke test topic |
| Consumer health | Check group assignment/lag |
| Topic access | Admin describe allowed topics |
| Schema access | Validate schema registry reachable |
| Outbox relay | Insert synthetic outbox event in non-business topic |
| DLQ path | Avoid poison in prod main topic; use test topic |
| ksqlDB query | `DESCRIBE` or safe pull query |
| Kafka Streams | Health state RUNNING |

Jangan mengirim poison event ke production business topic hanya untuk smoke test.

---

## 39. Observability Assertions in Tests

Testing tidak harus hanya data result. Pastikan metric/log penting terisi.

| Behavior | Assertion |
|---|---|
| Publish success | Metric `records_sent_total` increment |
| Publish failure | Failure metric/log contains eventId |
| Consumer success | Processing metric increment |
| DLQ | DLQ metric increment |
| Duplicate | Duplicate metric increment |
| Retry | Retry metric with error class |
| Correlation failure | Bridge DLQ/metric |
| Outbox delay | pending age visible |
| Shutdown | log graceful stop |

---

## 40. Common Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Dampak |
|---|---|
| Hanya test happy path | Failure model tidak terbukti |
| Semua test pakai real Kafka | CI lambat/flaky |
| Tidak ada real Kafka test sama sekali | Config/protocol bug lolos |
| Producer wrapper tidak injectable | Sulit MockProducer |
| Consumer handler menerima `ConsumerRecord` langsung | Domain test sulit |
| Auto commit di test | Offset correctness tidak terlihat |
| `Thread.sleep` untuk async assertion | Flaky |
| Reuse group id antar test | Offset saling ganggu |
| Tidak test duplicate event | Side effect double di prod |
| Tidak test DLQ publish failure | Bisa commit offset sebelum DLQ aman |
| Tidak test rollback outbox | Event bisa publish untuk state yang rollback |
| Golden event tidak ada | Contract berubah diam-diam |
| Schema auto-register di test tapi prod false | Environment mismatch |
| Tidak test replay | Projection recovery risk |
| Tidak sanitize logs in test | Secret/PII bisa bocor |

## 41. Production Readiness Checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| Unit tests | Mapper, producer wrapper, handler, classifier |
| Contract tests | Schema, golden event, key/header |
| Consumer tests | Idempotency, offset, retry, DLQ |
| Outbox tests | Transaction atomicity, relay, duplicate |
| Integration tests | Kafka + PostgreSQL container |

| Saga tests | Correlation, timeout, compensation |
| Failure tests | Broker down, poison, retry, shutdown |

| Flake control | Unique topics/groups, await not sleep |
| Observability | Metrics/log assertions |

## 42. Quick Decision Guide

```text id="testing-quick-guide"
Need to test topic/key/header?
  → MockProducer unit test

Need to test handler business logic?
  → Pure unit test without Kafka

Need to test poll loop/offset?
  → MockConsumer component test

Need to test real Kafka config?
  → Testcontainers Kafka integration test

Need to test DB + Kafka consistency?
  → PostgreSQL + Kafka Testcontainers

Need to test Kafka Streams topology?
  → TopologyTestDriver

Need to test event contract?
  → Golden event + schema compatibility

Need to test duplicate/replay?
  → Produce same eventId / replay history

Need to test failure handling?
  → Inject exception and assert retry/DLQ/no unsafe commit
```

## 43. Ringkasan Praktis

Testing strategy yang sehat untuk Kafka-based Java/Jersey microservice:

```text id="testing-summary"
Producer:
  mapper test
  golden event
  MockProducer
  real Kafka smoke

Consumer:
  pure handler test
  idempotency test
  MockConsumer poll/offset test
  real Kafka + DB integration

Outbox:
  transaction rollback test
  relay success/failure test
  duplicate publish test

EDA:
  retry/DLQ test
  replay test
  saga correlation/timeout/compensation test

Governance:
  schema compatibility
  key/header contract
  CI quality gate
```

Invariant utama:

```text id="testing-invariants"
Every Kafka feature must prove:
  - correct contract
  - correct key/header
  - correct success behavior
  - correct failure behavior
  - no unsafe offset commit
  - idempotency under duplicate
  - replay safety when applicable
  - observability evidence exists
```

# Cheatsheet - Kafka Deployment & Kubernetes Operations dalam Java/Jersey Microservice

## 1. Core Mental Model

Deployment Kafka client di Kubernetes bukan hanya “pod jalan”. Untuk Java/Jersey microservice yang memakai Kafka, deployment harus memastikan:

```text id="kafka-k8s-core-model"
Container starts
  ↓
Config + secrets loaded
  ↓
Kafka producer/consumer/admin initialized
  ↓
Required topics/schema/dependencies validated
  ↓
Readiness becomes UP
  ↓
Pod joins consumer group / starts publishing
  ↓
Rolling deployment happens safely
  ↓
Pod receives SIGTERM
  ↓
Stop accepting traffic
  ↓
Stop polling / stop claiming work
  ↓
Finish or safely abort in-flight records
  ↓
Commit only safe offsets
  ↓
Close producer/consumer/admin
  ↓
Pod exits before termination grace expires
```

Kubernetes memiliki **liveness, readiness, dan startup probes** untuk membedakan apakah container hidup, siap menerima traffic, atau masih dalam fase startup; jika startup probe didefinisikan, liveness dan readiness tidak dijalankan sampai startup probe berhasil. ([Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/probes/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 2. Deployment Concern Map
