# Cheatsheet - Kafka Connect & Debezium Deep Dive  
## Source/Sink Connector, PostgreSQL CDC, Outbox Event Router, Monitoring, Failure Recovery

## Status seri

Ini adalah **Seri 2 dari 4 seri tersisa**.

Setelah seri ini, sisa:

| Sisa | Seri |
|---:|---|
| 2 | Kafka Runbook & Incident Response Playbook |
| 1 | Final Integration Blueprint |

---

## 1. Core Mental Model

Kafka Connect adalah runtime untuk memindahkan data **ke Kafka** atau **dari Kafka** tanpa menulis producer/consumer custom dari nol. Confluent mendeskripsikan Kafka Connect sebagai tool untuk streaming data secara scalable dan reliable antara Kafka dan sistem lain; source connector membawa data masuk ke Kafka, sedangkan sink connector membawa data keluar dari Kafka ke sistem target. Kafka Connect distributed mode menyimpan config, offset, dan status task di Kafka internal topics sehingga worker bisa scalable dan fault-tolerant. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/connect/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```text id="connect-core-model"
External system / Database
  ↓
Source Connector
  ↓
Kafka Connect Worker
  ↓
Kafka Topic
  ↓
Sink Connector / Java Consumer / Streams / ksqlDB
  ↓
Target system
```

Untuk stack Anda, Kafka Connect paling penting untuk:

```text id="connect-use-cases"
1. PostgreSQL CDC dengan Debezium
2. Transactional Outbox → Kafka event
3. Sink ke Elasticsearch/OpenSearch/Data Warehouse/Search Index
4. Sink/source integration ke legacy system
5. Data replication antar platform
6. Audit/event pipeline tanpa menambah logic di Jersey service
```

---

## 2. Kafka Connect Decomposition

```text id="connect-decomposition"
Kafka Connect
│
├── Worker
│   ├── standalone mode
│   ├── distributed mode
│   ├── plugin.path
│   ├── converters
│   ├── internal topics
│   └── REST API
│
├── Connector
│   ├── source connector
│   ├── sink connector
│   ├── connector config
│   └── connector lifecycle
│
├── Task
│   ├── unit of parallel work
│   ├── assigned to workers
│   ├── can fail independently
│   └── has status
│
├── Transform
│   ├── SMT / Single Message Transform
│   ├── route topic
│   ├── unwrap envelope
│   ├── mask/drop fields
│   └── outbox router
│
├── Converter
│   ├── JSON
│   ├── Avro
│   ├── Protobuf
│   ├── String
│   └── ByteArray
│
├── Storage
│   ├── config.storage.topic
│   ├── offset.storage.topic
│   ├── status.storage.topic
│   └── connector-specific offsets
│
└── Operations
    ├── deploy connector
    ├── pause/resume/restart
    ├── monitor task status
    ├── inspect lag
    ├── handle failure
    └── upgrade safely
```

---

## 3. Source vs Sink Connector

| Connector type | Direction | Example | Use case |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source connector | External system → Kafka | Debezium PostgreSQL | CDC dari PostgreSQL ke Kafka |
| Sink connector | Kafka → External system | JDBC Sink, Elasticsearch Sink | Projection/indexing dari Kafka |
| Source CDC | DB log → Kafka | Debezium | Capture committed changes |
| Sink batch-ish | Kafka → file/lake/search | S3/HDFS/OpenSearch | Analytics/search |
| Custom connector | Either | Internal legacy connector | Saat connector siap pakai tidak cukup |

```text id="source-sink-flow"
Source:
  PostgreSQL WAL → Debezium → Kafka topic

Sink:
  Kafka topic → Sink Connector → Search index / warehouse / DB
```

---

## 4. Worker Mode: Standalone vs Distributed

| Mode | Cocok untuk | Jangan untuk |
|---|---|---|
| Standalone | Local dev, simple test, single process | Production HA |
| Distributed | Production, staging, scalable runtime | Very small one-off local test |

Kafka Connect distributed mode menyimpan **offsets**, **configs**, dan **task statuses** di Kafka topics. Dokumentasi Apache Kafka merekomendasikan membuat internal topics tersebut secara manual agar partition count, replication factor, dan cleanup policy sesuai kebutuhan; jika tidak, topic dapat auto-created dengan default yang tidak cocok. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/37/kafka-connect/user-guide/))

### Distributed mode internal topics

| Topic | Fungsi | Config penting |
|---|---|---|
| `config.storage.topic` | Connector/task config | Single partition, compacted, replicated |
| `offset.storage.topic` | Source connector offsets | Many partitions, compacted, replicated |
| `status.storage.topic` | Connector/task status | Multiple partitions, compacted, replicated |

Apache Kafka docs menyebut `config.storage.topic` sebaiknya single partition, highly replicated, compacted; `offset.storage.topic` sebaiknya banyak partition, replicated, compacted; dan `status.storage.topic` dapat multiple partitions serta replicated/compacted. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/37/kafka-connect/user-guide/))

---

## 5. Kafka Connect Worker Config

### Production-ish distributed worker config

```properties id="connect-distributed-worker"
bootstrap.servers=kafka-1:9093,kafka-2:9093,kafka-3:9093

group.id=connect-cluster-prod

config.storage.topic=connect-prod-configs
offset.storage.topic=connect-prod-offsets
status.storage.topic=connect-prod-status

config.storage.replication.factor=3
offset.storage.replication.factor=3
status.storage.replication.factor=3

key.converter=org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter
value.converter=org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter
key.converter.schemas.enable=false
value.converter.schemas.enable=false

plugin.path=/opt/kafka/plugins

rest.port=8083
```

Confluent worker config reference mencatat replication factor internal topic offset/status sebaiknya minimal 3 untuk production, tidak boleh lebih besar dari jumlah broker. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/connect/references/allconfigs.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Jika pakai Avro + Schema Registry

```properties id="connect-avro-worker"
key.converter=io.confluent.connect.avro.AvroConverter
key.converter.schema.registry.url=http://schema-registry:8081

value.converter=io.confluent.connect.avro.AvroConverter
value.converter.schema.registry.url=http://schema-registry:8081
```

### Jika pakai JSON tanpa schema

```properties id="connect-json-worker"
key.converter=org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter
key.converter.schemas.enable=false

value.converter=org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter
value.converter.schemas.enable=false
```

---

## 6. Kafka Connect REST API

Kafka Connect distributed mode dikelola lewat REST API. Confluent REST API docs mencakup endpoint untuk membaca connector config, membuat/mengubah config dengan `PUT /connectors/{name}/config`, membaca status dengan `GET /connectors/{name}/status`, serta stop/pause/resume/restart lifecycle connector. Endpoint update config dapat mengembalikan `409 Conflict` jika rebalance sedang berjalan. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/connect/references/restapi.html))

### Common commands

```bash id="connect-rest-commands"
# List connectors
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors

# Get connector config
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/order-outbox-postgres/config | jq

# Get connector status
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/order-outbox-postgres/status | jq

# Create or update connector config
curl -X PUT http://connect:8083/connectors/order-outbox-postgres/config \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @connector-order-outbox.json

# Pause connector
curl -X PUT http://connect:8083/connectors/order-outbox-postgres/pause

# Resume connector
curl -X PUT http://connect:8083/connectors/order-outbox-postgres/resume

# Restart connector
curl -X POST http://connect:8083/connectors/order-outbox-postgres/restart
```

### Status response yang perlu dilihat

```json id="connect-status-example"
{
  "name": "order-outbox-postgres",
  "connector": {
    "state": "RUNNING",
    "worker_id": "connect-1:8083"
  },
  "tasks": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "state": "RUNNING",
      "worker_id": "connect-2:8083"
    }
  ],
  "type": "source"
}
```

---

## 7. Debezium Mental Model

Debezium adalah CDC platform open-source. Debezium homepage saat ini menampilkan **latest stable 3.6** dan menjelaskan Debezium sebagai platform CDC yang memonitor database, lalu membuat aplikasi dapat bereaksi terhadap insert, update, dan delete yang sudah di-commit. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/))

```text id="debezium-core"
PostgreSQL write transaction
  ↓
WAL / logical decoding
  ↓
Debezium PostgreSQL connector
  ↓
Kafka Connect source task
  ↓
Kafka topic
  ↓
Java consumer / Streams / ksqlDB / sink connector
```

Debezium PostgreSQL connector menangkap row-level changes untuk table PostgreSQL. Pertama kali connect, connector melakukan consistent snapshot; setelah snapshot selesai, connector terus menangkap row-level insert/update/delete yang sudah committed dan mengirim change event records ke Kafka topics. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 8. Debezium PostgreSQL: Logical Decoding & Replication Slot

PostgreSQL logical decoding memungkinkan perubahan yang committed di transaction log diekstrak dan diproses melalui output plugin. Debezium PostgreSQL connector biasanya memakai `pgoutput`, plugin logical decoding standar PostgreSQL 10+ yang tidak memerlukan library tambahan. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```text id="logical-decoding-flow"
PostgreSQL transaction commit
  ↓
WAL entry
  ↓
logical decoding plugin: pgoutput
  ↓
replication slot
  ↓
Debezium connector
  ↓
Kafka topic
```

PostgreSQL documentation menjelaskan replication slot merepresentasikan stream perubahan yang dapat direplay ke client dalam urutan perubahan dibuat di origin server. Debezium docs juga menekankan replication slot akan menahan WAL segment yang dibutuhkan Debezium saat outage, sehingga replication slot harus dimonitor agar tidak menyebabkan disk consumption berlebihan atau catalog bloat jika slot tidak dipakai terlalu lama. ([PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logicaldecoding-explanation.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 9. PostgreSQL Prerequisites

### PostgreSQL config

```properties id="postgres-logical-config"
wal_level=logical
max_wal_senders=10
max_replication_slots=10
```

Debezium docs menyebut parameter seperti `max_wal_senders` dan `max_replication_slots` perlu disesuaikan jika ada beberapa connector yang mengakses server secara concurrency. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/1.9/connectors/postgresql.html))

### Replication user

```sql id="debezium-user-sql"
CREATE USER debezium WITH PASSWORD 'change-me' REPLICATION;

GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE orders TO debezium;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO debezium;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO debezium;

ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public
GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO debezium;
```

Debezium docs merekomendasikan membuat user khusus Debezium dengan privilege spesifik, bukan memberi superuser privilege, karena superuser meningkatkan risiko akses data yang berlebihan. Untuk PostgreSQL connector, user harus memiliki privileges yang diperlukan untuk replication, publication, dan SELECT pada table yang disnapshot. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 10. Debezium PostgreSQL Connector Config - Table CDC

Contoh connector untuk CDC table biasa:

```json id="debezium-postgres-basic-config"
{
  "name": "order-service-postgres-cdc",
  "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
  "tasks.max": "1",

  "database.hostname": "postgres",
  "database.port": "5432",
  "database.user": "debezium",
  "database.password": "${file:/opt/connect/secrets/postgres.properties:password}",
  "database.dbname": "orders",

  "topic.prefix": "orderdb",
  "plugin.name": "pgoutput",
  "slot.name": "order_service_debezium_slot",
  "publication.name": "order_service_publication",

  "schema.include.list": "public",
  "table.include.list": "public.orders,public.order_item",

  "snapshot.mode": "initial",

  "key.converter": "org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter",
  "key.converter.schemas.enable": "false",
  "value.converter": "org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter",
  "value.converter.schemas.enable": "false"
}
```

Debezium connector config requires `connector.class`, database host/port/user/password/dbname, `topic.prefix`, and include/exclude lists can restrict what schema/table is monitored. Debezium writes one connector task that connects to PostgreSQL, reads transaction log, and streams change records to Kafka. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 11. Default Debezium Topic Naming

Default topic naming kira-kira:

```text id="debezium-default-topic"
<topic.prefix>.<schema>.<table>
```

Contoh:

```text id="debezium-topic-examples"
orderdb.public.orders
orderdb.public.order_item
orderdb.public.customer
```

Debezium docs memberikan contoh topic seperti `fulfillment.inventory.products` atau `fulfillment.public.products`, mengikuti `topic.prefix`, schema, dan table. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Kapan pakai raw table topic?

| Use case | Cocok? |
|---|---:|
| Rebuild search index dari table | Ya |
| Data replication ke warehouse | Ya |
| Cache invalidation by table | Ya |
| Business integration event publik | Biasanya tidak |
| Domain event untuk service lain | Lebih baik outbox |
| Saga event | Lebih baik outbox/event contract |

---

## 12. Raw CDC vs Outbox Event

| Aspek | Raw table CDC | Outbox Event Router |
|---|---|---|
| Source | Table business langsung | `outbox_event` table |
| Event semantic | Row changed | Business event |
| Topic name | DB/schema/table-based | Domain/event-based |
| Payload | Debezium before/after envelope | Event payload |
| Consumer coupling | Coupled ke DB schema | Coupled ke event contract |
| Cocok untuk | Replication, indexing, analytics | Microservice integration event |
| Risiko | Leaking internal DB model | Butuh outbox discipline |
| Ordering | Per table/key | Per aggregate key |

Rule praktis:

```text id="raw-vs-outbox-rule"
Gunakan raw CDC untuk data replication/search/indexing.

Gunakan outbox untuk business integration event antar microservice.
```

---

## 13. Debezium Outbox Event Router

Debezium Outbox Event Router adalah Single Message Transform untuk menerapkan transactional outbox pattern. Debezium docs menjelaskan default outbox table memiliki kolom `id`, `aggregatetype`, `aggregateid`, `type`, dan `payload`; `id` menjadi event ID header, `aggregatetype` dipakai routing topic, `aggregateid` menjadi Kafka message key untuk menjaga ordering, dan `payload` menjadi message value. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html))

### Default outbox table

```sql id="outbox-table-debezium"
CREATE TABLE outbox_event (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    aggregatetype VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    aggregateid VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    type VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    payload JSONB,
    timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    traceid TEXT,
    correlationid TEXT,
    tenantid TEXT
);
```

### Why this shape?

| Column | Function |
|---|---|
| `id` | Unique event ID; useful for dedup |
| `aggregatetype` | Routing dimension / topic suffix |
| `aggregateid` | Kafka message key |
| `type` | Event type |
| `payload` | Business payload |
| `timestamp` | Event timestamp |
| `traceid` | Observability |
| `correlationid` | End-to-end correlation |
| `tenantid` | Multi-tenant boundary |

Debezium docs also note additional custom columns can be added to outbox events either into payload or as Kafka message headers. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html))

---

## 14. Outbox Event Router Config

```json id="debezium-outbox-router-config"
{
  "name": "order-outbox-postgres",
  "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
  "tasks.max": "1",

  "database.hostname": "postgres",
  "database.port": "5432",
  "database.user": "debezium",
  "database.password": "${file:/opt/connect/secrets/postgres.properties:password}",
  "database.dbname": "orders",

  "topic.prefix": "orderdb",
  "plugin.name": "pgoutput",
  "slot.name": "order_outbox_slot",
  "publication.name": "order_outbox_publication",

  "table.include.list": "public.outbox_event",
  "snapshot.mode": "initial",

  "transforms": "outbox",
  "transforms.outbox.type": "io.debezium.transforms.outbox.EventRouter",

  "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.id": "id",
  "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.key": "aggregateid",
  "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.payload": "payload",
  "transforms.outbox.route.by.field": "aggregatetype",
  "transforms.outbox.route.topic.replacement": "${routedByValue}.events.v1",

  "transforms.outbox.table.fields.additional.placement": "type:header:eventType,traceid:header:traceId,correlationid:header:correlationId,tenantid:header:tenantId",

  "key.converter": "org.apache.kafka.connect.storage.StringConverter",
  "value.converter": "org.apache.kafka.connect.json.JsonConverter",
  "value.converter.schemas.enable": "false"
}
```

Debezium docs recommend applying the Outbox Event Router SMT selectively, because Debezium connectors may also emit heartbeat, tombstone, metadata, transaction, or schema change messages with a different structure from outbox events. You can use predicates or `route.topic.regex` so the SMT only processes intended outbox table changes. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html))

---

## 15. Topic Output Example

Jika `aggregatetype = order.order`, maka config:

```text id="outbox-topic-route"
route.topic.replacement = ${routedByValue}.events.v1
```

menghasilkan:

```text id="outbox-topic-result"
order.order.events.v1
```

Event:

```json id="outbox-row-example"
{
  "id": "3d9fb047-4956-4c70-9b01-c25a4423de54",
  "aggregatetype": "order.order",
  "aggregateid": "order-123",
  "type": "OrderCreated",
  "payload": {
    "orderId": "order-123",
    "customerId": "customer-456",
    "status": "CREATED"
  },
  "traceid": "trace-abc",
  "correlationid": "corr-123",
  "tenantid": "tenant-a"
}
```

Kafka output:

```text id="outbox-kafka-output"
topic: order.order.events.v1
key: order-123
headers:
  id=3d9fb047-4956-4c70-9b01-c25a4423de54
  eventType=OrderCreated
  traceId=trace-abc
  correlationId=corr-123
  tenantId=tenant-a
value:
  {
    "orderId": "order-123",
    "customerId": "customer-456",
    "status": "CREATED"
  }
```

Debezium docs explicitly state that the SMT uses the configured event key column as the emitted Kafka message key, important for maintaining correct order in Kafka partitions. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html))

---

## 16. Outbox Write Path di Java/Jersey

```text id="jersey-outbox-cdc-flow"
POST /orders
  ↓
Jersey Resource
  ↓
Application Service
  ↓
PostgreSQL transaction:
  - insert/update business table
  - insert outbox_event row
  ↓
commit
  ↓
Debezium reads WAL
  ↓
Outbox Event Router emits Kafka event
```

### Application service sketch

```java id="java-outbox-cdc-service"
public OrderId createOrder(CreateOrderCommand command, RequestContext ctx) {
    return transaction.inTransaction(() -> {
        Order order = Order.create(command.customerId(), command.items());

        orderRepository.insert(order);

        OutboxEvent event = OutboxEvent.builder()
                .id(UUID.randomUUID())
                .aggregateType("order.order")
                .aggregateId(order.id().value())
                .type("OrderCreated")
                .payload(objectMapper.valueToTree(Map.of(
                        "orderId", order.id().value(),
                        "customerId", order.customerId().value(),
                        "status", order.status().name()
                )))
                .traceId(ctx.traceId())
                .correlationId(ctx.correlationId())
                .tenantId(ctx.tenantId())
                .build();

        outboxRepository.insert(event);

        return order.id();
    });
}
```

### MyBatis mapper insert

```xml id="mybatis-outbox-insert"
<insert id="insertOutboxEvent">
  INSERT INTO outbox_event (
      id,
      aggregatetype,
      aggregateid,
      type,
      payload,
      traceid,
      correlationid,
      tenantid,
      timestamp
  )
  VALUES (
      #{id},
      #{aggregateType},
      #{aggregateId},
      #{type},
      CAST(#{payloadJson} AS jsonb),
      #{traceId},
      #{correlationId},
      #{tenantId},
      now()
  )
</insert>
```

---

## 17. Outbox Table Discipline

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Insert-only outbox | Outbox event should be immutable |
| No UPDATE payload | Avoid changing already-emitted meaning |
| Stable `id` | Consumer dedup |
| Stable `aggregateid` | Partition ordering |
| `payload` already contract-shaped | Avoid exposing DB schema |
| No secret/PII unless approved | Kafka retains/replays |
| Include correlation metadata | Debugging |
| Cleanup strategy needed | Table growth |

Debezium Outbox docs mention `table.op.invalid.behavior` controls behavior when an `UPDATE` happens on outbox table. In practice, update on outbox event is usually a smell because event should be immutable after insert. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html))

---

## 18. Cleanup Outbox Table

Karena Debezium reads WAL, bukan polling status column, outbox row bisa dibersihkan setelah aman.

### Simple cleanup

```sql id="outbox-cleanup-simple"
DELETE FROM outbox_event
WHERE timestamp < now() - interval '7 days';
```

### Safer cleanup with partitioning

```sql id="outbox-partitioned-cleanup"
-- Use time-based partitions:
-- outbox_event_2026_07_13
-- outbox_event_2026_07_14

DROP TABLE outbox_event_2026_07_01;
```

### Cleanup caution

| Concern | Guidance |
|---|---|
| Delete too early | Debug/audit harder |
| Long retention | Table bloat |
| Partitioning | Better for high-volume outbox |
| Audit requirement | Archive before delete |
| Debezium lag | Do not delete before connector captured row |

---

## 19. Snapshot Modes

Debezium PostgreSQL connector performs an initial snapshot because PostgreSQL WAL usually does not retain all database history. After the snapshot, it streams changes from the point where snapshot was taken. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

| Snapshot mode idea | Use |
|---|---|
| `initial` | First connector start; snapshot existing data |
| `no_data` / schema-only style | Start streaming from current point without existing rows |
| Never snapshot business table for pure outbox? | Often acceptable if outbox only needs new events |
| Re-snapshot | Recovery/migration with caution |

Practical guidance:

```text id="snapshot-guidance"
For raw table CDC:
  initial snapshot often needed.

For outbox event table:
  initial snapshot can emit old outbox rows if present.
  clean/empty table or choose snapshot behavior intentionally.
```

---

## 20. Connector Offsets & LSN

Debezium PostgreSQL connector stores its progress as PostgreSQL LSN offset. On restart, it continues streaming from that offset as long as replication slot remains intact; Debezium docs warn never to drop the replication slot on primary server or you lose the ability to resume safely from that stored position. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```text id="lsn-model"
Kafka Connect offset topic
  stores Debezium source offset
  includes PostgreSQL LSN

PostgreSQL replication slot
  retains WAL needed from that LSN

Connector restart:
  reads stored offset
  asks PostgreSQL slot for changes from there
```

### Offset safety rule

```text id="connect-offset-rule"
Do not delete Connect offset topic.
Do not drop Debezium replication slot casually.
Do not rename connector without migration plan.
```

---

## 21. Connector Name, Slot Name, Publication Name

| Name | Scope | Why important |
|---|---|---|
| Connector name | Kafka Connect cluster | REST lifecycle, config, status |
| `slot.name` | PostgreSQL primary | WAL retention / resume point |
| `publication.name` | PostgreSQL logical replication | Tables included in replication |
| `topic.prefix` | Kafka topics | Namespace for CDC topics |
| Connect `group.id` | Connect worker cluster | Worker membership |
| Internal topics | Kafka Connect cluster | Config/offset/status durability |

### Naming convention

```text id="connector-naming-convention"
<env>.<domain>.<service>.<purpose>.cdc
```

Example:

```text id="connector-naming-examples"
prod.order.order-service.outbox.cdc
staging.order.order-service.outbox.cdc
dev.order.alice.order-service.outbox.cdc
```

---

## 22. Single Message Transforms / SMT

SMT = transform per record di Kafka Connect.

| SMT use case | Example |
|---|---|
| Route topic | Outbox EventRouter |
| Extract payload | Debezium unwrap |
| Mask field | Hide sensitive column |
| Drop field | Remove internal metadata |
| Add header | Put event type/correlation |
| Rename field | Normalize contract |
| Filter | Keep only relevant records |

### SMT caution

```text id="smt-caution"
SMT is good for lightweight routing/shape changes.

Do not put heavy business logic in SMT.
Do not hide critical semantic transformation in connector config only.
```

---

## 23. Debezium Envelope vs Unwrapped Event

Raw Debezium CDC event usually contains metadata/envelope such as before/after/op/source. For business event consumers, this is often too database-centric.

| Format | Use case |
|---|---|
| Full Debezium envelope | Audit/debug/CDC consumers |
| Unwrapped row | Simple table replication |
| Outbox routed payload | Microservice integration event |
| Custom transformed event | Carefully governed |

### Raw CDC consumer smell

```text id="raw-cdc-smell"
Billing service consumes:
  orderdb.public.orders
  and reads "after.status"

Problem:
  billing now depends on order DB schema.
```

Better:

```text id="outbox-better"
Billing service consumes:
  order.order.events.v1
  eventType = OrderCreated / OrderConfirmed

Benefit:
  billing depends on integration event contract,
  not order table structure.
```

---

## 24. Error Handling in Kafka Connect

Connector failure bisa terjadi di beberapa layer.

| Failure | Signal | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Connector config invalid | Connector fails to start | Fix config |
| DB unavailable | Task FAILED / retrying | Check DB/network/credentials |
| Replication slot issue | WAL/slot error | DBA + connector recovery |
| Kafka unavailable | Connect task/backpressure | Platform incident |
| Serialization/converter error | Task failure / DLQ if configured | Fix converter/schema |
| SMT error | Task failure | Fix transform/config |
| Authorization error | Cannot write topic/internal topic | Fix ACL |
| Topic missing | Auto-create disabled | Provision topic |
| Plugin missing | Connector class not found | Fix image/plugin.path |

### Connector status triage

```bash id="connector-status-triage"
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/order-outbox-postgres/status | jq
```

Look for:

```text id="connector-status-fields"
connector.state
connector.worker_id
tasks[].state
tasks[].trace
tasks[].worker_id
```

---

## 25. Dead Letter Queue in Connect

Kafka Connect supports error handling configs for some converter/SMT/connector errors depending on connector behavior. DLQ is commonly configured for sink connectors and some transform/conversion cases.

```properties id="connect-dlq-config"
errors.tolerance=all
errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name=connect-order-sink-dlq.v1
errors.deadletterqueue.context.headers.enable=true
errors.log.enable=true
errors.log.include.messages=false
```

### Use carefully

| Config | Caution |
|---|---|
| `errors.tolerance=all` | Can hide data loss if no alert |
| DLQ topic | Must be monitored |
| Include messages | May leak PII |
| Context headers | Useful for debugging |
| Sink DLQ | Common |
| Source CDC DLQ | Be cautious; failed source records may stop connector depending error |

Rule:

```text id="connect-dlq-rule"
Never enable tolerant errors without:
  - DLQ topic
  - alert
  - owner
  - replay/triage process
```

---

## 26. Monitoring Kafka Connect

### Connect-level metrics

| Metric | Why |
|---|---|
| Worker alive | Runtime availability |
| Connector state | RUNNING/FAILED/PAUSED |
| Task state | Task-level failure |
| Task restart count | Flapping |
| Source record poll rate | CDC activity |
| Source record write rate | Kafka output |
| Offset commit success/failure | Progress |
| Error count | Converter/SMT/connector errors |
| DLQ count | Data issues |
| REST API availability | Ops control |

### Debezium PostgreSQL metrics

| Metric | Why |
|---|---|
| Snapshot running/completed | Initial load status |
| Streaming lag | CDC delay |
| Last event time | Staleness |
| Number of events | Throughput |
| Replication slot retained WAL | Disk risk |
| Connector task failed | Pipeline stopped |
| Queue size | Backpressure |
| LSN progress | CDC progress |
| Heartbeat events | Slot/WAL progress |

Debezium PostgreSQL docs include dedicated monitoring sections for snapshot metrics and streaming metrics, and Debezium installation docs mention monitoring via JMX metrics from Kafka and Kafka Connect. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 27. PostgreSQL Monitoring for Debezium

### Replication slot query

```sql id="pg-replication-slot-monitoring"
SELECT
    slot_name,
    plugin,
    slot_type,
    database,
    active,
    restart_lsn,
    confirmed_flush_lsn,
    pg_size_pretty(
        pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)
    ) AS retained_wal
FROM pg_replication_slots
WHERE slot_type = 'logical';
```

### Publication check

```sql id="pg-publication-check"
SELECT pubname, puballtables, pubinsert, pubupdate, pubdelete, pubtruncate
FROM pg_publication;
```

### Replication activity

```sql id="pg-replication-activity"
SELECT
    pid,
    usename,
    application_name,
    client_addr,
    state,
    sent_lsn,
    write_lsn,
    flush_lsn,
    replay_lsn
FROM pg_stat_replication;
```

Important: replication slot retaining WAL is expected, but **retained WAL growing unbounded** means Debezium/Connect is down, slow, or blocked.

---

## 28. Heartbeat

Heartbeat membantu memastikan connector tetap mengirim activity sehingga offsets/LSN dapat maju even saat table changes jarang.

```json id="debezium-heartbeat-config"
{
  "heartbeat.interval.ms": "10000",
  "heartbeat.action.query": "INSERT INTO debezium_heartbeat(ts) VALUES (now())"
}
```

Debezium docs warn replication slots retain WAL needed by Debezium even during outages, so slots must be monitored to avoid disk growth. Heartbeat is commonly used as part of slot/WAL hygiene when traffic is low, though exact behavior depends on connector configuration and database activity. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/1.9/connectors/postgresql.html))

---

## 29. Deployment on Kubernetes

```text id="connect-k8s"
KafkaConnect Deployment / StatefulSet
  ↓
plugin image contains connector jars
  ↓
worker config via ConfigMap/Secret
  ↓
connect REST exposed internally
  ↓
connector config applied via GitOps/operator/API
```

### Container image principle

| Approach | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Mount plugin jar manually | OK for dev |
| Bake plugin into image | Better for staging/prod |
| Use random internet image | Avoid |
| Use tested internal base image | Best |
| Use Debezium example image in prod | Validate security; docs caution test/eval images |

Debezium PostgreSQL docs state connector plugin must be installed into Kafka Connect `plugin.path`, and if using immutable containers, Debezium has container images with PostgreSQL connector installed, but the docs caution that quay.io Debezium images are for testing/evaluation and not intended for production without proper vendor/security validation. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 30. Kubernetes Config Example

```yaml id="kafka-connect-deployment"
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: kafka-connect
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: kafka-connect
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: kafka-connect
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: connect
          image: registry.example.com/platform/kafka-connect-debezium:3.6.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8083
          env:
            - name: BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS
              value: kafka-1:9093,kafka-2:9093,kafka-3:9093
            - name: GROUP_ID
              value: connect-prod
            - name: CONFIG_STORAGE_TOPIC
              value: connect-prod-configs
            - name: OFFSET_STORAGE_TOPIC
              value: connect-prod-offsets
            - name: STATUS_STORAGE_TOPIC
              value: connect-prod-status
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: kafka-connect-secrets
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /connectors
              port: 8083
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: 8083
            periodSeconds: 20
```

## 31. Connector Deployment as Code

Jangan create connector manual di production tanpa version control.

```text id="connector-as-code"
connector-order-outbox.json
  ↓
PR review
  ↓
CI config validation
  ↓
staging apply
  ↓
prod apply
  ↓
monitor connector status
```

### Connector manifest

```json id="connector-manifest-prod"
{
  "name": "prod.order.order-service.outbox.cdc",
  "config": {
    "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
    "tasks.max": "1",
    "database.hostname": "orders-postgres.internal",
    "database.port": "5432",
    "database.user": "debezium_order",
    "database.password": "${file:/opt/connect/secrets/orders.properties:password}",
    "database.dbname": "orders",
    "topic.prefix": "orderdb",
    "plugin.name": "pgoutput",
    "slot.name": "prod_order_outbox_slot",
    "publication.name": "prod_order_outbox_publication",
    "table.include.list": "public.outbox_event",
    "snapshot.mode": "initial",
    "transforms": "outbox",
    "transforms.outbox.type": "io.debezium.transforms.outbox.EventRouter",
    "transforms.outbox.route.by.field": "aggregatetype",
    "transforms.outbox.route.topic.replacement": "${routedByValue}.events.v1",
    "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.key": "aggregateid",
    "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.payload": "payload",
    "transforms.outbox.table.fields.additional.placement": "type:header:eventType,correlationid:header:correlationId,tenantid:header:tenantId"
  }
}
```

---

## 32. Source Connector Parallelism

Debezium PostgreSQL connector for one database stream is typically constrained by the single ordered database log stream. `tasks.max` often remains `1` for a single PostgreSQL connector because WAL order and source offset are sequential.

```text id="debezium-task-parallelism"
PostgreSQL WAL stream
  ↓
one ordered logical replication stream
  ↓
Debezium source task
  ↓
Kafka topics
```

| Need more throughput? | Consider |
|---|---|
| Connector slow | Check DB/WAL/network/Kafka/serialization |
| Many tables | Include only needed tables |
| Huge snapshot | Incremental snapshot strategy / staging |
| One connector too broad | Split by database/schema where safe |
| Outbox high volume | Partition topic by aggregate key; tune Connect/Kafka |
| Kafka write slow | Broker/topic capacity |

---

## 33. Sink Connector Notes

Sink connector reads Kafka topics and writes to target system.

```text id="sink-model"
Kafka topic
  ↓
Kafka Connect Sink Task
  ↓
Target system
```

| Sink concern | Risk |
|---|---|
| At-least-once delivery | Target must be idempotent/upsert-capable |
| Offset commit after write | Duplicate possible on crash |
| Bad target schema | Task failure/DLQ |
| Target slow | Consumer lag |
| Ordering | Per partition only |
| Delete/tombstone handling | Must be configured intentionally |
| Primary key mapping | Critical for upsert |

For PostgreSQL/JDBC sink use cases, prefer idempotent upserts keyed by event/entity ID rather than blind inserts unless append-only audit is intended.

---

## 34. Security

| Layer | Control |
|---|---|
| Connect worker → Kafka | SASL_SSL / SSL / ACL |
| Connector → PostgreSQL | Dedicated DB user, TLS, least privilege |
| Connect REST API | Internal-only, auth protected |
| Secrets | FileConfigProvider / secret manager / mounted secret |
| Connector config | Avoid plaintext secrets in repo |
| DLQ | Restricted ACL |
| Outbox payload | Data classification |
| Plugin image | Vulnerability scanned |

### DB privilege principle

```text id="debezium-db-privilege"
Debezium user:
  replication privilege
  SELECT only on included tables
  publication privileges as needed

Avoid:
  superuser in production
```

Debezium docs explicitly recommend using a dedicated replication user with specific privileges instead of granting broad superuser access. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 35. Failure Recovery Scenarios

### Kafka Connect worker dies

```text id="worker-dies"
Worker dies
  ↓
Connect cluster rebalances tasks
  ↓
Another worker picks up task
  ↓
Task resumes from offset topic
```

Distributed mode provides automatic work balancing and fault tolerance for active tasks and config/offset commit data through Kafka-backed internal topics. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/37/kafka-connect/user-guide/))

### PostgreSQL unavailable

```text id="pg-unavailable"
PostgreSQL unavailable
  ↓
Debezium task fails/retries
  ↓
Replication slot retains WAL
  ↓
Connector resumes when DB returns
  ↓
Monitor retained WAL
```

### Kafka unavailable

```text id="kafka-unavailable-connect"
Kafka unavailable
  ↓
Connect cannot write records/internal offsets
  ↓
Task may fail/block
  ↓
PostgreSQL slot may retain WAL
  ↓
Recover Kafka then connector catches up
```

### Connector stopped too long

```text id="connector-stopped-too-long"
Connector stopped
  ↓
Replication slot inactive
  ↓
WAL retained
  ↓
Disk usage grows
  ↓
If WAL unavailable/slot removed:
      re-snapshot or restore recovery path needed
```

---

## 36. Runbook: Debezium Lag / WAL Growth

```text id="runbook-debezium-lag"
Alert: retained WAL growing / Debezium lag high
  ↓
Check connector status
  ↓
Check Connect worker logs
  ↓
Check PostgreSQL replication slot active
  ↓
Check Kafka broker/topic availability
  ↓
Check connector task error trace
  ↓
Check sink/consumer side if Connect queue blocked
  ↓
Resume/restart connector if safe
  ↓
If slot broken/lost:
      plan re-snapshot or restore from backup
```

### SQL checks

```sql id="runbook-slot-sql"
SELECT
    slot_name,
    active,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) AS retained_wal
FROM pg_replication_slots
WHERE slot_type = 'logical';
```

## 37. Runbook: Connector FAILED

```text id="runbook-connector-failed"
Connector FAILED
  ↓
GET /connectors/{name}/status
  ↓
Read task trace
  ↓
Classify:
    config error
    DB auth/network
    replication slot/publication
    converter/schema
    SMT config
    Kafka ACL/topic
  ↓
Fix root cause
  ↓
Restart task/connector
  ↓
Verify records flowing and lag decreasing
```

Commands:

```bash id="runbook-connect-commands"
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/prod.order.order-service.outbox.cdc/status | jq

curl -X POST http://connect:8083/connectors/prod.order.order-service.outbox.cdc/restart

curl -X POST http://connect:8083/connectors/prod.order.order-service.outbox.cdc/tasks/0/restart
```

## 38. Runbook: Bad Connector Config Deployed

```text id="runbook-bad-config"
Bad connector config deployed
  ↓
Pause connector
  ↓
Capture current status/config
  ↓
Rollback connector config from Git
  ↓
PUT previous config
  ↓
Resume/restart connector
  ↓
Validate topic output and LSN progress
```

Important:

```text id="bad-config-warning"
Do not casually change:
  connector name
  topic.prefix
  slot.name
  publication.name
  table.include.list
  transforms routing
  converter format

These can change offsets, topics, schema, or WAL behavior.
```

## 39. Runbook: Need Connector Migration

```text id="connector-migration-runbook"
Need change connector/topic/schema
  ↓
Classify change:
    compatible config update?
    topic routing change?
    slot/publication change?
    schema converter change?
  ↓
Test in staging
  ↓
Plan pause/resume or new connector
  ↓
If new connector:
    new connector name
    new slot if needed
    snapshot mode selected
    duplicate strategy defined
  ↓
Deploy
  ↓
Monitor duplicate/lag/topic output
```

## 40. Operational Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Dampak |
|---|---|
| Connect internal topics auto-created in prod | Wrong RF/partition/cleanup |
| Connect REST API public | Anyone can alter connectors |
| Connector config not versioned | No audit/rollback |
| Debezium user is superuser | Security risk |
| Replication slot not monitored | WAL fills disk |
| Outbox SMT applied to all Debezium messages | Heartbeat/tombstone/schema events fail |
| Raw CDC used as public domain event | Consumers coupled to DB schema |
| Connector name changed casually | Offset/lifecycle confusion |
| Slot dropped casually | Data loss / re-snapshot needed |
| No DLQ/alert for sink failures | Silent data loss/backlog |
| `errors.tolerance=all` without monitoring | Bad records disappear into operational debt |
| Secrets in connector JSON repo | Credential leak |
| Production uses eval container image blindly | Supply-chain/security risk |
| No staging connector rehearsal | Prod connector failure |
| Outbox table updated after insert | Event immutability broken |

---

## 41. Production Readiness Checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| Connect cluster | Distributed mode, HA workers |
| Internal topics | Manually created, compacted, replicated |
| Worker config | Secure Kafka auth, plugin path, converters |
| REST API | Internal-only and protected |
| Connector config | Version controlled |
| PostgreSQL | `wal_level=logical`, slots/senders sized |
| DB user | Dedicated least-privilege replication user |
| Debezium | Slot/publication/topic prefix named clearly |
| Outbox | Insert-only, stable event ID/key/payload |
| SMT | Applied selectively to outbox table |
| Schema | Converter and compatibility aligned |
| Security | Secrets externalized, ACL least privilege |
| Monitoring | Connector/task state, lag, WAL retained |
| Alerts | Task failed, slot inactive, WAL growth, DLQ |
| Runbooks | Connector failed, lag, bad config, migration |
| Cleanup | Outbox table cleanup/archive |
| Testing | Local/staging CDC, failure, restart, re-snapshot |
| Governance | Topic/schema/connector catalog maintained |

---

## 42. Quick Decision Guide

```text id="connect-quick-guide"
Need stream DB table changes to Kafka?
  → Debezium PostgreSQL source connector.

Need business events from a Jersey service?
  → Transactional outbox table + Debezium Outbox Event Router.

Need search index or warehouse from Kafka?
  → Sink connector if target connector mature.

Need custom business processing?
  → Java consumer / Kafka Streams, not connector.

Need schema-safe event contract?
  → Schema Registry + Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema converter.

Need lightweight JSON outbox?
  → JSON payload + JsonConverter + explicit contract tests.

Need retry/triage of bad sink records?
  → Connect DLQ + alerts + replay policy.

Need high reliability?
  → Distributed Connect + replicated compacted internal topics + monitored replication slot.

Need production deployment?
  → Connector config as code, REST API internal, secrets externalized, staging rehearsal.
```

---

## 43. Ringkasan Praktis

Kafka Connect adalah runtime integrasi data. Debezium adalah CDC connector yang membaca perubahan committed dari PostgreSQL melalui logical decoding dan replication slot. Untuk microservice Java/Jersey, pattern paling aman adalah:

```text id="connect-summary"
Jersey service
  ↓
PostgreSQL transaction:
  - update domain table
  - insert outbox_event
  ↓
Debezium PostgreSQL connector
  ↓
Outbox Event Router SMT
  ↓
Kafka topic:
  <domain>.<aggregate>.events.v1
  key = aggregateId
  headers = eventId/eventType/correlationId/tenantId
  value = business payload
  ↓
Idempotent consumers
```

Invariant utama:

```text id="connect-invariants"
1. Kafka Connect distributed mode needs durable compacted internal topics.
2. Connector config must be versioned and reviewable.
3. Debezium PostgreSQL depends on logical decoding and replication slots.
4. Replication slots must be monitored because they can retain WAL.
5. Raw CDC is not the same as business integration event.
6. Outbox events must be inserted in the same DB transaction as business state.
7. Outbox Event Router should be applied selectively.
8. Kafka key must use stable aggregate ID for ordering.
9. Connector REST API must not be public.
10. Connector failure must have alerts, runbooks, and recovery plan.
```

# Cheatsheet - Kafka Runbook & Incident Response Playbook  
## Lag Spike, DLQ Spike, Retry Storm, Missing Event, Duplicate Side Effect, Schema Break, Connector Failure, Outbox Backlog, Rollback, Replay

## Status seri

Ini adalah **Seri 3 dari 4 seri tersisa**.

Setelah seri ini, sisa:

| Sisa | Seri |
|---:|---|
| 1 | **Final Integration Blueprint** |

---

## 1. Core Mental Model

Incident Kafka biasanya bukan hanya “Kafka error”. Dalam microservice Java/Jersey, incident Kafka sering muncul sebagai gabungan dari:

```text id="incident-core-map"
Kafka Incident
│
├── Producer side
│   ├── event tidak terkirim
│   ├── outbox backlog
│   ├── serialization error
│   ├── topic/ACL error
│   └── bad event produced
│
├── Broker / platform side
│   ├── topic unavailable
│   ├── ISR/replication issue
│   ├── quota/throttling
│   ├── broker latency
│   └── retention/offset expired
│
├── Consumer side
│   ├── lag spike
│   ├── rebalance loop
│   ├── retry storm
│   ├── DLQ spike
│   ├── duplicate side effect
│   └── stuck handler
│
├── Contract side
│   ├── schema break
│   ├── unknown event version
│   ├── invalid payload
│   └── incompatible serializer
│
├── Connect / Debezium side
│   ├── connector failed
│   ├── task failed
│   ├── replication slot WAL growth
│   ├── bad SMT route
│   └── CDC lag
│
└── Recovery side
    ├── rollback
    ├── replay
    ├── DLQ repair
    ├── outbox re-drive
    ├── compensation
    └── postmortem
```

Consumer lag penting dipantau karena menunjukkan gap antara progress consumer dan data yang tersedia; Confluent mendefinisikan consumer lag sebagai kombinasi offset lag dan consumer latency, dan menyebutnya bisa dipantau lewat Control Center, JMX metrics, Metrics API, Cloud Console, atau Kafka Admin API tergantung platform. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/monitor/monitor-consumer-lag.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 2. Incident Triage First 5 Minutes

Saat alert Kafka masuk, jangan langsung restart semua pod. Ambil snapshot evidence dulu.

```text id="first-5-minutes"
1. Identify affected flow
2. Identify event/topic/group
3. Check blast radius
4. Check recent deploy/config/schema change
5. Classify failure
6. Stabilize
7. Recover
8. Prevent recurrence
```

### First questions

| Pertanyaan | Kenapa penting |
|---|---|
| Topic apa? | Menentukan owner dan data contract |
| Consumer group apa? | Menentukan affected processor |
| Event type apa? | Menentukan business impact |
| Sejak kapan? | Korelasi dengan deploy/config |
| Ada deploy/schema change? | Penyebab umum DLQ/contract break |
| Lag semua partition atau satu partition? | Capacity vs hot key |
| Retry/DLQ naik? | Failure processing |
| Outbox backlog naik? | Producer publication issue |
| Connector task failed? | CDC/Connect issue |
| Ada duplicate side effect? | Correctness incident |
| Data loss mungkin? | Prioritas recovery naik |

### Minimal evidence to capture

```text id="minimal-evidence"
- incident start time
- service version / deploy hash
- topic
- partition
- offset range
- consumer group
- eventId / eventType / eventVersion
- correlationId
- producer service/version
- errorClass
- DLQ/retry record count
- consumer lag by partition
- outbox pending count/oldest age
- connector/task status if CDC
```

---

## 3. Severity Classification

| Severity | Condition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| SEV-1 | Business-critical data flow stopped / data loss likely / money-order impact | Payment events not processed, orders stuck globally |
| SEV-2 | Major degradation with backlog but recoverable | Consumer lag rising for core service |
| SEV-3 | Isolated flow affected, workaround exists | One non-critical projection DLQ spike |
| SEV-4 | Low-risk alert / dev/staging only | Local connector failed |
| Security SEV | Credential/PII/DLQ exposure | DLQ contains secrets/PII visible broadly |

### Severity decision rule

```text id="severity-rule"
Data correctness > availability > latency > observability noise.

If money, entitlement, customer order state, or compliance is affected:
  escalate severity.
```

---

## 4. Global Incident Checklist

```text id="global-checklist"
Before action:
  - snapshot metrics
  - snapshot logs
  - identify latest deployment
  - identify exact topic/group/event
  - check if producer is still emitting bad data
  - check if consumer is still causing side effects

Stabilize:
  - stop bad producer if emitting invalid events
  - pause consumer if causing bad side effects
  - pause retry consumer if retry storm
  - rollback bad app/config
  - protect downstream DB/API

Recover:
  - drain lag
  - replay DLQ if safe
  - re-drive outbox if safe
  - restart connector/task if root cause fixed
  - run reconciliation

Close:
  - verify metrics normal
  - document offset/event range
  - update tests/runbook/alerts
```

---

# 5. Runbook - Consumer Lag Spike

## 5.1 Symptoms

```text id="lag-spike-symptoms"
- consumer_lag rising
- end-to-end latency rising
- records consumed/sec lower than produced/sec
- backlog grows after deployment
- downstream projections delayed
```

Consumer lag can be caused by configuration, performance issues, network latency, large messages, slow consumers, or high throughput; Confluent specifically calls out slow consumers and throughput/network/message-size issues as common contributors. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/monitor/monitor-consumer-lag.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 5.2 Triage flow

```text id="lag-spike-flow"
Consumer lag spike
  ↓
Is lag rising on all partitions?
  ├── yes → capacity / handler / downstream / broker issue
  └── no
       ↓
Is lag concentrated on one partition?
  ├── yes → hot key / poison event / partition-specific issue
  └── no → inspect assignment/rebalance/metrics
  ↓
Was there a recent deploy?
  ├── yes → compare processing latency before/after
  └── no → check producer traffic surge / downstream outage
  ↓
Are retry/DLQ increasing?
  ├── yes → processing failure
  └── no → throughput bottleneck/stuck consumer
```

## 5.3 Checks

| Check | How to interpret |
|---|---|
| Lag by partition | One partition high = hot key/poison |
| Records produced/sec | Producer surge? |
| Records processed/sec | Consumer throughput drop? |
| Processing latency p95/p99 | Handler slow? |
| DB pool wait | DB bottleneck? |
| Downstream API latency/error | External dependency issue? |
| Rebalance count | Group unstable? |
| Pod restarts/OOM | Deployment/runtime issue? |
| CPU throttling | Kubernetes resource issue? |
| DLQ/retry rate | Failure path active? |

## 5.4 Immediate actions

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Lag spike temporary during deploy | Monitor; do not panic |
| Lag rising after deploy | Rollback or scale if safe |
| DB bottleneck | Rate-limit/pause consumer; do not blindly scale |
| One hot partition | Identify key/event at stuck offset |
| Poison event | DLQ/quarantine if safe, then commit |
| Rebalance loop | Fix poll interval/pod restarts/shutdown |
| Producer surge | Temporarily scale consumers if partitions/downstream allow |
| Retry storm | Pause retry consumers; protect dependency |

## 5.5 Evidence commands / queries

```sql id="lag-db-downstream-check"
-- Check DB lock/wait if PostgreSQL is suspected
SELECT
    pid,
    state,
    wait_event_type,
    wait_event,
    now() - query_start AS query_age,
    query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state <> 'idle'
ORDER BY query_age DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

```text id="lag-dashboard-panels"
Dashboard panels:
  - consumer lag total
  - consumer lag by partition
  - produced rate
  - processed rate
  - processing latency p95/p99
  - DB latency
  - retry/DLQ count
  - rebalance count
  - pod restart count
```

---

# 6. Runbook - DLQ Spike

## 6.1 Symptoms

```text id="dlq-spike-symptoms"
- dlq_published_total spikes
- DLQ unresolved count grows
- specific eventType dominates
- schema validation errors appear
- consumer keeps processing but routes many records to DLQ
```

DLQ best practice includes configuring a DLQ topic, routing failed records into it, setting retry limits before DLQ, and monitoring DLQ traffic; it should not be a silent trash bin. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/monitor/monitor-consumer-lag.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 6.2 Triage flow

```text id="dlq-spike-flow"
DLQ spike
  ↓
Group DLQ by:
  - errorClass
  - eventType
  - eventVersion
  - producerVersion
  - tenantId
  ↓
Recent producer deploy/schema change?
  ├── yes → suspect producer contract break
  └── no
       ↓
Recent consumer deploy?
  ├── yes → suspect consumer bug/strict validation change
  └── no → inspect bad data/dependency/business rule
  ↓
Is bad producer still emitting?
  ├── yes → stop/rollback producer
  └── no → plan replay/fix-forward
```

## 6.3 DLQ grouping query

Jika DLQ juga disimpan ke quarantine table:

```sql id="dlq-grouping-query"
SELECT
    event_type,
    event_version,
    error_class,
    count(*) AS count,
    min(created_at) AS first_seen,
    max(created_at) AS last_seen
FROM kafka_quarantine_event
WHERE status = 'NEW'
GROUP BY event_type, event_version, error_class
ORDER BY count DESC;
```

## 6.4 DLQ decision matrix

| Root cause | Stop producer? | Replay? | Action |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Producer emitted invalid schema | Ya | After transform/fix | Rollback/fix producer |
| Consumer too strict | Tidak selalu | Yes after consumer fix | Patch consumer |
| Unknown event version | Maybe | After compatibility fix | Add handler/router |
| Bad business data | Maybe | Usually no as-is | Reject/repair data |
| Security/PII violation | Ya | No until review | Restrict DLQ, compliance |
| Transient dependency mislabeled DLQ | No | Maybe | Fix classifier to retry |
| Code bug in consumer | No | Yes after fix | Patch and replay |

## 6.5 DLQ replay rule

```text id="dlq-replay-rule"
Replay only after:
  - root cause identified
  - fix deployed
  - replay scope defined
  - event IDs known
  - idempotency verified
  - rate limit configured
  - replay audit enabled
```

---

# 7. Runbook - Retry Storm

## 7.1 Symptoms

```text id="retry-storm-symptoms"
- retry topic lag rising
- retry attempts increasing
- same errorClass dominates
- downstream DB/API latency worsening
- main consumer also slowing
- retry exhausted count increases
```

## 7.2 Triage flow

```text id="retry-storm-flow"
Retry storm
  ↓
Identify top errorClass / dependency
  ↓
Is dependency down or degraded?
  ├── yes → pause retry consumers, protect dependency
  └── no
       ↓
Is same payload failing repeatedly?
  ├── yes → poison; move to DLQ after threshold
  └── no
       ↓
Is retry classifier too broad?
  ├── yes → fix classifier
  └── no → check capacity / rate limit
```

## 7.3 Immediate controls

| Control | When |
|---|---|
| Pause retry consumer | Dependency outage or retry amplification |
| Increase backoff | Dependency degraded |
| Add jitter | Thundering herd |
| Reduce retry concurrency | DB/API bottleneck |
| Move exhausted records to DLQ | Poison / deterministic failure |
| Pause main consumer | If main flow causes harmful side effect |
| Rollback recent deploy | Retry started after deploy |
| Rate-limit replay | Recovery backlog large |

## 7.4 Retry storm anti-pattern

```text id="retry-storm-anti-pattern"
DB is down
  ↓
100 consumers retry immediately
  ↓
DB tries to recover
  ↓
retry load kills DB again
  ↓
incident extends
```

Better:

```text id="retry-storm-better"
DB is down
  ↓
pause retry consumers
  ↓
main flow applies backpressure
  ↓
DB recovers
  ↓
resume slowly with rate limit
```

---

# 8. Runbook - Missing Event Downstream

## 8.1 Symptoms

```text id="missing-event-symptoms"
- downstream says record/projection missing
- source DB has state, target DB does not
- no DLQ found initially
- customer/order stuck in pending state
```

## 8.2 Triage flow

```text id="missing-event-flow"
Missing event downstream
  ↓
Find business ID:
  orderId / aggregateId / eventId / correlationId
  ↓
Check source DB state
  ↓
Check outbox row exists?
  ├── no → producer/app transaction issue
  └── yes
       ↓
Check outbox status:
  PENDING / FAILED / PUBLISHED
  ↓
If PUBLISHED:
  find Kafka topic/partition/offset
  ↓
Check downstream consumer group lag
  ↓
Check processed_event table
  ↓
Check retry/DLQ/quarantine
  ↓
Decide replay/re-drive/repair
```

## 8.3 Source DB / outbox queries

```sql id="missing-event-outbox-query"
SELECT
    id,
    aggregate_type,
    aggregate_id,
    event_type,
    status,
    retry_count,
    created_at,
    published_at,
    last_error
FROM outbox_event
WHERE aggregate_id = :aggregate_id
ORDER BY created_at;
```

```sql id="missing-event-processed-query"
SELECT
    event_id,
    event_type,
    aggregate_id,
    processed_at
FROM processed_event
WHERE aggregate_id = :aggregate_id
ORDER BY processed_at;
```

## 8.4 Interpretation

| Finding | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| No outbox row | App did not emit event | Investigate app transaction/mapper |
| Outbox PENDING old | Relay/CDC stuck | Check relay/connector |
| Outbox FAILED | Publish failure | Fix root cause, re-drive |
| Outbox PUBLISHED but no Kafka record | Publisher metadata missing / compaction? | Investigate producer logs/topic |
| Kafka record exists, consumer lag high | Consumer behind | Drain lag |
| Kafka record exists, processed_event absent | Consumer did not process | Check retry/DLQ/handler |
| processed_event exists, target missing | Handler bug/transaction mismatch | Repair projection |
| DLQ has event | Contract/processing failure | Fix/replay |
| Duplicate processed_event only | Missing business side effect | Check transaction boundary |

## 8.5 Recovery choices

| Case | Recovery |
|---|---|
| Outbox pending | Restart/fix relay/connector |
| Outbox failed | Re-drive outbox after fix |
| Event in DLQ | Replay after fix |
| Projection missing | Replay event or rebuild projection |
| Event never emitted | Generate compensating event/manual repair after business approval |
| Source state wrong | Fix source state first |

---

# 9. Runbook - Duplicate Side Effect

## 9.1 Symptoms

```text id="duplicate-side-effect-symptoms"
- duplicate email sent
- duplicate payment/charge/authorization
- duplicate projection row
- duplicate external API call
- duplicate command to participant service
```

## 9.2 Triage flow

```text id="duplicate-flow"
Duplicate side effect
  ↓
Find eventId / commandId / businessId
  ↓
Was the same Kafka record reprocessed?
  ├── yes → consumer idempotency gap
  └── no
       ↓
Was duplicate event published?
  ├── yes → producer/outbox duplicate, consumer should still dedup
  └── no
       ↓
Was side effect idempotency key missing?
  ├── yes → external side effect gap
  └── no → investigate app bug/manual replay
```

## 9.3 Evidence

| Evidence | Where |
|---|---|
| `eventId` occurrences | logs, Kafka, processed_event |
| `commandId` occurrences | command ledger |
| Outbox row ID | outbox_event |
| Kafka offsets | topic/partition/offset |
| Consumer restarts/rebalance | deployment logs |
| Replay job logs | replay audit |
| External API idempotency key | API logs |
| Business duplicate record | target DB |

## 9.4 Queries

```sql id="duplicate-event-query"
SELECT event_id, count(*)
FROM processed_event
WHERE event_id = :event_id
GROUP BY event_id;
```

```sql id="duplicate-side-effect-query"
SELECT
    business_id,
    side_effect_type,
    idempotency_key,
    count(*),
    min(created_at),
    max(created_at)
FROM side_effect_audit
WHERE business_id = :business_id
GROUP BY business_id, side_effect_type, idempotency_key
HAVING count(*) > 1;
```

## 9.5 Root cause matrix

| Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| No `processed_event` guard | Add idempotent consumer |
| Guard not in same DB transaction | Move dedup + side effect into one transaction |
| Side effect external API lacks idempotency key | Add command/event ID as idempotency key |
| Outbox duplicate publish | Expected; consumer must dedup |
| Replay used existing group incorrectly | Add replay audit and scope |
| Rebalance before commit | Expected duplicate window; dedup needed |
| Consumer group reset accidentally | Governance and access control |
| Manual re-drive without approval | Replay process control |

## 9.6 Recovery

```text id="duplicate-recovery"
1. Stop further duplicate side effect if ongoing.
2. Identify exact duplicate scope.
3. Apply business compensation if needed.
4. Patch idempotency guard.
5. Backfill side_effect_audit if missing.
6. Add regression test.
```

---

# 10. Runbook - Schema / Contract Break

## 10.1 Symptoms

```text id="schema-break-symptoms"
- deserialization error spike
- schema validation failure
- DLQ spike after producer deploy
- unknown eventVersion
- consumer fails on enum/string change
- Schema Registry compatibility check failed or bypassed
```

## 10.2 Triage flow

```text id="schema-break-flow"
Schema break
  ↓
Identify eventType/eventVersion/producerVersion
  ↓
Compare last good vs bad event
  ↓
Was schema registered/changed?
  ↓
Did producer deploy happen?
  ↓
Did consumer deploy happen?
  ↓
Is bad producer still running?
  ├── yes → rollback/stop producer
  └── no → contain DLQ and plan replay
```

## 10.3 Breaking change examples

| Change | Usually breaking? |
|---|---:|
| Remove required field | Yes |
| Rename field | Yes |
| Change field type | Yes |
| Change field meaning | Yes |
| Add required field without default | Yes |
| Add optional field | Usually no |
| Add enum without fallback | Consumer-dependent |
| Change topic key semantics | Yes |
| Change serializer format | Yes |
| Change subject strategy | Yes |

Schema compatibility should be enforced in CI/CD. Kafka itself will keep retained messages until retention/compaction rules apply, so consumers may see old and new versions during replay and normal processing.

## 10.4 Immediate actions

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Bad producer still emitting | Rollback/stop producer |
| Consumer too strict | Patch consumer for compatibility |
| Schema policy bypassed | Stop pipeline, restore governance |
| Bad records in topic | Decide DLQ/replay/transform |
| PII leaked in bad event | Security/compliance incident |
| Unknown version but valid event | Add router/handler or DLQ intentionally |

## 10.5 Contract break runbook

```text id="schema-break-runbook"
Contract break
  ↓
Freeze new producer rollout
  ↓
Identify bad offset/time range
  ↓
Rollback producer or hotfix consumer
  ↓
Patch schema/compatibility tests
  ↓
Drain or DLQ bad events
  ↓
Transform/replay if needed
  ↓
Add golden event regression test
```

---

# 11. Runbook - Connector Failure

## 11.1 Symptoms

```text id="connector-failure-symptoms"
- Kafka Connect connector state FAILED
- task state FAILED
- CDC topics stop receiving data
- outbox table grows
- Debezium lag increases
- PostgreSQL retained WAL grows
```

Kafka Connect REST API provides endpoints to list connectors, get status, add/update connector configs, pause/resume connectors, and restart connectors/tasks without stopping the worker process. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/connect/references/restapi.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 11.2 Triage flow

```text id="connector-failure-flow"
Connector failed
  ↓
GET /connectors/{name}/status
  ↓
Read task trace
  ↓
Classify:
    - config error
    - DB auth/network
    - replication slot/publication
    - Kafka ACL/topic
    - converter/schema
    - SMT routing
    - worker/plugin issue
  ↓
Fix root cause
  ↓
Restart task/connector
  ↓
Verify LSN progress and output topic rate
```

## 11.3 Commands

```bash id="connect-runbook-commands"
# list connectors
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors | jq

# status
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/prod.order.outbox.cdc/status | jq

# config
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/prod.order.outbox.cdc/config | jq

# restart connector
curl -X POST http://connect:8083/connectors/prod.order.outbox.cdc/restart

# restart task
curl -X POST http://connect:8083/connectors/prod.order.outbox.cdc/tasks/0/restart
```

## 11.4 PostgreSQL replication slot checks

Debezium PostgreSQL connector uses logical decoding and replication slots; replication slots can retain WAL needed by Debezium, so if the connector is down or slow, retained WAL can grow and pressure PostgreSQL disk. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/connectors/postgresql.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

```sql id="slot-check-query"
SELECT
    slot_name,
    plugin,
    slot_type,
    active,
    restart_lsn,
    confirmed_flush_lsn,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) AS retained_wal
FROM pg_replication_slots
WHERE slot_type = 'logical';
```

## 11.5 Connector root cause matrix

| Failure | Evidence | Action |
|---|---|---|
| DB password expired | Auth error trace | Rotate secret, restart |
| DB network blocked | Connection timeout | Fix network/security group |
| Replication slot missing | Slot error | Recreate carefully; may need snapshot |
| WAL removed/slot invalid | Cannot resume | Re-snapshot/recovery plan |
| Publication missing table | No events for table | Fix publication/table include |
| Kafka topic ACL denied | Authorization error | Fix ACL |
| SMT config wrong | Transform exception | Rollback config |
| Converter mismatch | Serialization error | Fix converter/schema |
| Plugin missing | Class not found | Fix Connect image/plugin.path |
| Worker down | Pod crash | Restart/fix worker |

---

# 12. Runbook - Debezium Lag / WAL Growth

## 12.1 Symptoms

```text id="debezium-lag-symptoms"
- replication slot retained WAL growing
- connector running but CDC output delayed
- outbox_event table grows
- Kafka topic no new events
- Postgres disk pressure
```

## 12.2 Triage flow

```text id="debezium-lag-flow"
Debezium lag / WAL growth
  ↓
Is connector task RUNNING?
  ├── no → connector failure runbook
  └── yes
       ↓
Is Kafka writable?
  ├── no → Kafka/platform issue
  └── yes
       ↓
Is PostgreSQL producing huge WAL?
  ├── yes → high write volume / connector behind
  └── no
       ↓
Check connector queue/backpressure/converter errors
  ↓
Check output topic rate and ACL
  ↓
Scale/fix bottleneck or pause writes if disk risk
```

## 12.3 Actions by risk

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Retained WAL small, lag draining | Monitor |
| Retained WAL growing quickly | Escalate to DBA/platform |
| Disk near full | Stop source writes if necessary / urgent fix |
| Connector failed | Fix/restart |
| Kafka unavailable | Restore Kafka first |
| Bad connector config deployed | Rollback connector config |
| Slot inactive long time | Restart connector or recovery plan |
| Slot lost/dropped | Re-snapshot or restore; data-loss assessment |

---

# 13. Runbook - Outbox Backlog

## 13.1 Symptoms

```text id="outbox-backlog-symptoms"
- outbox pending count rising
- oldest pending age exceeds SLA
- event publication latency rising
- Kafka topic output rate drops
- consumer downstream sees missing/delayed events
```

## 13.2 Triage flow

```text id="outbox-backlog-flow"
Outbox backlog
  ↓
Which implementation?
  ├── polling relay
  └── Debezium CDC
  ↓
If polling:
  check relay pods, locks, failures, Kafka producer errors
  ↓
If Debezium:
  check connector status, slot lag, Kafka output
  ↓
Check outbox table:
  pending/failed/locked/stale lock
  ↓
Classify:
  Kafka unavailable / DB slow / relay bug / connector issue / bad event
  ↓
Recover and drain backlog
```

## 13.3 Queries for polling outbox

```sql id="outbox-backlog-summary"
SELECT
    status,
    count(*) AS count,
    min(created_at) AS oldest_created_at,
    max(created_at) AS newest_created_at
FROM outbox_event
GROUP BY status
ORDER BY status;
```

```sql id="outbox-oldest-pending"
SELECT
    id,
    aggregate_type,
    aggregate_id,
    event_type,
    retry_count,
    next_attempt_at,
    created_at,
    last_error
FROM outbox_event
WHERE status = 'PENDING'
ORDER BY created_at
LIMIT 20;
```

```sql id="outbox-stale-lock"
SELECT
    id,
    locked_by,
    lock_until,
    event_type,
    created_at
FROM outbox_event
WHERE status = 'IN_PROGRESS'
  AND lock_until < now()
ORDER BY lock_until
LIMIT 20;
```

## 13.4 Recovery

| Root cause | Recovery |
|---|---|
| Relay pod down | Restart / rollback relay |
| Kafka auth failure | Fix ACL/secret |
| Topic missing | Provision topic |
| Bad event serialization | Mark failed, fix mapper, re-drive |
| Stale locks | Release expired leases |
| DB query slow | Check index/vacuum/partition |
| Debezium connector failed | Connector runbook |
| Kafka unavailable | Wait/retry, monitor backlog |

---

# 14. Runbook - Rebalance Loop

## 14.1 Symptoms

```text id="rebalance-loop-runbook-symptoms"
- rebalance_total increases continuously
- assigned/revoked logs repeat
- consumer lag sawtooth pattern
- CommitFailedException appears
- max.poll.interval exceeded
- pods restart/OOM
```

`max.poll.interval.ms` sets the maximum delay between `poll()` calls when using consumer group management; if the consumer does not call `poll()` before this timeout, it is considered failed and the group rebalances. The Apache Kafka config reference shows the default as 300000 ms. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/10/configuration/consumer-configs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 14.2 Triage flow

```text id="rebalance-loop-flow"
Rebalance loop
  ↓
Recent deploy/HPA scaling?
  ↓
Pod restarts/OOMKilled?
  ↓
Processing p99 > max.poll.interval?
  ↓
DB/API latency spike?
  ↓
CPU throttling / GC pause?
  ↓
Liveness probe too aggressive?
  ↓
Assignment strategy/protocol changed?
```

## 14.3 Actions

| Cause | Action |
|---|---|
| Handler too slow | Reduce `max.poll.records`, optimize handler |
| DB/API hangs | Add timeout/circuit breaker |
| CPU throttling | Adjust CPU requests/limits |
| Pod restart loop | Fix crash/OOM/probe |
| Aggressive HPA | Add cooldown/stabilization |
| Bad shutdown | Use `consumer.wakeup()` and close cleanly |
| Large batch | Reduce poll batch |
| Deployment churn | Slow rollout / maxUnavailable 0 |

---

# 15. Runbook - Offset Expired / Reset Needed

## 15.1 Symptoms

```text id="offset-expired-symptoms"
- consumer cannot continue from committed offset
- OffsetOutOfRangeException
- consumer starts at latest/earliest unexpectedly
- old data no longer available due retention
```

`auto.offset.reset` controls what a consumer does when there is no initial offset or the current offset no longer exists; current Kafka docs include values like `earliest`, `latest`, `by_duration`, and `none`, depending on client/platform version. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/41/configuration/consumer-configs/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 15.2 Triage flow

```text id="offset-expired-flow"
Offset expired
  ↓
Check topic retention
  ↓
Check consumer downtime duration
  ↓
Check last committed offset
  ↓
Check source of truth / archive
  ↓
Decide:
    rebuild from source DB?
    replay from archive?
    start latest with reconciliation?
    fail and manual repair?
```

## 15.3 Recovery decision

| Use case | Action |
|---|---|
| Projection rebuild possible | Reset group to earliest if retained; else rebuild from DB/archive |
| Audit-critical event lost | Escalate; restore from backup/archive |
| Real-time non-critical | Start latest with documented gap |
| Consumer bug caused downtime | Patch + replay if retained |
| Retention too short | Increase retention after capacity review |

---

# 16. Runbook - Kafka Producer Publish Failure

## 16.1 Symptoms

```text id="producer-failure-symptoms"
- producer send failures
- outbox pending/failed grows
- publish callback exceptions
- topic auth errors
- serialization failures
```

## 16.2 Triage flow

```text id="producer-failure-flow"
Producer failure
  ↓
Classify exception:
    - serialization
    - authorization
    - topic missing
    - timeout
    - message too large
    - buffer full
  ↓
Direct producer or outbox?
  ├── direct → assess potential event loss
  └── outbox → event should still be pending/failed
  ↓
Fix root cause
  ↓
Re-drive from outbox/source of truth if needed
```

## 16.3 Producer failure matrix

| Error | Retry? | Action |
|---|---:|---|
| Serialization error | No | Fix code/schema |
| Authorization error | No | Fix ACL/credential |
| Topic missing | No until provisioned | Provision topic |
| Timeout | Yes | Retry/outbox |
| Buffer full | Capacity | Backpressure/tune |
| Message too large | No | Redesign payload |
| Broker unavailable | Yes | Outbox backlog expected |
| Unknown fatal config | No | Fail startup/rollback |

---

# 17. Runbook - Bad Deployment / Rollback

## 17.1 Symptoms

```text id="bad-deploy-symptoms"
- DLQ starts exactly after deploy
- processing latency jumps
- lag grows after deploy
- schema errors after producer deploy
- new connector config fails
- side effects wrong
```

## 17.2 Rollback flow

```text id="rollback-flow"
Bad deployment suspected
  ↓
Capture evidence:
    deploy version, start time, logs, metrics
  ↓
Stop damage:
    rollback producer if bad events emitted
    pause consumer if bad side effects
  ↓
Rollback app/config/connector
  ↓
Verify:
    pods ready
    consumer group stable
    DLQ/retry stopped increasing
    lag draining
  ↓
Assess data produced during bad window
  ↓
Replay/repair/compensate
```

## 17.3 Kafka-specific rollback questions

| Question | Why |
|---|---|
| Did bad producer publish invalid events? | Need bad offset range |
| Did bad consumer commit offsets after wrong handling? | Replay may require reset/new group |
| Did bad consumer cause side effects? | Compensation needed |
| Did schema registry accept bad schema? | Governance rollback |
| Did connector route to wrong topic? | Need topic cleanup/replay |
| Did outbox contain bad payloads? | Fix rows/re-drive? |

---

# 18. Runbook - Replay

## 18.1 Replay is not just “consume from beginning”

Replay can rebuild state or repair incidents, but it can also duplicate side effects.

```text id="replay-definition"
Replay:
  intentionally process historical event(s)
  to rebuild/repair/recover state
  with controlled scope and audit
```

## 18.2 Replay sources

| Source | Use |
|---|---|
| Original Kafka topic | Event retained and valid |
| DLQ topic | Failed events after fix |
| Quarantine table | Triage/replay workflow |
| Outbox table | Re-drive unpublished/failed event |
| Source DB | Rebuild projection from source of truth |
| Archive/data lake | If Kafka retention expired |
| CDC snapshot | Rehydrate downstream |

## 18.3 Replay flow

```text id="replay-flow"
Replay request
  ↓
Define scope:
    eventId / aggregateId / topic offset range / time range
  ↓
Classify side effects:
    pure projection?
    external email/payment/API?
  ↓
Verify idempotency
  ↓
Choose replay method:
    new group / assign+seek / DLQ replay / outbox re-drive
  ↓
Rate limit
  ↓
Run
  ↓
Validate state
  ↓
Record audit
```

## 18.4 Replay safety checklist

| Check | Required |
|---|---|
| Root cause fixed | Yes |
| Scope bounded | Yes |
| Idempotency verified | Yes |
| External side effects guarded | Yes |
| Business approval for critical flows | Yes |
| Rate limit set | Yes |
| Observability active | Yes |
| Audit trail | Yes |
| Rollback plan | Yes |

## 18.5 Replay methods

| Method | Use | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| New consumer group | Rebuild projection | Duplicates if writes same target |
| Reset existing group offset | Reprocess same flow | Dangerous if side effects |
| `assign()` + `seek()` tool | Targeted offset replay | Manual complexity |
| DLQ replay topic | Repair failed records | Need transform/fix |
| Outbox re-drive | Publish missing events | Duplicate possible |
| DB rebuild job | Projection full rebuild | Source schema coupling |

---

# 19. Runbook - Data Reconciliation

Reconciliation memastikan source-of-truth dan downstream state kembali konsisten.

```text id="reconciliation-flow"
After recovery
  ↓
Compare source state vs projection/target
  ↓
Find missing/extra/mismatched records
  ↓
Classify differences
  ↓
Replay/repair/compensate
  ↓
Mark incident resolved only after reconciliation
```

## 19.1 Example reconciliation query

```sql id="reconciliation-example"
-- In projection DB, find orders expected from source export but missing locally
SELECT s.order_id
FROM expected_source_orders s
LEFT JOIN order_projection p ON p.order_id = s.order_id
WHERE p.order_id IS NULL;
```

## 19.2 Reconciliation categories

| Category | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Missing downstream | Event not processed | Replay |
| Extra downstream | Duplicate/wrong side effect | Compensate/remove if safe |
| Mismatched field | Old/bad event mapping | Rebuild/update |
| Stale status | Consumer lag/retry | Drain/replay |
| Source wrong | Business correction | Fix source then emit corrective event |

---

# 20. Runbook - Security / PII Incident in Kafka

## 20.1 Symptoms

```text id="security-incident-symptoms"
- secret/token/password found in event payload
- PII in broad-access topic
- DLQ contains raw sensitive payload
- wrong service has ACL read access
- prod credential used in local/dev
```

## 20.2 Flow

```text id="security-incident-flow"
Sensitive data issue
  ↓
Stop producer if still emitting
  ↓
Restrict topic/DLQ ACL
  ↓
Identify offset/time range
  ↓
Rotate leaked credential if any
  ↓
Assess consumers that read data
  ↓
Decide delete/compact/tombstone/archive policy with compliance
  ↓
Patch producer/contract tests
  ↓
Postmortem
```

## 20.3 Important note

Kafka retention and replication mean sensitive data may persist in logs until retention/compaction and backup policies remove it. For compacted topics, tombstone can remove keys eventually, but it is not instant deletion of all historical copies. Treat this as a compliance/security workflow, not normal app replay.

## 21.1 Kubernetes

kubectl rollout status deployment/order-service
kubectl get pods -l app=order-service
kubectl describe pod <pod>
kubectl logs deployment/order-service --tail=300

kubectl rollout undo deployment/order-service
