```bash id="connect-ops-commands"
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors | jq
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/<name>/status | jq
curl -s http://connect:8083/connectors/<name>/config | jq
curl -X PUT http://connect:8083/connectors/<name>/pause
curl -X PUT http://connect:8083/connectors/<name>/resume
curl -X POST http://connect:8083/connectors/<name>/restart
curl -X POST http://connect:8083/connectors/<name>/tasks/0/restart
```

## 21.3 PostgreSQL outbox / Debezium

```sql id="ops-sql-catalog"
-- Outbox backlog
SELECT status, count(*), min(created_at)
FROM outbox_event
GROUP BY status;

-- Oldest pending
SELECT *
FROM outbox_event
WHERE status = 'PENDING'
ORDER BY created_at
LIMIT 10;

-- Replication slot WAL retention
SELECT
    slot_name,
    active,
    pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) AS retained_wal
FROM pg_replication_slots
WHERE slot_type = 'logical';
```

# 25. Postmortem Checklist

| Area | Questions |
|---|---|
| Detection | Did alert fire early enough? |
| Triage | Was topic/group/event identified quickly? |
| Blast radius | Which services/customers/tenants affected? |
| Mitigation | Did we stop bad data/side effects fast? |
| Recovery | Was replay/reconciliation controlled? |
| Correctness | Any data loss or duplicate side effect? |
| Governance | Did schema/topic/ACL process fail? |
| Testing | Which test would have caught it? |
| Observability | Were logs/metrics sufficient? |
| Runbook | Was runbook accurate? |
| Ownership | Was escalation path clear? |
| Prevention | What guardrail is now automated? |

# 26. Production Guardrails to Prevent Recurrence

| Incident type | Guardrail |
|---|---|
| Schema break | CI compatibility + golden event |
| Missing event | Outbox + outbox pending alert |
| Duplicate side effect | Idempotency table + side effect idempotency key |
| Retry storm | Backoff, jitter, rate limit, circuit breaker |
| DLQ hidden | DLQ unresolved age alert |
| Connector failure | Task state + WAL retention alert |
| Rebalance loop | Poll interval dashboard + pod restart alerts |
| Retention too short | Lag/oldest unprocessed age alert |
| Bad producer deploy | Canary/staged rollout |
| Wrong topic config | Topic catalog drift detection |
| ACL failure after deploy | Startup validation + staging rehearsal |
| Sensitive payload | Contract privacy scan |

# 27. Testing the Runbooks

A runbook that is never tested is just documentation.

```text id="runbook-test-drills"
Quarterly / per major release:
  - simulate DLQ spike
  - simulate retry storm
  - stop connector
  - break schema in staging
  - create outbox backlog
  - restart consumer during processing
  - replay DLQ safely
  - rollback producer
```

### Staging drills

| Drill | Success criteria |
|---|---|
| DLQ poison event | Alert fires, DLQ metadata complete |
| Retry storm | Retry paused/rate-limited |
| Connector task failed | On-call finds status and restarts |
| Outbox backlog | Pending age alert and relay recovery |
| Schema break | CI or staging catches before prod |
| Rebalance loop | Metrics identify cause |
| Replay | Audit and idempotency verified |

---

# 28. Common Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Dampak |
|---|---|
| Restart all consumers first | Evidence hilang, rebalance storm |
| Scale consumers while DB is bottleneck | Incident makin parah |
| Replay before root cause fixed | DLQ/retry berulang |
| Commit offset after failed DLQ publish | Data loss |
| Ignore outbox backlog because API still works | Downstream misses events |
| Drop Debezium slot to “fix lag” | Data loss / re-snapshot required |
| Treat business rejection as retryable | Retry storm |
| Treat schema break as transient | DLQ/retry noise |
| No eventId/correlationId in logs | Triage lambat |
| No bad offset range recorded | Replay sulit |
| DLQ topic broadly readable | Security risk |
| Rollback without checking bad events already emitted | Bad data remains |
| Incident resolved before reconciliation | Hidden data inconsistency |
| No postmortem action owner | Recurrence likely |

---

# 29. Production Readiness Checklist

| Area | Checklist |
|---|---|
| Alerts | Lag, DLQ, retry, outbox, connector, WAL, rebalance |
| Dashboards | Topic/group/event/error-class visibility |
| Logs | eventId, correlationId, topic, partition, offset |
| DLQ | Metadata complete, restricted ACL, replay plan |
| Retry | Backoff, jitter, max attempts, pause switch |
| Outbox | Pending/failed/oldest age monitored |
| Connect | Connector/task status monitored |
| Debezium | Replication slot/WAL monitored |
| Rebalance | Rebalance count and poll age monitored |
| Replay | Tooling, audit, idempotency, rate limit |
| Rollback | App + connector rollback documented |
| Reconciliation | Source vs downstream validation |
| Ownership | Topic/service/on-call owners known |
| Runbooks | Tested in staging |
| Postmortem | Template and action tracking |

## 30. Quick Decision Guide

```text id="incident-quick-guide"
Lag rising?
  → Check all partitions vs one partition, processing latency, DB/downstream, rebalance.

DLQ spike?
  → Group by eventType/errorClass/producerVersion, stop bad producer if active.

Retry storm?
  → Pause retry, protect dependency, add backoff/rate limit.

Missing event?
  → Trace source DB → outbox → Kafka offset → processed_event → DLQ/retry.

Duplicate side effect?
  → Check eventId/commandId idempotency, outbox duplicate, replay/rebalance.

Schema break?
  → Rollback producer or patch consumer, identify bad offset range, replay after fix.

Connector failed?
  → Check Connect status/task trace, DB/slot/Kafka/SMT/converter.

Debezium WAL growing?
  → Connector lag/down; fix fast before disk fills.

Outbox backlog?
  → Determine relay vs Debezium; check pending/failed/stale locks.

Need replay?
  → Fix root cause first, define scope, verify idempotency, rate-limit, audit.
```

---

## 31. Ringkasan Praktis

Kafka incident response yang sehat mengikuti urutan:

```text id="incident-summary-flow"
Detect
  ↓
Classify
  ↓
Contain damage
  ↓
Recover safely
  ↓
Reconcile data
  ↓
Prevent recurrence
```

Invariant utama:

```text id="incident-invariants"
1. Jangan restart/scale sebelum tahu bottleneck.
2. Jangan replay sebelum root cause fixed.
3. Jangan commit offset jika retry/DLQ publish gagal.
4. Jangan drop replication slot tanpa recovery plan.
5. Jangan anggap DLQ selesai hanya karena main consumer jalan.
6. Jangan close incident sebelum reconciliation.
7. Semua recovery harus punya audit trail.
8. Semua duplicate harus dianggap normal sampai idempotency membuktikan aman.
9. Semua schema break harus menjadi CI regression test.
10. Semua incident Kafka harus mencatat topic, partition, offset, eventId, dan correlationId.
```

# Final Integration Blueprint - Java/Jersey + PostgreSQL + Outbox + Kafka + Consumers + Streams/ksqlDB + Camunda + Kubernetes

## Status seri

Ini adalah **Seri 4 dari 4** dan menjadi penutup rangkaian **Java Kafka Client + EDA dalam Jersey/JAX-RS microservice**.

✅ Setelah cheatsheet ini, rangkaian seri Kafka untuk onboarding Anda **selesai**.

## 1. Executive Blueprint

Blueprint produksi yang paling aman untuk stack Anda:

```text id="final-blueprint-high-level"
Client / External System
  ↓
Jersey / JAX-RS Resource
  ↓
Application Service
  ↓
PostgreSQL Transaction
  ├── update business tables
  └── insert outbox_event
       ↓
Debezium / Outbox Relay
       ↓
Kafka Topic
       ↓
Consumers
  ├── idempotent handler
  ├── retry topic
  ├── DLQ / quarantine
  └── projections / side effects
       ↓
Kafka Streams / ksqlDB / Camunda where needed
       ↓
Observability + Security + Governance
```

Kafka memisahkan producer dan consumer; producer menulis event ke Kafka, consumer membaca dan memproses event, dan keduanya tidak perlu saling menunggu secara langsung. Kafka juga menyediakan guarantee tertentu, termasuk dukungan exactly-once pada skenario tertentu, tetapi boundary aplikasi seperti DB/API eksternal tetap harus didesain idempotent. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/documentation/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 2. Reference Architecture

```text id="reference-architecture"
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        API Layer                               │
│  Jersey Resource / Filters / ExceptionMapper / Auth Context     │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Application Layer                           │
│  Use Case Service / Transaction Boundary / Domain Validation    │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Persistence Layer                           │
│  PostgreSQL + MyBatis                                           │
│  - business tables                                              │
│  - outbox_event                                                 │
│  - processed_event                                              │
│  - projection tables                                            │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                 commit DB transaction
                            │
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Publication Layer                           │
│  Option A: Debezium PostgreSQL CDC + Outbox Event Router        │
│  Option B: Polling Outbox Relay                                 │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       Kafka Layer                              │
│  Topics / Partitions / ACL / Schema Registry / Retention        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Consumption Layer                           │
│  Plain Consumer / Kafka Streams / ksqlDB / Connect Sink         │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                            │
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Process & Orchestration Layer                 │
│  Camunda Saga / BPMN / Job Workers / Message Correlation        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Debezium adalah platform CDC yang memonitor database dan membuat aplikasi bisa bereaksi terhadap insert, update, dan delete yang sudah di-commit. Untuk transactional outbox, Debezium Outbox Event Router menangkap perubahan pada outbox table lalu merutekannya menjadi event Kafka yang lebih business-oriented. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

---

## 3. Recommended Production Pattern

Untuk event bisnis penting, gunakan pattern berikut:

```text id="recommended-prod-pattern"
HTTP Command
  ↓
Jersey Resource
  ↓
Application Service
  ↓
PostgreSQL transaction:
  - validate command
  - update domain state
  - insert outbox_event
  ↓
commit
  ↓
Debezium / Outbox Relay publishes Kafka event
  ↓
Consumer:
  - deserialize
  - validate contract
  - check processed_event
  - apply side effect/projection in DB transaction
  - commit Kafka offset after safe outcome
```

### Kenapa ini baseline terbaik?

| Problem | Solusi |
|---|---|
| DB commit sukses tapi Kafka publish gagal | Transactional outbox |
| Kafka event duplicate | Idempotent consumer |
| Consumer crash setelah DB commit sebelum offset commit | `processed_event` dedup |
| Schema berubah | Schema compatibility + contract tests |
| Poison event | DLQ/quarantine |
| Downstream lambat | Retry topic + backpressure |
| Saga long-running | Camunda orchestration |
| Debugging sulit | eventId + correlationId + topic/partition/offset logs |
| Rollback/replay | Outbox + retained topic + replay tooling |


Rule boundary:

```text id="module-boundary-rule"
Resource layer must not publish Kafka directly.
Domain layer must not depend on Kafka APIs.
Application layer owns transaction boundary.
Messaging layer owns Kafka protocol details.
Persistence layer owns SQL/MyBatis.
```

## 5. Write Path Blueprint

### Flow

```text id="write-path"
POST /orders
  ↓
OrderResource
  ↓
CreateOrderService
  ↓
BEGIN PostgreSQL TX
  ↓
insert order
insert order_items
insert outbox_event
  ↓
COMMIT
  ↓
HTTP 201 Created
  ↓
Debezium / Outbox Relay emits OrderCreated
```

### SQL: outbox table

```sql id="blueprint-outbox-table"
CREATE TABLE outbox_event (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    aggregate_type  TEXT NOT NULL,
    aggregate_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
    event_type      TEXT NOT NULL,
    event_version   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payload         JSONB NOT NULL,
    headers         JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_outbox_event_aggregate
ON outbox_event (aggregate_type, aggregate_id, created_at);
```

### Java service sketch

```java id="blueprint-create-order-service"
public OrderId createOrder(CreateOrderCommand command, RequestContext ctx) {
    return transaction.inTransaction(() -> {
        Order order = Order.create(command.customerId(), command.items());

        orderRepository.insert(order);

        EventEnvelope<OrderCreatedPayload> event =
                EventEnvelope.<OrderCreatedPayload>builder()
                        .eventId(UUID.randomUUID())
                        .eventType("OrderCreated")
                        .eventVersion(1)
                        .occurredAt(clock.instant())
                        .producer("order-service")
                        .correlationId(ctx.correlationId())
                        .causationId(ctx.commandId())
                        .tenantId(ctx.tenantId())
                        .aggregateType("Order")
                        .aggregateId(order.id().value())
                        .payload(new OrderCreatedPayload(
                                order.id().value(),
                                order.customerId().value(),
                                order.status().name()
                        ))
                        .build();

        outboxRepository.insert(event);

        return order.id();
    });
}
```

Invariant:

```text id="write-path-invariant"
Business state and outbox event must commit together.
Never publish Kafka event before DB transaction commits.
```

### Topic contract

```yaml id="topic-contract-blueprint"
topic: order.order.events.v1
owner: order-platform
producer: order-service
key: aggregateId
ordering: per order
schemaSubject: order.order.events.v1-value
```

## 7. Topic & Partitioning Blueprint

```text id="topic-blueprint"
Business event:
  <domain>.<aggregate>.events.v1

Command:
  <domain>.<capability>.commands.v1

Retry:
  <domain>.<stream>.retry.<delay>.v1

DLQ:
  <domain>.<stream>.dlq.v1

Audit:
  <domain>.<process>.audit.v1
```

| Topic | Key | Cleanup | Retention | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order.order.events.v1` | `orderId` | delete | 7d+ | Main order lifecycle |
| `billing.payment.events.v1` | `paymentId` | delete | 30d | Payment audit-sensitive |
| `customer.profile.changelog.v1` | `customerId` | compact | policy | Latest profile state |
| `inventory.reservation.commands.v1` | `reservationId` | delete | short | Saga command |
| `order.order-events.dlq.v1` | original key | delete | 14d+ | Restricted ACL |
| `saga.order-process.audit.v1` | `sagaId` | delete | long | Process audit |

Partition rule:

```text id="partition-rule-final"
Need ordering per aggregate:
  key = aggregateId

Need throughput:
  partitions >= desired active consumers

Need both:
  key by aggregate and capacity-plan partition count early
```

## 8. Consumer Blueprint

### Flow

```text id="consumer-blueprint-flow"
Kafka poll
  ↓
deserialize
  ↓
validate envelope/schema/version
  ↓
BEGIN PostgreSQL TX
  ↓
try insert processed_event(event_id)
  ├── duplicate → no-op success
  └── first time → apply side effect/projection
  ↓
COMMIT
  ↓
commit Kafka offset
```

### `processed_event` table

```sql id="processed-event-blueprint"
CREATE TABLE processed_event (
    event_id      UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    event_type    TEXT NOT NULL,
    aggregate_id  TEXT,
    consumer_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    processed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_processed_event_aggregate
ON processed_event (aggregate_id, processed_at);
```

### Consumer pseudocode

```java id="consumer-blueprint-code"
public void process(ConsumerRecord<String, String> record) {
    try {
        EventEnvelope<?> event = deserializer.deserialize(record.value());
        validator.validate(event);

        transaction.inTransaction(() -> {
            boolean firstTime = processedEventRepository.tryInsert(
                    event.eventId(),
                    event.eventType(),
                    event.aggregateId(),
                    "order-projection-service"
            );

            if (!firstTime) {
                metrics.duplicateEvent(event.eventType());
                return null;
            }

            dispatcher.dispatch(event);
            return null;
        });

        offsets.markProcessed(record);
    } catch (Exception error) {
        FailureAction action = classifier.classify(error);

        switch (action) {
            case SEND_TO_RETRY_TOPIC -> {
                retryPublisher.publish(record, error);
                offsets.markProcessed(record);
            }
            case SEND_TO_DLQ -> {
                dlqPublisher.publish(record, error);
                offsets.markProcessed(record);
            }
            case STOP_CONSUMER -> throw new FatalConsumerException(error);
            default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Unsupported action: " + action);
        }
    }
}
```

Invariant:

```text id="consumer-invariant-final"
Kafka offset commit means:
  record is safely handled by business logic,
  or safely moved to retry/DLQ,
  or safely identified as duplicate.
```

## 9. Retry, DLQ, Quarantine Blueprint

```text id="retry-dlq-blueprint"
main topic
  ↓
consumer
  ↓ failure classifier
  ├── transient → retry topic
  ├── permanent contract/data → DLQ
  ├── business rejection → rejected event / BPMN branch
  └── fatal config/code bug → stop consumer
```

### Failure action table

| Failure | Action | Commit original offset? |
|---|---|---:|
| Success | Commit | Yes |
| Duplicate | Treat success | Yes |
| DB timeout | Publish retry | After retry publish success |
| HTTP 503 | Publish retry | After retry publish success |
| Bad JSON | Publish DLQ | After DLQ publish success |
| Unknown schema version | DLQ or stop | After DLQ publish success |
| ACL denied | Stop | No |
| Code bug | Stop | No |
| Business rejection | Rejected event / process branch | After durable outcome |

### Quarantine table

```sql id="quarantine-blueprint"
CREATE TABLE kafka_quarantine_event (
    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    consumer_group      TEXT NOT NULL,
    original_topic      TEXT NOT NULL,
    original_partition  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    original_offset     BIGINT NOT NULL,
    original_key        TEXT,
    event_id            UUID,
    event_type          TEXT,
    event_version       INTEGER,
    correlation_id      TEXT,
    tenant_id           TEXT,
    classification      TEXT NOT NULL,
    error_class         TEXT NOT NULL,
    error_message       TEXT,
    payload             JSONB NOT NULL,
    status              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NEW',
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (consumer_group, original_topic, original_partition, original_offset)
);
```

---

## 10. Kafka Streams / ksqlDB Blueprint

Gunakan Kafka Streams atau ksqlDB hanya jika problem-nya memang stream processing, bukan sekadar consume-write-DB biasa.

```text id="streams-ksqldb-decision"
Plain Consumer:
  event → DB side effect/projection

Kafka Streams:
  stream transformation, join, aggregation, window, materialized view

ksqlDB:
  SQL-first stream processing, simple routing/filtering/aggregation,
  operational query managed outside Java service
```

Kafka exactly-once support kuat untuk pemrosesan Kafka-to-Kafka seperti Kafka Streams dan transaksi producer/consumer, tetapi tidak otomatis membuat side effect ke PostgreSQL atau REST API menjadi exactly-once. Untuk boundary eksternal, tetap gunakan idempotency, dedup table, dan transaction boundary aplikasi. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/kafka/design/delivery-semantics.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Kafka Streams placement

```text id="streams-placement"
order.order.events.v1
  ↓
Kafka Streams app
  ├── enrich with customer.profile.changelog.v1
  ├── aggregate order count by tenant
  └── output order.summary.events.v1
```

### ksqlDB placement

```text id="ksqldb-placement"
order.order.events.v1
  ↓
ksqlDB persistent query:
  - filter OrderCreated
  - aggregate hourly count
  - materialized table
  ↓
derived topic / pull query
```

---

## 11. Camunda Saga Blueprint

Camunda cocok untuk proses long-running, timeout, compensation, human task, dan orchestration. Camunda 8 service task memakai task type dan job workers untuk menjalankan pekerjaan; message events digunakan ketika process instance menunggu message dari external system. ([Camunda 8 Docs](https://docs.camunda.io/docs/components/best-practices/development/writing-good-workers/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Orchestration model

```text id="camunda-saga-blueprint"
OrderCreated event
  ↓
Start Order Fulfillment Process
  ↓
Reserve Inventory command
  ↓
InventoryReserved / InventoryRejected message
  ↓
Authorize Payment command
  ↓
PaymentAuthorized / PaymentRejected message
  ↓
Confirm Order
  ↓
OrderConfirmed event
```

### Command/event boundary

| Type | Example | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| Event | `OrderCreated` | Service → Kafka |
| Command | `ReserveInventory` | Camunda/Orchestrator → Participant |
| Reply event | `InventoryReserved` | Participant → Kafka |
| BPMN message | `InventoryReservedMessage` | Bridge → Camunda |
| Compensation command | `ReleaseInventory` | Camunda → Participant |

### Correlation fields

```text id="saga-correlation-fields"
sagaId
businessKey
processInstanceKey
commandId
eventId
correlationId
causationId
aggregateId
tenantId
```

Invariant:

```text id="saga-invariant-final"
Camunda owns process state.
Microservice owns domain state.
Kafka carries commands/events.
PostgreSQL remains source of truth for each service-local domain.
```

---

## 12. Kafka Connect / Debezium Blueprint

```text id="connect-debezium-blueprint"
PostgreSQL outbox_event
  ↓
Debezium PostgreSQL Connector
  ↓
Outbox Event Router SMT
  ↓
Kafka topic:
  <domain>.<aggregate>.events.v1
```

Debezium’s outbox pattern is designed to avoid inconsistency between service internal state and emitted events. The Outbox Event Router captures changes from an outbox table and routes them into Kafka messages using fields such as aggregate type, aggregate ID, event type, and payload. ([Debezium](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/stable/transformations/outbox-event-router.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Connector config skeleton

```json id="final-debezium-config"
{
  "name": "prod.order.order-service.outbox.cdc",
  "connector.class": "io.debezium.connector.postgresql.PostgresConnector",
  "tasks.max": "1",

  "database.hostname": "orders-postgres.internal",
  "database.port": "5432",
  "database.user": "debezium_order",
  "database.password": "${file:/opt/connect/secrets/orders.properties:password}",
  "database.dbname": "orders",

  "topic.prefix": "orderdb",
  "plugin.name": "pgoutput",
  "slot.name": "prod_order_outbox_slot",
  "publication.name": "prod_order_outbox_publication",

  "table.include.list": "public.outbox_event",

  "transforms": "outbox",
  "transforms.outbox.type": "io.debezium.transforms.outbox.EventRouter",
  "transforms.outbox.route.by.field": "aggregate_type",
  "transforms.outbox.route.topic.replacement": "${routedByValue}.events.v1",
  "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.key": "aggregate_id",
  "transforms.outbox.table.field.event.payload": "payload"
}
```

## 13. Kubernetes Deployment Blueprint

```text id="k8s-blueprint"
Deployment
  ↓
ConfigMap + Secret
  ↓
startupProbe
  ↓
readinessProbe
  ↓
livenessProbe
  ↓
SIGTERM graceful shutdown
  ↓
consumer.wakeup()
  ↓
commit safe offsets
  ↓
close producer/consumer/admin
```

Kubernetes Pod termination uses a grace period; kubelet attempts graceful shutdown by sending TERM/SIGTERM before forceful termination after the grace period. This matters for Kafka consumers because shutdown must stop new work, finish safe in-flight work, commit safe offsets, and close clients before the Pod is killed. ([Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

### Deployment skeleton

```yaml id="k8s-deployment-blueprint"
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: order-service
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: order-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: order-service
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 90
      containers:
        - name: order-service
          image: registry.example.com/order-service:1.0.0
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: order-service-config
            - secretRef:
                name: order-service-secrets
          volumeMounts:
            - name: kafka-secrets
              mountPath: /etc/kafka/secrets
              readOnly: true
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/startup
              port: http
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/ready
              port: http
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health/live
              port: http
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "768Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "2"
              memory: "1536Mi"
      volumes:
        - name: kafka-secrets
          secret:
            secretName: kafka-client-secrets
```

```properties id="final-producer-config"
bootstrap.servers=${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS}
client.id=${SERVICE_NAME}-${HOSTNAME}-producer
```

## 15. Security Blueprint

```text id="security-blueprint"
Security layers:
  - TLS in transit
  - SASL / mTLS / IAM / OAuth authentication
  - ACL authorization
  - per-service identity
  - secret manager
  - topic-level least privilege
  - Schema Registry access control
  - DLQ restricted access
  - payload classification
```

### Least privilege example

| Principal | Permissions |
|---|---|
| `order-service` | Write `order.order.events.v1`; read/write its retry/DLQ if needed |
| `billing-service` | Read `order.order.events.v1`; write billing events |
| `order-outbox-connector` | Read DB, write order event topics |
| `ops-replay-tool` | Read DLQ, write replay topic, restricted |
| `admin-diagnostics` | Describe topic/group only |

Never:

```text id="security-never-final"
- shared Kafka credential across all services
- wildcard Write for app services
- public Connect REST API
- secrets in Docker image
- full payload logging in production
- broad DLQ read access
```

## 16. Observability Blueprint

```text id="observability-blueprint"
Every event flow must expose:
  - eventId
  - correlationId
  - eventType
  - eventVersion
  - topic
  - partition
  - offset
  - consumerGroup
  - processing latency
  - retry/DLQ status
  - outbox status
```

### Dashboard set

| Dashboard | Panels |
|---|---|
| Producer | send rate, error rate, latency, outbox pending age |
| Consumer | lag, lag by partition, processed rate, failure rate |
| Retry/DLQ | retry backlog, DLQ count, oldest unresolved |
| Outbox | pending, failed, oldest pending, publish latency |
| Debezium/Connect | connector state, task state, WAL retained, CDC lag |
| Kafka Streams | app state, process latency, state restore |
| Camunda saga | active instances, incidents, timeout, compensation |
| Kubernetes | pod restart, readiness, CPU/memory, shutdown duration |

### Promotion artifacts

| Artifact | Versioned? |
|---|---:|

## 19. Operational Runbook Map

| Alert | Primary runbook |
|---|---|
| Consumer lag rising | Lag spike |
| One partition lag high | Hot partition / poison event |
| DLQ spike | Contract/data failure |
| Retry backlog rising | Retry storm |
| Outbox pending age high | Outbox backlog |
| Connector FAILED | Kafka Connect / Debezium |
| WAL retained high | Debezium lag / slot issue |
| Duplicate side effect | Idempotency incident |
| Schema validation spike | Schema break |
| Rebalance loop | Consumer group instability |
| Producer publish failure | Producer/outbox issue |
| Sensitive payload in event | Security incident |

---

## 20. Failure Mode Blueprint

```text id="failure-mode-blueprint"
DB commit success + Kafka publish fail:
  solved by outbox

Kafka publish duplicate:
  solved by consumer idempotency

Consumer crash after DB side effect:
  solved by processed_event dedup

Bad schema:
  solved by schema gate + DLQ + rollback

Downstream unavailable:
  solved by retry topic + backoff + circuit breaker

Poison event:
  solved by DLQ/quarantine

Long-running process:
  solved by Camunda saga + compensation

Connector down:
  solved by task monitoring + replication slot/WAL monitoring

Deployment kills consumer:
  solved by graceful shutdown + safe offset commit
```

### Topic catalog example

```yaml id="topic-catalog-final"
topics:
  - name: order.order.events.v1
    owner: order-platform
    producer: order-service
    key: orderId
    partitions: 24
    cleanupPolicy: delete
    retention: 7d
    schemaSubject: order.order.events.v1-value
    compatibility: BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE
    classification: confidential
    consumers:
      - billing-service
      - search-indexer
      - order-projection-service
    dlq: order.order-events.dlq.v1
    runbook: order-kafka-runbook
```

## 24. Anti-Patterns to Block

| Anti-pattern | Why dangerous |
|---|---|
| Publish Kafka event inside request before DB commit | Ghost event |
| Direct publish for critical DB state without outbox | Lost event risk |
| Consumer auto-commit with DB side effect | Data loss |
| No idempotency table | Duplicate side effect |
| Random key for ordered aggregate lifecycle | Ordering broken |
| Key by tenant for high-volume tenant | Hot partition |
| Retry all exceptions | Retry storm |
| DLQ without owner/alert | Operational debt |
| Raw CDC as public business event | DB schema coupling |
| Camunda process stores full domain state | Split-brain state |
| Kafka Streams doing external side effects casually | Exactly-once boundary illusion |
| Schema compatibility disabled in prod | Contract break |
| Topic auto-create in prod | Wrong config silently |
| Public Kafka Connect REST API | Connector takeover risk |
| No graceful shutdown | Rebalance/duplicates |
| Replay without audit | Uncontrolled recovery |

---

## 25. Final Architecture Decision Matrix

| Need | Choose |
|---|---|
| REST command changes DB and emits event | PostgreSQL transaction + outbox |
| Publish event after DB commit reliably | Debezium Outbox Event Router or polling relay |
| Simple side-effect consumer | Plain KafkaConsumer + idempotency |
| Stateful stream aggregation | Kafka Streams |
| SQL-based stream transform | ksqlDB |
| Long-running business process | Camunda saga orchestration |
| DB CDC for analytics/search | Debezium raw CDC |
| Business event for other services | Outbox event, not raw CDC |
| Retry transient failure | Retry topic with backoff |
| Isolate bad payload | DLQ/quarantine |
| Rebuild projection | Replay with new group / controlled tool |
| Cross-service command | Command topic + commandId idempotency |
| Current-state lookup stream | Compacted topic / KTable |
| Production topic creation | IaC/topic catalog |

---

## 26. End-to-End Example: Order Flow

```text id="order-flow-final"
1. Client sends POST /orders
2. Order service validates request
3. PostgreSQL transaction:
     - insert order
     - insert order_item
     - insert outbox_event OrderCreated
4. Debezium emits Kafka record:
     topic = order.order.events.v1
     key = order-123
5. Billing consumer receives OrderCreated
6. Billing inserts processed_event(evt-001)
7. Billing creates billing projection
8. Billing commits Kafka offset
9. Search indexer consumes same event
10. Camunda process starts order fulfillment saga
11. Inventory reservation command emitted
12. Inventory replies InventoryReserved
13. Camunda correlates message and continues process
14. Observability connects all steps by correlationId
```

## 28. Final Summary

Blueprint final untuk stack Anda:

```text id="final-summary"
Java/Jersey:
  API and use case boundary

PostgreSQL/MyBatis:
  source of truth + transaction + outbox + idempotency tables

Kafka:
  durable event backbone with topic/key/schema governance

Debezium/Kafka Connect:
  reliable CDC/outbox publishing path

Consumers:
  idempotent processing + manual commit + retry/DLQ

Kafka Streams/ksqlDB:
  stream processing, aggregation, enrichment, materialized views

Camunda:
  long-running saga/process orchestration

Kubernetes:
  controlled rollout, readiness, graceful shutdown, resource governance

Observability:
  trace event from REST command to Kafka offset to side effect

Security/Governance:
  least privilege, schema compatibility, topic catalog, replay control
```

Invariant paling penting:

```text id="final-invariants"
1. State change and event intent must be committed atomically.
2. Kafka publication can be at-least-once; consumers must be idempotent.
3. Offset commit means the record is safely handled.
4. Event key must match ordering requirement.
5. Schema evolution must be governed.
6. Retry only transient failures.
7. DLQ must be owned, monitored, secured, and replayable.
8. Camunda orchestrates process state, not service-local domain state.
9. Kubernetes shutdown must protect offset correctness.
10. Every event must be traceable by eventId and correlationId.
```

7/15/2026, 1:36:19 PM

Saya akan rangkum sebagai **cheatsheet referensi praktis**: Kafka Client biasa, Kafka Streams, dan ksqlDB Java Client. Saya akan fokus ke class/API/config yang paling sering dipakai di production Java/Jersey, bukan seluruh API internal Kafka.

# Cheatsheet - Java Kafka Client API  
## Kafka biasa, Kafka Streams, dan ksqlDB Java Client

> Fokus: **Java SE 17+**, Maven, Jersey/JAX-RS microservice, PostgreSQL/outbox, Kubernetes-ready.  
> Catatan penting: **Kafka Java Client native hampir tidak memakai annotation**. API Kafka lebih banyak berbasis **class, interface, method, `Properties`, dan config key**. Annotation seperti `@KafkaListener` adalah milik **Spring Kafka**, bukan Apache Kafka Java Client native.

---

# 1. Maven Artifacts

## 1.1 Kafka biasa: Producer, Consumer, Admin

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.apache.kafka</groupId>
  <artifactId>kafka-clients</artifactId>
  <version>${kafka.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

`kafka-clients` berisi API utama producer, consumer, admin, serializer/deserializer, common type, exception, metric, dan protocol client. Kafka 4.3 adalah rilis Apache Kafka yang diumumkan pada 22 Mei 2026, dan dokumentasi konfigurasi 4.3 mencakup producer, consumer/share consumer, admin, topic, dan Streams config. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/blog/2026/05/22/apache-kafka-4.3.0-release-announcement/?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

## 1.2 Kafka Streams

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.apache.kafka</groupId>
  <artifactId>kafka-streams</artifactId>
  <version>${kafka.version}</version>
</dependency>

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.apache.kafka</groupId>
  <artifactId>kafka-streams-test-utils</artifactId>
  <version>${kafka.version}</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

Kafka Streams adalah library Java/Scala untuk stream processing; topology dapat dibuat dengan **Streams DSL** atau **Processor API**. Dokumentasi Apache menyebut DSL sebagai API high-level untuk operasi umum seperti `map`, `filter`, `join`, dan aggregation, sedangkan Processor API memberi kontrol lebih rendah atas processor dan state store. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/42/streams/developer-guide/write-streams-app/))

## 1.3 ksqlDB Java Client

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.confluent.ksql</groupId>
  <artifactId>ksqldb-api-client</artifactId>
  <version>${ksqldb.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

ksqlDB Java Client menyediakan `Client`, `ClientOptions`, `streamQuery()`, `executeQuery()`, `executeStatement()`, `insertInto()`, `streamInserts()`, list/describe metadata, dan connector operations. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/ksqldb/developer-guide/java-client/java-client.html))

# 2. Annotation Availability

| Area | Annotation native Kafka? | Catatan |
|---|---:|---|
| Kafka Producer | Tidak umum | Pakai `KafkaProducer`, `ProducerRecord`, `Properties` |
| Kafka Consumer | Tidak umum | Pakai `KafkaConsumer`, `subscribe`, `poll`, `commitSync` |
| Kafka Admin | Tidak umum | Pakai `Admin`, `NewTopic`, `ConfigResource` |
| Kafka Streams | Tidak umum | Pakai `StreamsBuilder`, `KStream`, `KTable`, `Topology` |
| ksqlDB Java Client | Tidak umum | Pakai `Client`, `ClientOptions`, SQL string |
| Spring Kafka | Ya | `@KafkaListener`, `@KafkaHandler`, `@EnableKafka`; **bukan native Apache Kafka Client** |
| Jakarta/Jersey integration | Ya di Jersey side | `@Path`, `@GET`, `@POST`, `@Provider`, bukan Kafka |

Practical rule:

```text
Native Kafka Java Client:
  class + interface + method + Properties

Spring Kafka:
  annotation-driven

Jersey/JAX-RS:
  annotation-driven HTTP layer, Kafka tetap class/config-driven
```

# 4. Kafka Producer - Classes

| Class / Interface | Fungsi |
|---|---|
| `KafkaProducer<K,V>` | Client utama untuk publish record |
| `Producer<K,V>` | Interface producer |
| `ProducerRecord<K,V>` | Record yang dikirim ke topic |
| `RecordMetadata` | Metadata hasil send: topic, partition, offset, timestamp |
| `Callback` | Callback async setelah send success/fail |
| `ProducerConfig` | Constant config key producer |
| `ProducerInterceptor<K,V>` | Intercept/mutate record sebelum publish |
| `Serializer<T>` | Convert object ke byte[] |
| `StringSerializer` | Serializer string |
| `ByteArraySerializer` | Serializer byte array |
| `IntegerSerializer`, `LongSerializer`, etc. | Serializer primitive wrapper |
| `Partitioner` | Custom partitioning strategy |
| `TransactionManager` internal | Jangan dipakai langsung |
| `KafkaException` | Base runtime exception Kafka |
| `RetriableException` | Failure yang mungkin retriable |
| `TimeoutException` | Timeout request/delivery |
| `RecordTooLargeException` | Record terlalu besar |
| `TopicAuthorizationException` | ACL topic denied |
| `SerializationException` | Serialization failed |

`ProducerRecord` merepresentasikan key/value pair yang dikirim ke Kafka, berisi topic, optional partition, optional key, dan value. `KafkaProducer.send(record, callback)` mengirim record secara async dan callback menerima `RecordMetadata` atau exception; metadata berisi partition, offset, dan timestamp. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/25/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/ProducerRecord.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 5. Kafka Producer - Important Methods

## 5.1 `KafkaProducer`

| Method | Fungsi | Production note |
|---|---|---|
| `send(ProducerRecord<K,V> record)` | Async send tanpa callback eksplisit | Kurang recommended untuk event penting |
| `send(record, Callback callback)` | Async send + handle result | Recommended |
| `flush()` | Block sampai buffered records terkirim | Gunakan saat shutdown/checkpoint |
| `close()` | Close producer | Wajib saat shutdown |
| `close(Duration timeout)` | Close dengan timeout | Cocok Kubernetes shutdown |
| `partitionsFor(String topic)` | Metadata partition topic | Bisa untuk diagnostics |
| `metrics()` | Client metrics | Export ke observability |
| `initTransactions()` | Init transactional producer | Untuk Kafka transaction |
| `beginTransaction()` | Mulai transaction Kafka | Kafka-to-Kafka use case |
| `sendOffsetsToTransaction(...)` | Commit offsets dalam Kafka transaction | Kafka transaction boundary |
| `commitTransaction()` | Commit Kafka transaction | Bukan DB transaction |
| `abortTransaction()` | Abort Kafka transaction | Error recovery |

# 6. Kafka Producer - Config Properties

Apache Kafka 4.3 producer config mendefinisikan `bootstrap.servers`, `key.serializer`, `value.serializer`, `buffer.memory`, `compression.type`, `retries`, `acks`, `enable.idempotence`, `max.in.flight.requests.per.connection`, dan security config seperti `security.protocol`, SSL, dan SASL. Dokumentasi 4.3 menyebut `acks` default `all`, `enable.idempotence` default `true` bila tidak ada config konflik, dan compression valid: `none`, `gzip`, `snappy`, `lz4`, `zstd`. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/configuration/producer-configs/))

| Property | Constant | Fungsi | Recommended baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bootstrap.servers` | `ProducerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG` | Broker bootstrap | wajib |
| `client.id` | `CLIENT_ID_CONFIG` | Identitas client | service-pod-producer |
| `key.serializer` | `KEY_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG` | Serializer key | `StringSerializer` |
| `value.serializer` | `VALUE_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG` | Serializer value | JSON/Avro/Protobuf |
| `acks` | `ACKS_CONFIG` | Durability ack | `all` |
| `enable.idempotence` | `ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCE_CONFIG` | Idempotent producer | `true` |
| `retries` | `RETRIES_CONFIG` | Retry transient failure | biarkan default / high |
| `delivery.timeout.ms` | `DELIVERY_TIMEOUT_MS_CONFIG` | Batas total delivery | `120000` |
| `request.timeout.ms` | `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS_CONFIG` | Timeout request | `30000` |
| `linger.ms` | `LINGER_MS_CONFIG` | Delay batching | `5`-`20` |
| `batch.size` | `BATCH_SIZE_CONFIG` | Batch per partition | `16384` / `32768` / `65536` |
| `compression.type` | `COMPRESSION_TYPE_CONFIG` | Compression | `lz4` atau `zstd` |
| `buffer.memory` | `BUFFER_MEMORY_CONFIG` | Buffer producer | default 32MiB atau tuned |
| `max.block.ms` | `MAX_BLOCK_MS_CONFIG` | Block saat metadata/buffer | `5000`-`60000` |
| `max.request.size` | `MAX_REQUEST_SIZE_CONFIG` | Max request size | align broker/topic |
| `max.in.flight.requests.per.connection` | `MAX_IN_FLIGHT_REQUESTS_PER_CONNECTION` | In-flight request | `<=5` dengan idempotence |
| `transactional.id` | `TRANSACTIONAL_ID_CONFIG` | Transactional producer | hanya jika Kafka transaction |
| `security.protocol` | `CommonClientConfigs.SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG` | PLAINTEXT/SSL/SASL_SSL | `SASL_SSL` prod |
| `sasl.mechanism` | `SaslConfigs.SASL_MECHANISM` | SCRAM/OAUTH/etc | platform-specific |
| `sasl.jaas.config` | `SaslConfigs.SASL_JAAS_CONFIG` | JAAS config | secret-managed |
| `ssl.truststore.location` | `SslConfigs.SSL_TRUSTSTORE_LOCATION_CONFIG` | Truststore path | prod |
| `ssl.endpoint.identification.algorithm` | `SslConfigs.SSL_ENDPOINT_IDENTIFICATION_ALGORITHM_CONFIG` | Hostname verification | `https` |

### Producer baseline

```properties
bootstrap.servers=kafka-1:9093,kafka-2:9093,kafka-3:9093
client.id=order-service-${HOSTNAME}-producer
key.serializer=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer
value.serializer=org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.StringSerializer

acks=all
enable.idempotence=true
compression.type=lz4
linger.ms=5
batch.size=32768
delivery.timeout.ms=120000
request.timeout.ms=30000
max.block.ms=5000

security.protocol=SASL_SSL
sasl.mechanism=SCRAM-SHA-512
```

# 7. Kafka Producer - Code Skeleton

```java
Properties props = new Properties();
props.put(ProducerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, bootstrapServers);
props.put(ProducerConfig.CLIENT_ID_CONFIG, "order-service-" + hostname + "-producer");
props.put(ProducerConfig.KEY_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringSerializer.class.getName());
props.put(ProducerConfig.VALUE_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringSerializer.class.getName());
props.put(ProducerConfig.ACKS_CONFIG, "all");
props.put(ProducerConfig.ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCE_CONFIG, "true");
props.put(ProducerConfig.COMPRESSION_TYPE_CONFIG, "lz4");

KafkaProducer<String, String> producer = new KafkaProducer<>(props);

ProducerRecord<String, String> record =
        new ProducerRecord<>("order.order.events.v1", "order-123", payloadJson);

record.headers()
        .add("event-id", eventId.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))
        .add("event-type", "OrderCreated".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8))
        .add("correlation-id", correlationId.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

producer.send(record, (metadata, exception) -> {
    if (exception == null) {
        log.info("published topic={} partition={} offset={}",
                metadata.topic(), metadata.partition(), metadata.offset());
    } else {
        log.error("publish failed topic={} key={}", record.topic(), record.key(), exception);
    }
});
```

| `OffsetOutOfRangeException` | Offset tidak valid/expired |
| `NoOffsetForPartitionException` | Offset tidak ada dan reset none |

`KafkaConsumer` adalah client untuk membaca record dari Kafka dan berinteraksi dengan broker untuk consumer group load balancing. Dokumentasi Kafka juga menegaskan consumer tidak thread-safe; `wakeup()` adalah pola umum untuk menghentikan consumer dari thread lain saat shutdown. ([Javadoc](https://javadoc.io/doc/org.apache.kafka/kafka-clients/latest/org/apache/kafka/clients/consumer/KafkaConsumer.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 10. Kafka Consumer - Config Properties

Kafka 4.3 consumer config mencakup `bootstrap.servers`, `key.deserializer`, `value.deserializer`, `group.id`, `group.protocol`, `heartbeat.interval.ms`, `session.timeout.ms`, `auto.offset.reset`, `enable.auto.commit`, `group.instance.id`, `isolation.level`, `max.poll.interval.ms`, `max.poll.records`, dan `partition.assignment.strategy`. Dokumentasi 4.3 juga mencatat `auto.offset.reset` mendukung `earliest`, `latest`, `none`, dan `by_duration:<duration>`; `enable.auto.commit` default `true`; `max.poll.records` default 500; dan default assignment list adalah `RangeAssignor, CooperativeStickyAssignor`. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/configuration/consumer-configs/))

| Property | Constant | Fungsi | Recommended baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bootstrap.servers` | `ConsumerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG` | Bootstrap broker | wajib |
| `client.id` | `CLIENT_ID_CONFIG` | Identitas client | service-pod-consumer |
| `group.id` | `GROUP_ID_CONFIG` | Consumer group | stable per service |
| `key.deserializer` | `KEY_DESERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG` | Key deserializer | `StringDeserializer` |
| `value.deserializer` | `VALUE_DESERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG` | Value deserializer | JSON/Avro/Protobuf |
| `enable.auto.commit` | `ENABLE_AUTO_COMMIT_CONFIG` | Auto commit offset | `false` untuk business |
| `auto.offset.reset` | `AUTO_OFFSET_RESET_CONFIG` | Jika offset tidak ada | `earliest` / `latest` / `none` |
| `max.poll.records` | `MAX_POLL_RECORDS_CONFIG` | Record per poll | 50-1000 |
| `max.poll.interval.ms` | `MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS_CONFIG` | Max delay antar poll | default 5 menit |
| `session.timeout.ms` | `SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS_CONFIG` | Failure detection classic group | default 45s |
| `heartbeat.interval.ms` | `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS_CONFIG` | Heartbeat interval classic | default 3s |
| `fetch.min.bytes` | `FETCH_MIN_BYTES_CONFIG` | Minimum fetch response | throughput tuning |
| `fetch.max.wait.ms` | `FETCH_MAX_WAIT_MS_CONFIG` | Max wait fetch | latency/throughput |
| `fetch.max.bytes` | `FETCH_MAX_BYTES_CONFIG` | Max fetch response | large message |
| `max.partition.fetch.bytes` | `MAX_PARTITION_FETCH_BYTES_CONFIG` | Max per partition fetch | large message |
| `isolation.level` | `ISOLATION_LEVEL_CONFIG` | Transaction visibility | `read_committed` if needed |

| `group.instance.id` | `GROUP_INSTANCE_ID_CONFIG` | Static membership | StatefulSet/stable identity |
| `allow.auto.create.topics` | `ALLOW_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_CONFIG` | Auto create on subscribe | `false` prod |

# 11. Kafka Consumer - Code Skeleton

```java
Properties props = new Properties();
props.put(ConsumerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, bootstrapServers);
props.put(ConsumerConfig.CLIENT_ID_CONFIG, "order-projection-" + hostname);
props.put(ConsumerConfig.GROUP_ID_CONFIG, "order-projection-service");
props.put(ConsumerConfig.KEY_DESERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringDeserializer.class.getName());
props.put(ConsumerConfig.VALUE_DESERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringDeserializer.class.getName());
props.put(ConsumerConfig.ENABLE_AUTO_COMMIT_CONFIG, "false");
props.put(ConsumerConfig.AUTO_OFFSET_RESET_CONFIG, "earliest");
props.put(ConsumerConfig.MAX_POLL_RECORDS_CONFIG, "200");

KafkaConsumer<String, String> consumer = new KafkaConsumer<>(props);

consumer.subscribe(
        List.of("order.order.events.v1"),
        new ConsumerRebalanceListener() {
            @Override
            public void onPartitionsRevoked(Collection<TopicPartition> partitions) {
                consumer.commitSync(safeOffsetsFor(partitions));
            }

            @Override
            public void onPartitionsAssigned(Collection<TopicPartition> partitions) {
                initializeState(partitions);
            }

            @Override
            public void onPartitionsLost(Collection<TopicPartition> partitions) {
                cleanupLocalState(partitions);
            }
        }
);

while (running.get()) {
    ConsumerRecords<String, String> records = consumer.poll(Duration.ofMillis(1000));

    for (ConsumerRecord<String, String> record : records) {
        handleIdempotently(record);
        markProcessed(record);
    }

    consumer.commitSync(safeOffsets());
}
```

# 14. Serialization / Deserialization / Serde

| Interface / Class | Area | Fungsi |
|---|---|---|
| `Serializer<T>` | Producer | Object → byte[] |
| `Deserializer<T>` | Consumer | byte[] → object |
| `Serde<T>` | Streams | Serializer + Deserializer |
| `Serdes` | Streams/Common | Factory built-in Serde |
| `StringSerializer` / `StringDeserializer` | Common | String |
| `ByteArraySerializer` / `ByteArrayDeserializer` | Common | byte[] |
| `IntegerSerializer`, `LongSerializer`, etc. | Common | Primitive wrapper |
| `UUIDSerializer` / `UUIDDeserializer` | Common | UUID |
| Custom serializer | Producer | JSON custom |
| Custom deserializer | Consumer | JSON custom |
| Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema SerDe | Confluent | Schema Registry integration |

### Custom serializer skeleton

```java
public final class JsonSerializer<T> implements Serializer<T> {
    private final ObjectMapper objectMapper = new ObjectMapper();

    @Override
    public byte[] serialize(String topic, T data) {
        try {
            return objectMapper.writeValueAsBytes(data);
        } catch (JsonProcessingException e) {
            throw new SerializationException("JSON serialization failed", e);
        }
    }
}
```

### Header extraction

```java
static Optional<String> header(ConsumerRecord<?, ?> record, String name) {
    Header header = record.headers().lastHeader(name);
    if (header == null) {
        return Optional.empty();
    }
    return Optional.of(new String(header.value(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
}
```

### Processor skeleton

```java
public final class DedupProcessor
        implements Processor<String, OrderEvent, String, OrderEvent> {

    private ProcessorContext<String, OrderEvent> context;
    private KeyValueStore<String, Long> seen;

    @Override
    public void init(ProcessorContext<String, OrderEvent> context) {
        this.context = context;
        this.seen = context.getStateStore("seen-event-store");
    }

    @Override
    public void process(Record<String, OrderEvent> record) {
        String eventId = record.value().eventId();

        if (seen.get(eventId) != null) {
            return;
        }

        seen.put(eventId, record.timestamp());
        context.forward(record);
    }

    @Override
    public void close() {
    }
}
```

Confluent Streams config reference menjelaskan `application.id` digunakan sebagai prefix client-id, group-id, dan changelog topic prefix; `state.dir` adalah lokasi state store; dan `default.key.serde` / `default.value.serde` adalah default serializer/deserializer. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/streams-configs.html))

| Property | Constant | Fungsi | Baseline |

| `client.id` | `CLIENT_ID_CONFIG` | Client prefix | service-pod |

| `commit.interval.ms` | `COMMIT_INTERVAL_MS_CONFIG` | Commit interval | lower for latency |
| `cache.max.bytes.buffering` | `CACHE_MAX_BYTES_BUFFERING_CONFIG` | Cache across threads | tuned |
| `num.standby.replicas` | `NUM_STANDBY_REPLICAS_CONFIG` | Standby task count | 0/1+ |

# 23. Kafka Streams - Code Skeleton

```java
Properties props = new Properties();
props.put(StreamsConfig.APPLICATION_ID_CONFIG, "order-summary-streams");
props.put(StreamsConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, bootstrapServers);
props.put(StreamsConfig.DEFAULT_KEY_SERDE_CLASS_CONFIG, Serdes.String().getClass());
props.put(StreamsConfig.DEFAULT_VALUE_SERDE_CLASS_CONFIG, orderEventSerde.getClass());
props.put(StreamsConfig.STATE_DIR_CONFIG, "/var/lib/kafka-streams/order-summary");

StreamsBuilder builder = new StreamsBuilder();

KStream<String, OrderEvent> orders =
        builder.stream(
                "order.order.events.v1",
                Consumed.with(Serdes.String(), orderEventSerde)
        );

orders
    .filter((key, event) -> event.eventType().equals("OrderCreated"))
    .groupByKey(Grouped.with(Serdes.String(), orderEventSerde))
    .count(Materialized.as("order-created-count-store"))
    .toStream()
    .to(
        "order.order-created-counts.v1",
        Produced.with(Serdes.String(), Serdes.Long())
    );

KafkaStreams streams = new KafkaStreams(builder.build(), props);

streams.setStateListener((newState, oldState) ->
        log.info("streams state changed old={} new={}", oldState, newState));

streams.setUncaughtExceptionHandler(exception -> {
    log.error("streams fatal error", exception);
    return StreamsUncaughtExceptionHandler.StreamThreadExceptionResponse.SHUTDOWN_APPLICATION;
});

streams.start();

Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(() ->
        streams.close(Duration.ofSeconds(30))));
```

| `client.close()` | Close connections |

Confluent docs menunjukkan `ClientOptions.create().setHost(...).setPort(...)`, lalu `Client.create(options)`; untuk Confluent Cloud, contoh memakai `setBasicAuthCredentials`, `setHost`, `setPort(443)`, `setUseTls(true)`, dan `setUseAlpn(true)`. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/ksqldb/developer-guide/java-client/java-client.html))

### ksqlDB client skeleton

```java
ClientOptions options = ClientOptions.create()
        .setHost("ksqldb.internal")
        .setPort(8088)
        .setUseTls(false);

Client client = Client.create(options);

try {
    ServerInfo serverInfo = client.serverInfo().get();
    log.info("ksqlDB version={}", serverInfo.getServerVersion());
} finally {
    client.close();
}
```

# 27. ksqlDB Java Client - Important Methods

## 27.1 Query methods

| Method | Fungsi | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| `streamQuery(String sql)` | Streaming row-by-row result | Push query |
| `streamQuery(sql, properties)` | Streaming + query properties | `auto.offset.reset` |
| `executeQuery(String sql)` | Batch result after query completes | Pull query / terminating push |
| `executeQuery(sql, properties)` | Batch + properties | Pull query |
| `terminatePushQuery(String queryId)` | Stop push query | Cleanup |
| `executeStatement(String sql)` | DDL/DML persistent statement | CREATE/DROP/CSAS/CTAS |
| `executeStatement(sql, properties)` | Statement + query properties | persistent from earliest |

`streamQuery()` cocok untuk push query dan bisa mengembalikan row satu per satu secara async via Reactive Streams subscriber atau sync via `poll()`. `executeQuery()` cocok untuk pull query atau push query yang terminating, misalnya memakai `LIMIT`; untuk push query non-terminating, gunakan `streamQuery()`. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/ksqldb/developer-guide/java-client/java-client.html))

## 27.2 Insert methods

| Method | Fungsi |
|---|---|
| `insertInto(String streamName, KsqlObject row)` | Insert satu row |
| `streamInserts(String streamName)` | Streaming inserts |
| `streamInserts(streamName, properties)` | Streaming inserts + properties |

## 27.3 Metadata/admin methods

| Method | Fungsi |
|---|---|
| `listStreams()` | List ksqlDB streams |
| `listTables()` | List ksqlDB tables |
| `listTopics()` | List Kafka topics visible to ksqlDB |
| `listQueries()` | List running queries |
| `describeSource(String)` | Describe stream/table |
| `serverInfo()` | ksqlDB server metadata |
| `createConnector(...)` | Create connector via ksqlDB |
| `dropConnector(...)` | Drop connector |
| `listConnectors()` | List connectors |
| `describeConnector(...)` | Connector details |
| `define(name, value)` | Define variable |
| `undefine(name)` | Remove variable |
| `getVariables()` | Current variables |
| `assertTopic(...)` | Assert topic existence |
| `assertSchema(...)` | Assert schema existence |
| `buildRequest(method, path)` | Low-level REST request |

ksqlDB Java Client mendukung list streams/tables/topics/queries, `describeSource()` untuk metadata stream/table, `serverInfo()` untuk metadata server, connector operations, session variables, dan `assertTopic`/`assertSchema`. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/ksqldb/developer-guide/java-client/java-client.html))

# 28. ksqlDB Java Client - Query Examples

## 28.1 Create stream

```java
String sql = """
    CREATE STREAM ORDERS (
        ORDER_ID STRING KEY,
        CUSTOMER_ID STRING,
        STATUS STRING
    ) WITH (
        KAFKA_TOPIC='order.order.events.v1',
        VALUE_FORMAT='JSON'
    );
    """;

client.executeStatement(sql).get();
```

## 28.2 Push query

```java
StreamedQueryResult result =
        client.streamQuery("""
            SELECT ORDER_ID, STATUS
            FROM ORDERS
            EMIT CHANGES;
            """).get();

Row row = result.poll(Duration.ofSeconds(5));
if (row != null) {
    String orderId = row.getString("ORDER_ID");
    String status = row.getString("STATUS");
}
```

## 28.3 Pull query

```java
BatchedQueryResult result =
        client.executeQuery("""
            SELECT * FROM ORDER_SUMMARY
            WHERE ORDER_ID = 'order-123';
            """);

List<Row> rows = result.get();
```

## 28.4 Persistent query

```java
Map<String, Object> queryProps = Map.of("auto.offset.reset", "earliest");

ExecuteStatementResult result =
        client.executeStatement("""
            CREATE TABLE ORDERS_BY_STATUS AS
            SELECT STATUS, COUNT(*) AS CNT
            FROM ORDERS
            GROUP BY STATUS
            EMIT CHANGES;
            """, queryProps).get();

Optional<String> queryId = result.queryId();
```

# 29. ksqlDB SQL Properties / WITH Properties

| Property | Area | Fungsi |
|---|---|---|
| `KAFKA_TOPIC` | stream/table | Topic backing |
| `VALUE_FORMAT` | stream/table | JSON, AVRO, PROTOBUF, etc. |
| `KEY_FORMAT` | stream/table | Key format |
| `PARTITIONS` | create source | Topic partitions |
| `REPLICAS` | create source | Topic replication |
| `TIMESTAMP` | stream/table | Event time column |
| `TIMESTAMP_FORMAT` | stream/table | Timestamp parsing |
| `WRAP_SINGLE_VALUE` | serialization | Single field handling |
| `KEY_SCHEMA_ID` | Schema Registry | Explicit key schema id |
| `VALUE_SCHEMA_ID` | Schema Registry | Explicit value schema id |

## Query properties

| Property | Fungsi |
|---|---|
| `auto.offset.reset=earliest` | Query starts from earliest for push/persistent |
| `ksql.streams.auto.offset.reset` | Server/statement behavior depending context |
| `ksql.query.pull.table.scan.enabled` | Allow table scan for pull queries, if configured |
| `ksql.query.push.v2.enabled` | Push query behavior, version dependent |
| `ksql.persistence.wrap.single.values` | Serialization behavior |

Practical note: untuk Java service production, jangan jadikan ksqlDB sebagai hidden business logic tanpa version control. Simpan SQL query sebagai artifact, review di PR, dan deploy melalui pipeline.

# 30. Exception & Error Handling Cheat Sheet

| Exception / Error | Area | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SerializationException` | Producer/Consumer | Serialization/deserialization failed | DLQ/fail fast |
| `TimeoutException` | Producer/Admin | Request/delivery timeout | retry/backoff |
| `RetriableException` | Common | Retriable Kafka error | retry |
| `RecordTooLargeException` | Producer | Payload too large | redesign payload |
| `TopicAuthorizationException` | Producer/Consumer/Admin | ACL denied | fix ACL, do not retry forever |
| `GroupAuthorizationException` | Consumer | Group ACL denied | fix ACL |
| `UnknownTopicOrPartitionException` | Producer/Admin | Topic missing/metadata issue | provision topic |
| `CommitFailedException` | Consumer | Commit failed due rebalance/ownership | fix poll/rebalance |
| `WakeupException` | Consumer | Shutdown interrupt | expected during close |
| `OffsetOutOfRangeException` | Consumer | Offset expired/invalid | replay/reset decision |
| `ConfigException` | Common | Invalid config | fail startup |
| `StreamsException` | Streams | Streams runtime failure | state handler |
| `TaskMigratedException` | Streams | Task moved/rebalance | usually handled by Streams |
| `InvalidStateStoreException` | Streams | Store not queryable | readiness/store routing |
| ksqlDB failed `CompletableFuture` | ksqlDB | Server non-200/error | handle async failure |

# 32. Native Kafka vs Streams vs ksqlDB Decision

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Publish integration event | `KafkaProducer` or outbox relay |
| Consume event and write DB | `KafkaConsumer` |
| Inspect/create topics/config/group lag | `Admin` |
| Join stream with table | Kafka Streams |
| Stateful aggregation/windowing in Java | Kafka Streams |
| Materialized state query in Java | Kafka Streams Interactive Queries |
| SQL filter/router/aggregation | ksqlDB |
| Pull query over materialized view | ksqlDB Java Client |
| Manage persistent streaming SQL | ksqlDB `executeStatement()` |
| Production critical DB-originated event | PostgreSQL outbox + Debezium/relay |
| Long-running business process | Camunda + Kafka commands/events |

# 35. Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Dampak |
|---|---|
| Mengira Kafka native punya annotation seperti Spring | Salah abstraction |
| `KafkaProducer` dibuat per request | Overhead tinggi |
| Producer callback diabaikan | Failure silent |
| Critical event direct publish tanpa outbox | Lost event risk |
| Consumer `enable.auto.commit=true` untuk DB side effect | Data loss |
| Commit offset sebelum side effect sukses | Data loss |
| Satu `KafkaConsumer` dipakai multi-thread | Unsafe |
| Random key untuk aggregate lifecycle | Ordering hilang |
| `max.poll.records` besar tanpa menghitung processing time | Rebalance loop |
| Retry semua exception | Retry storm |
| DLQ tanpa metadata/owner | Tidak bisa recovery |
| Kafka Streams untuk external side effect langsung | Exactly-once illusion |
| ksqlDB query ad-hoc tanpa version control | Hidden production logic |
| Topic auto-create di production | Config drift |
| PLAINTEXT di production | Security risk |

# Cheatsheet - Kafka Client Code Templates untuk Jersey/JAX-RS Production Style

## 0. Scope

Template ini berisi pola class yang bisa Anda adaptasi untuk:

```text id="scope"
1. KafkaProducerManager
2. KafkaConsumerWorker
3. OffsetTracker
4. FailureClassifier
5. RetryPublisher
6. DlqPublisher
7. AdminDiagnosticsService
8. AdminDiagnosticsResource untuk Jersey/JAX-RS
9. KafkaStreamsLifecycleManager
10. KsqlDbClientService
11. Config factories
12. Graceful shutdown pattern
```

Catatan penting: native Apache Kafka Client memakai **class, interface, method, dan config**, bukan annotation-driven seperti Spring Kafka. Untuk producer, API `send(record, callback)` menyediakan async completion handling, `flush()` menunggu buffered records terkirim, dan `metrics()` membuka client metrics. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/Producer.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 3. Common Config Model

Gunakan config object sendiri agar tidak menyebar `System.getenv()` ke seluruh codebase.

```java id="common-config"
public record KafkaCommonConfig(
        String bootstrapServers,
        String securityProtocol,
        String saslMechanism,
        String saslJaasConfig,
        String sslTruststoreLocation,
        String sslTruststorePassword,
        String clientIdPrefix,
        String environment
) {
    public boolean isProduction() {
        return "prod".equalsIgnoreCase(environment);
    }
}
```

# 4. Producer Config Factory

```java id="producer-config-factory"
public final class KafkaProducerConfigFactory {
    private final KafkaCommonConfig common;

    public KafkaProducerConfigFactory(KafkaCommonConfig common) {
        this.common = common;
    }

    public Properties create(String clientName) {
        Properties props = new Properties();

        props.put(ProducerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, common.bootstrapServers());
        props.put(ProducerConfig.CLIENT_ID_CONFIG, common.clientIdPrefix() + "-" + clientName);

        props.put(ProducerConfig.KEY_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringSerializer.class.getName());
        props.put(ProducerConfig.VALUE_SERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringSerializer.class.getName());

        props.put(ProducerConfig.ACKS_CONFIG, "all");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCE_CONFIG, "true");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.COMPRESSION_TYPE_CONFIG, "lz4");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.LINGER_MS_CONFIG, "5");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.BATCH_SIZE_CONFIG, "32768");

        props.put(ProducerConfig.DELIVERY_TIMEOUT_MS_CONFIG, "120000");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS_CONFIG, "30000");
        props.put(ProducerConfig.MAX_BLOCK_MS_CONFIG, "5000");

        applySecurity(props);

        validate(props);

        return props;
    }

    private void applySecurity(Properties props) {
        if (common.securityProtocol() == null || common.securityProtocol().isBlank()) {
            return;
        }

        props.put(CommonClientConfigs.SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG, common.securityProtocol());

        if (common.saslMechanism() != null && !common.saslMechanism().isBlank()) {
            props.put(SaslConfigs.SASL_MECHANISM, common.saslMechanism());
            props.put(SaslConfigs.SASL_JAAS_CONFIG, common.saslJaasConfig());
        }

        if (common.sslTruststoreLocation() != null && !common.sslTruststoreLocation().isBlank()) {
            props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_TRUSTSTORE_LOCATION_CONFIG, common.sslTruststoreLocation());
            props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD_CONFIG, common.sslTruststorePassword());
            props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_ENDPOINT_IDENTIFICATION_ALGORITHM_CONFIG, "https");
        }
    }

    private void validate(Properties props) {
        if (common.isProduction()) {
            String protocol = String.valueOf(props.get(CommonClientConfigs.SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG));

            if ("PLAINTEXT".equals(protocol) || "SASL_PLAINTEXT".equals(protocol)) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("Insecure Kafka protocol is forbidden in production: " + protocol);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

Producer config penting di production biasanya meliputi `acks=all`, idempotence, timeout, batching, compression, dan security. Kafka 4.3 mendokumentasikan producer config seperti `acks`, `enable.idempotence`, `delivery.timeout.ms`, `request.timeout.ms`, `linger.ms`, `batch.size`, dan `compression.type`. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/KafkaProducer.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 5. Event Header Helper

```java id="event-headers"
public final class EventHeaders {
    public static final String EVENT_ID = "event-id";
    public static final String EVENT_TYPE = "event-type";
    public static final String EVENT_VERSION = "event-version";
    public static final String CORRELATION_ID = "correlation-id";
    public static final String CAUSATION_ID = "causation-id";
    public static final String TENANT_ID = "tenant-id";
    public static final String PRODUCER = "producer";
    public static final String TRACEPARENT = "traceparent";

    private EventHeaders() {
    }

    public static void add(Headers headers, String name, String value) {
        if (value == null || value.isBlank()) {
            return;
        }

        headers.add(name, value.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }

    public static Optional<String> get(Headers headers, String name) {
        Header header = headers.lastHeader(name);

        if (header == null) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }

        return Optional.of(new String(header.value(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }
}
```

# 7. KafkaProducerManager

Pattern: producer dibuat **singleton per service**, bukan per request. `send()` async, callback wajib menangani success/failure.

```java id="kafka-producer-manager"
@Singleton
public final class KafkaProducerManager implements AutoCloseable {
    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(KafkaProducerManager.class);

    private final KafkaProducer<String, String> producer;
    private final AtomicBoolean closed = new AtomicBoolean(false);

    @Inject
    public KafkaProducerManager(KafkaProducerConfigFactory configFactory) {
        this.producer = new KafkaProducer<>(configFactory.create("producer"));
    }

    public CompletionStage<RecordMetadata> publish(PublishedEvent event) {
        if (closed.get()) {
            CompletableFuture<RecordMetadata> failed = new CompletableFuture<>();
            failed.completeExceptionally(new IllegalStateException("Kafka producer is already closed"));
            return failed;
        }

        ProducerRecord<String, String> record =
                new ProducerRecord<>(event.topic(), event.key(), event.payloadJson());

        EventHeaders.add(record.headers(), EventHeaders.EVENT_ID, event.eventId());
        EventHeaders.add(record.headers(), EventHeaders.EVENT_TYPE, event.eventType());
        EventHeaders.add(record.headers(), EventHeaders.EVENT_VERSION, String.valueOf(event.eventVersion()));
        EventHeaders.add(record.headers(), EventHeaders.CORRELATION_ID, event.correlationId());
        EventHeaders.add(record.headers(), EventHeaders.CAUSATION_ID, event.causationId());
        EventHeaders.add(record.headers(), EventHeaders.TENANT_ID, event.tenantId());
        EventHeaders.add(record.headers(), EventHeaders.PRODUCER, event.producer());

        CompletableFuture<RecordMetadata> result = new CompletableFuture<>();

        producer.send(record, (metadata, exception) -> {
            if (exception == null) {
                log.info(
                        "Kafka event published topic={} partition={} offset={} key={} eventId={} eventType={} correlationId={}",
                        metadata.topic(),
                        metadata.partition(),
                        metadata.offset(),
                        event.key(),
                        event.eventId(),
                        event.eventType(),
                        event.correlationId()
                );

                result.complete(metadata);
                return;
            }

            log.error(
                    "Kafka event publish failed topic={} key={} eventId={} eventType={} correlationId={} errorClass={}",
                    event.topic(),
                    event.key(),
                    event.eventId(),
                    event.eventType(),
                    event.correlationId(),
                    exception.getClass().getSimpleName(),
                    exception
            );

            result.completeExceptionally(exception);
        });

        return result;
    }

    public Map<MetricName, ? extends Metric> metrics() {
        return producer.metrics();
    }

    @Override
    public void close() {
        if (!closed.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
            return;
        }

        try {
            producer.flush();
        } finally {
            producer.close(Duration.ofSeconds(10));
        }
    }
}
```

Callback producer dipanggil ketika record sudah di-acknowledge atau gagal; jika exception tidak null, callback menerima failure state. ([Apache Kafka](https://kafka.apache.org/43/javadoc/org/apache/kafka/clients/producer/Callback.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 8. Consumer Config Factory

```java id="consumer-config-factory"
public final class KafkaConsumerConfigFactory {
    private final KafkaCommonConfig common;

    public KafkaConsumerConfigFactory(KafkaCommonConfig common) {
        this.common = common;
    }

    public Properties create(String clientName, String groupId) {
        Properties props = new Properties();

        props.put(ConsumerConfig.BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS_CONFIG, common.bootstrapServers());
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.CLIENT_ID_CONFIG, common.clientIdPrefix() + "-" + clientName);
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.GROUP_ID_CONFIG, groupId);

        props.put(ConsumerConfig.KEY_DESERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringDeserializer.class.getName());
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.VALUE_DESERIALIZER_CLASS_CONFIG, StringDeserializer.class.getName());

        props.put(ConsumerConfig.ENABLE_AUTO_COMMIT_CONFIG, "false");
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.AUTO_OFFSET_RESET_CONFIG, "earliest");
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.MAX_POLL_RECORDS_CONFIG, "200");
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.MAX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS_CONFIG, "300000");
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.ISOLATION_LEVEL_CONFIG, "read_committed");
        props.put(ConsumerConfig.ALLOW_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_CONFIG, "false");

        props.put(
                ConsumerConfig.PARTITION_ASSIGNMENT_STRATEGY_CONFIG,
                CooperativeStickyAssignor.class.getName()
        );

        applySecurity(props);
        validate(props);

        return props;
    }

    private void applySecurity(Properties props) {
        if (common.securityProtocol() == null || common.securityProtocol().isBlank()) {
            return;
        }

        props.put(CommonClientConfigs.SECURITY_PROTOCOL_CONFIG, common.securityProtocol());

        if (common.saslMechanism() != null && !common.saslMechanism().isBlank()) {
            props.put(SaslConfigs.SASL_MECHANISM, common.saslMechanism());
            props.put(SaslConfigs.SASL_JAAS_CONFIG, common.saslJaasConfig());
        }

        if (common.sslTruststoreLocation() != null && !common.sslTruststoreLocation().isBlank()) {
            props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_TRUSTSTORE_LOCATION_CONFIG, common.sslTruststoreLocation());
            props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_TRUSTSTORE_PASSWORD_CONFIG, common.sslTruststorePassword());
            props.put(SslConfigs.SSL_ENDPOINT_IDENTIFICATION_ALGORITHM_CONFIG, "https");
        }
    }

    private void validate(Properties props) {
        if (Boolean.parseBoolean(String.valueOf(props.get(ConsumerConfig.ENABLE_AUTO_COMMIT_CONFIG)))) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Business consumers must use enable.auto.commit=false");
        }
    }
}
```

Consumer config penting untuk business processing: `enable.auto.commit=false`, `max.poll.records`, `max.poll.interval.ms`, `isolation.level`, assignment strategy, dan security. Kafka 4.3 mendokumentasikan consumer config seperti `enable.auto.commit`, `auto.offset.reset`, `group.id`, `max.poll.records`, `max.poll.interval.ms`, `group.instance.id`, dan `partition.assignment.strategy`. ([Confluent Documentation](https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com))

# 11. OffsetTracker

Template aman untuk commit offset manual per partition. Ingat: committed offset = **offset berikutnya**.

```java id="offset-tracker"
public final class OffsetTracker {
    private final Map<TopicPartition, Long> highestContiguousCompleted = new HashMap<>();
    private final Map<TopicPartition, NavigableSet<Long>> completedOutOfOrder = new HashMap<>();

    public synchronized void initialize(Collection<TopicPartition> partitions) {
        for (TopicPartition partition : partitions) {
            highestContiguousCompleted.putIfAbsent(partition, -1L);
            completedOutOfOrder.putIfAbsent(partition, new TreeSet<>());
        }
    }

    public synchronized void markProcessed(ConsumerRecord<?, ?> record) {
        TopicPartition partition = new TopicPartition(record.topic(), record.partition());
        markCompleted(partition, record.offset());
    }

    public synchronized void markCompleted(TopicPartition partition, long offset) {
        long current = highestContiguousCompleted.getOrDefault(partition, -1L);

        if (offset == current + 1) {
            current = offset;

            NavigableSet<Long> pending =
                    completedOutOfOrder.computeIfAbsent(partition, ignored -> new TreeSet<>());

            while (pending.remove(current + 1)) {
                current++;
            }

            highestContiguousCompleted.put(partition, current);
            return;
        }

        if (offset > current + 1) {
            completedOutOfOrder
                    .computeIfAbsent(partition, ignored -> new TreeSet<>())
                    .add(offset);
        }
    }

    public synchronized Map<TopicPartition, OffsetAndMetadata> safeOffsets() {
        Map<TopicPartition, OffsetAndMetadata> result = new HashMap<>();

        for (Map.Entry<TopicPartition, Long> entry : highestContiguousCompleted.entrySet()) {
            long completedOffset = entry.getValue();

            if (completedOffset >= 0) {
                result.put(entry.getKey(), new OffsetAndMetadata(completedOffset + 1));
            }
        }

        return result;
    }

    public synchronized Map<TopicPartition, OffsetAndMetadata> safeOffsetsFor(
            Collection<TopicPartition> partitions
    ) {
        Map<TopicPartition, OffsetAndMetadata> all = safeOffsets();

        return all.entrySet().stream()
                .filter(entry -> partitions.contains(entry.getKey()))
                .collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getKey, Map.Entry::getValue));
    }

    public synchronized void clear(Collection<TopicPartition> partitions) {
        for (TopicPartition partition : partitions) {
            highestContiguousCompleted.remove(partition);
            completedOutOfOrder.remove(partition);
        }
    }
}
```
